linear.title: [NET11-DEC] Owner decision: global.json rollForward policy and test-floor raise
linear.description:
## Decision needed

Two owner calls block PR 1 of the .NET 11 upgrade.

**1.** `rollForward`**.** `global.json` uses `latestMajor`. `tools/buildkite/agent-bootstrap-dotnet.sh` documents that as intentional. Consequences:

* Any machine with SDK 11 installed has built `main` with it since 2026-11-10. `actions/setup-dotnet` reads `global.json`, so GitHub CI may already be on SDK 11 while Buildkite and ReSharper (exact `10.0.403`) are not. Not yet confirmed from CI logs.
* After the upgrade the same setting selects .NET 12 preview SDKs wherever installed, from early 2027.

Options:

* `latestFeature` (recommended): stays on 11.0.x, still takes SDK servicing updates.
* Keep `latestMajor`: record that the pin is a minimum, not a version.

**2. Test floor.** `production/test-floor.json` holds 1,638. The 2026-11-01 dispatch measured 4,058. Raise the floor to the baseline measured in the baseline-capture issue, or leave it.

## Done when

Both choices are recorded on this issue and the upgrade plan is updated to match.

linear.title: [NET11-A] Capture the SDK 10.0.403 baseline before any upgrade change
linear.description:
## Problem

The upgrade's acceptance criteria compare against a baseline that does not exist yet. "Zero warnings" is unenforced today: no project sets `TreatWarningsAsErrors` or `AnalysisLevel`.

## Scope

On `main`, with SDK `10.0.403` forced, on one fixed machine, record:

* Full-suite pass count and total test count.
* Build warning count.
* ReplayGolden result, Baltic v2 hash, v3 goldens, PlayModeSmoke count.
* File list and count of the staged Unity plug-in DLLs.
* ReSharper SARIF from CLI 2026.2.1.
* CPU check on every Buildkite agent and self-hosted runner. .NET 11 refuses to start below x86-64-v2.
* Which SDK version recent GitHub and Buildkite CI runs actually used.

No repository edits. Can start now.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One baseline record committed as a doc or attached here, with machine, commit SHA, and SDK version.
2. Every agent and runner confirmed at or above x86-64-v2, or listed as a blocker.
3. The CI SDK finding is reported on the rollForward decision issue.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

Commands:

* `dotnet --version` (must print 10.0.403; use an isolated install if a newer SDK is present)

linear.title: [AI-W0-D] Architecture gates and ADR-030: package-leak test, process-execution patterns, AI host boundary
linear.description:
Surface: `src/ProjectAegis.Data.Tests/Architecture/**` (new gate test file(s) only; do not edit `NoDynamicExecutionGateTests.cs`); `docs/architecture/adr-030-ai-host-boundary.md` (new, Proposed)

**Reservation (Decision CMANO successor):** reserved-by: Decision (CMANO successor) · claimed-by: bc-47f0bddd-7ca0-587a-b9cf-9501840d21cf · Surface: src/ProjectAegis.Data.Tests/Architecture/\*\*; docs/architecture/adr-030-ai-host-boundary.md

**Owner flag:** ADR-030 accept/waive remains owner — this track delivers gates + Proposed ADR only.

## Problem

Two boundaries are stated but not enforced.

* `tools/copy-delegation-assemblies.sh` copies every DLL from the UnityAdapter `netstandard2.1` publish into Unity. An AI package on a shared project would ship into the plug-in folder.
* `NoDynamicExecutionGateTests` forbids `Process.Start` on the authoring path. The .NET 11 `Process.Run*` helpers are not matched by that substring.

## Scope

1. New architecture test: the four `netstandard2.1` csproj files contain no `Microsoft.Extensions.AI*` or provider reference; `Assets/Plugins/ProjectAegis` contains no such DLL; `Ai.Contracts` has zero package references.
2. New test (do not edit the existing gate file) that applies the same scanned-file list with added patterns: `Process.Run`, `RunAndCapture`, `StartAndForget`, `SafeProcessHandle.Start`.
3. Draft `docs/architecture/adr-030-ai-host-boundary.md`: separate AI assemblies, the egress rule tied to the dual-track firewall, the artifact envelope, side filtering before prompt construction, evidence text treated as untrusted data.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Both tests green on `main`.
2. Each test fails when a violating reference or pattern is introduced (show this once in the PR).
3. ADR-030 is in Proposed status with owner sign-off requested.

## Dependencies

None. Can start now.

`docs/architecture/waivers/waiver-c2-topbar-sim-read-2026-11-16.md`

ADR-010 status stays **Accepted**; this waiver does not amend the ADR.

1. Expose `PlayerInfoModel` (or equivalent fog/info-model field) on a headless projection the top bar already binds (prefer extending an existing top-bar / loop-policy projection).

* Disjoint from [DRG-772](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-772>) (MissionEditor.Cli → [Ai.Host](<http://Ai.Host>) / ADR-030)

## Surface (when implementing)

```
Surface: unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/C2TopBarPanelHost.cs ; matching projection / binder / *Tests under UnityAdapter or Presentation ; no DelegationBridge / SimulationSession / CatalogWriteGate / MapPlaceholderPanelHost
```

linear.title: [NET11-D] Compatibility fixtures: corrupt-CRC scenario package test and net10/net11 replay comparison
linear.description:
## Problem

Two .NET 11 behaviour changes touch code this repository depends on, and neither has a test today.

* ZIP: CRC32 is now validated on read, and async open loads entries eagerly. `AegisScenarioPackage` uses `ZipFile.OpenAsync` and `OpenReadAsync`, so a corrupt package now fails at open instead of at entry read.
* Runtime numerics: `Math.Round(value, digits)` is now correctly rounded, and unchecked float-to-small-integer casts saturate. Replay determinism needs direct proof.

## Scope

1. Add one corrupt-CRC scenario package fixture and a test that asserts the failure is reported cleanly through both the sync and async paths. The test must pass on `net10.0` and `net11.0`.
2. Run the replay comparison experiment: with SDK 11 installed, temporarily multi-target the replay test project to `net10.0;net11.0` on a throwaway branch and compare fingerprints from one commit on one machine. Report the result. Do not merge the multi-target change.
3. Confirm by analyzer or search that Sim, Delegation, and Data contain no unchecked float-to-`byte`/`short`/`char` casts. A pattern search found none.

New test files only. Can start now.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Corrupt-package test green on the current target.
2. Replay comparison result posted here: fingerprints equal, or the first differing tick identified.
3. Cast audit result posted here.
4. Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged. No golden re-bless.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

>>> Agent notes

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): new fixture and test under `src/ProjectAegis.Data.Tests/Scenario/`. Read-only: `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/AegisScenarioPackage.cs`, `AegisScenarioPackage.Async.cs`.

`Math.Round(value, digits)` call sites outside tick paths: `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Validation/Rules/ValidationRules.cs` (lines near 286 and 356), `src/ProjectAegis.Data/PlatformAssistant/PlatformRelativeScaler.cs`. Check that their existing tests cover a midpoint value.

linear.title: [H6] Draft ADR: save/load + multiplayer vs DelegationBridge ZERO-touch constraint
linear.description:
## Context

The H6 entry gate requires an ADR for the ZERO-touch constraint:

* `AGENTS.md`: "DelegationBridge.cs | Zero-touch through Release v1 — no hotpath changes"
* `production/agentic/local-cloud-agent-routing.md`: "Zero-touch: DelegationBridge hotpath / SimulationSession unless product waiver"

No game-state save/load exists today. `ReplayCheckpointStore` holds hashes only. `SimulationSession` is a frozen hub (`docs/architecture/adr-simulation-session-frozen-hub-spirit1-2026-06-20.md`).

## Scope of the ADR

Write a new ADR under `docs/architecture/` using the next free number. ADR-027 is taken by open PR <pull-request id="540d1213-7de1-4ff7-a462-c2a405c9d241" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#679" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/docsunity-record-unity-mcp-stack-choice-adr-027-and-fix-0860-version-176dd2257933" />, so check before numbering.

1. **Save model options**, compared:
   * (a) Replay-to-tick: persist scenario id + seed + catalog snapshot hash + human/player order log, then load by deterministic re-simulation
   * (b) Full state snapshot
   * (c) Hybrid: periodic state checkpoint + log tail, as the GDD `design/gdd/simulation-core-time.md` describes
2. **ZERO-touch analysis**: which option can run entirely *outside* `DelegationBridge.Tick` and the `SimulationSession` hotpath (for example, a new orchestration-level driver that replays orders through existing public APIs). Which one needs a product waiver, and exactly which methods it would touch.
3. **Determinism and ReplayGolden**: prove the Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` and ReplayGolden 6/6 are unaffected, or state the re-bless plan under this ADR. **No silent re-bless.** Cover order-log schema impact (ADR-003) and the `SeededRng` / `SimWorldHash` contract (`docs/engineering/determinism-and-replay.md`).
4. **Multiplayer section**, scoped by the product decision (<issue id="bd666834-41d3-4329-b768-035ac588db6f" label="DRG-328" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-328/h6-product-decision-save-load-only-vs-multiplayer-for-h6" />): lockstep over the same order log vs server-authoritative, and why either touches `TryEnqueueHumanOrder` / `TryIssuePlayerCommand` (CMD-31/32/34 seams).
5. **Catalog**: saves pin `CatalogSnapshotHasher` output and never write through `CatalogWriteGate`.
6. **Presentation**: how Play Mode rebinds after a load without editing `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` / `GlobeMapProductHost` (ADR-010 / 007 / 001 presentation wall).

## Entry gate

This story **is** the ADR half of the H6 gate. The owner can draft it before the product decision; it becomes Accepted only after <issue id="bd666834-41d3-4329-b768-035ac588db6f" label="DRG-328" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-328/h6-product-decision-save-load-only-vs-multiplayer-for-h6" /> is decided.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR file merged with Status Proposed, then Accepted by the owner
- [ ] Each option lists touched symbols, or states that none are touched
- [ ] Explicit statement: product waiver granted or not required
- [ ] Replay-hash plan stated
- [ ] First implementation slice named, with a non-`TBD` Surface

Surface: `docs/architecture/adr-0NN-*.md` (docs-only; zero `src/` or `unity/` edits)

## Start condition

**Nothing is started until the owner gives GO for H6.** This issue stays in Backlog and no agent is dispatched.

2026-09-30 recommendation adopted as planning direction: same-build/catalog save first, multiplayer separate and later. <issue id="d224a671-afb7-4ea8-bf7e-84279249c710" label="DRG-348" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-348/h6-save-contract-define-complete-same-buildcatalog-save-resume-state" /> defines complete authoritative state/compatibility before <issue id="acb8038b-874f-4d97-9005-499caaa1bb1a" label="DRG-349" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-349/h6-save-slice-prove-deterministic-same-build-save-and-resume-before" /> implementation; checkpoint hashes alone are insufficient. Manual/autosave/retention details and any zero-touch waiver remain unresolved. This is not acceptance of the ADR.

No match. <issue id="48c739d7-136d-4f7d-8435-3ad2c763e120" label="DRG-188" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-188/configure-notion-linear-github-and-graphite-traceability-workflow" /> is broader traceability work and <issue id="fe9a9a54-d706-4c68-9ce0-ed6db9c7b3da" label="DRG-241" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-241/hyg-09-dual-project-surface-labels-for-combat-ux-vs-cmano-clone" /> covers Linear surface/\* labels (not the CMANO Surface stamp), so neither is a duplicate.

## Design

A new hosted workflow (`ubuntu-latest`) that is non-required and triggers only on pull_request: `.github/workflows/pr-agent-gate.yml`.

* `contents: read` (plus `pull-requests: read` if needed).
* No `pull_request_target` and no checkout of PR code; it reads the event payload and the REST API with GITHUB_TOKEN.
* (a) Fail unless the title, branch, or body matches `DRG-\d+`. CMA- on its own does not count.
* (b) Parse the `Surface:` line in the PR body. Flag overlap with another open PR's Surface or changed files.
* A DRG-id PR with no Surface line fails (b).
* Flag any change to the hard-no surfaces: SimulationSession, DelegationBridge, CatalogWriteGate, MapPlaceholderPanelHost, GlobeMapProductHost.
* Renovate and dependabot PRs are skipped. Owner PRs still need a DRG id.

## Acceptance

* The hosted, non-required, pull_request-only workflow fails unless the title, branch, or body contains DRG-<n>.
* The same workflow flags overlapping Surface reservations and changed paths against other open PRs.
* Renovate and dependabot are skipped. Fork PRs are safe: no pull_request_target and no checkout of PR code.
* The check is not added to required checks until drg applies a ruleset or branch-protection edit after a Decision soak ruling.

linear.title: Manual autonomy is non-functional — GateResult.QueueForApproval has no product consumer
linear.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28. Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD.

## The contradiction

Req 04 defines autonomy level **Manual** as:

> **Manual** — Agent suggests actions only; player must approve (`HUMAN_IN_LOOP`)

There is no approval path. The suggestion is computed, logged, and discarded.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | The gate models an approval outcome | `Orchestration/AutonomyGate.cs:7` — `GateResult(bool ExecuteNow, bool QueueForApproval, bool Rejected, FireAbortReason PolicyDenialReason)` |
| 2 | Manual autonomy sets it | `AutonomyGate.cs:29` — `AutonomyLevel.Manual => new GateResult(playerApproved, !playerApproved, false)` |
| 3 | The caller hardcodes no approval | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:141` — `gate.Evaluate(Autonomy, order, playerApproved: false)` |
| 4 | Only two branches are handled | `AgentController.cs:142-158` — `if (gateResult.Rejected && ...)` logs a denial; `if (gateResult.ExecuteNow)` issues. `QueueForApproval` **is never read** |
| 5 | Nothing else consumes it | Repo-wide grep for `QueueForApproval` outside its declaration returns only `AutonomyGateTests.cs` (3 assertions) |

## Effect

At **Manual** autonomy — and at **Assisted** with a high-risk order — the agent runs its full decision pipeline, appends a `DecisionRecord` (chosen action, candidate set, rationale, attention load/budget, RNG draw), and the resulting order is then **silently dropped**. The player is never asked. The unit does nothing.

The decision *record* survives in the order log, so a replay shows the agent deciding and no order following — which reads as an engine bug rather than a missing feature.

## Why it matters beyond the one level

`HUMAN_IN_LOOP` is the autonomy tier that makes lethal delegation defensible (req 13: full-auto lethal engagement requires explicit opt-in per mission phase). The tier below full-auto currently does nothing at all.

## To close

- [ ] Retain approval-gated orders as durable pending items bound to unit + agent + originating `DecisionRecord` (req 04 **AGD-07**)
- [ ] Approve/reject path, both logged, so an AAR distinguishes *proposed and refused* from *never proposed* (**AGD-08**)
- [ ] Tick-based expiry, identical at 1× and 60× compression — must not vary with frame rate, to preserve replay determinism (**AGD-09**)
- [ ] Surface the backlog with alert priority (**AGD-10**, doc 20 **ALR-01**)
- [ ] Determinism: `ReplayGolden` held; Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged or golden-updated with an ADR

## Related

Requirements written up in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-07 – AGD-10, acceptance criteria 1–2). The UI half depends on the command result channel tracked separately in doc 20 **CMD-16**.

linear.title: DRG-361 follow-up: [S124 rebrief] refresh Hindsight personality routing after TryRebriefAgent
linear.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review finding on [PR #704](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/704>) (S124 headless Assign Agent + Rebrief success path; <issue id="890865f3-14ca-41b0-aedb-f527fc1daf93" label="DRG-361" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-361/s124-06-w2-del-02-rebrief-success-path" /> S124-06).

## Finding

`DelegationOrchestrator.cs:479` **— Hindsight personality routing is not refreshed after rebrief.** `TryRebriefAgent` swaps the personality preset (traits + slug) and logs `personality.rebrief`, but does not re-call `RegisterAgent`, so Hindsight memory/routing keeps using the old personality slug.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #704)

Hindsight is off in CI and replay, so the stale routing cannot affect tests, goldens, or deterministic replay. Low risk; only matters when Hindsight is enabled in a live session.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* After a successful rebrief, Hindsight routing reflects the new personality (re-call `RegisterAgent` or an equivalent refresh), only when Hindsight is enabled.
* Test with a fake/stub Hindsight client proves the post-rebrief registration uses the new slug; refused rebriefs do not re-register.
* No change to DecisionLog contents or replay hash with Hindsight off; `DelegationBridge` hotpath untouched.

linear.title: Manual autonomy is non-functional — GateResult.QueueForApproval has no product consumer
linear.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28. Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD.

## The contradiction

Req 04 defines autonomy level **Manual** as:

> **Manual** — Agent suggests actions only; player must approve (`HUMAN_IN_LOOP`)

There is no approval path. The suggestion is computed, logged, and discarded.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | The gate models an approval outcome | `Orchestration/AutonomyGate.cs:7` — `GateResult(bool ExecuteNow, bool QueueForApproval, bool Rejected, FireAbortReason PolicyDenialReason)` |
| 2 | Manual autonomy sets it | `AutonomyGate.cs:29` — `AutonomyLevel.Manual => new GateResult(playerApproved, !playerApproved, false)` |
| 3 | The caller hardcodes no approval | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:141` — `gate.Evaluate(Autonomy, order, playerApproved: false)` |
| 4 | Only two branches are handled | `AgentController.cs:142-158` — `if (gateResult.Rejected && ...)` logs a denial; `if (gateResult.ExecuteNow)` issues. `QueueForApproval` **is never read** |
| 5 | Nothing else consumes it | Repo-wide grep for `QueueForApproval` outside its declaration returns only `AutonomyGateTests.cs` (3 assertions) |

## Effect

At **Manual** autonomy — and at **Assisted** with a high-risk order — the agent runs its full decision pipeline, appends a `DecisionRecord` (chosen action, candidate set, rationale, attention load/budget, RNG draw), and the resulting order is then **silently dropped**. The player is never asked. The unit does nothing.

The decision *record* survives in the order log, so a replay shows the agent deciding and no order following — which reads as an engine bug rather than a missing feature.

## Why it matters beyond the one level

`HUMAN_IN_LOOP` is the autonomy tier that makes lethal delegation defensible (req 13: full-auto lethal engagement requires explicit opt-in per mission phase). The tier below full-auto currently does nothing at all.

## To close

- [ ] Retain approval-gated orders as durable pending items bound to unit + agent + originating `DecisionRecord` (req 04 **AGD-07**)
- [ ] Approve/reject path, both logged, so an AAR distinguishes *proposed and refused* from *never proposed* (**AGD-08**)
- [ ] Tick-based expiry, identical at 1× and 60× compression — must not vary with frame rate, to preserve replay determinism (**AGD-09**)
- [ ] Surface the backlog with alert priority (**AGD-10**, doc 20 **ALR-01**)
- [ ] Determinism: `ReplayGolden` held; Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged or golden-updated with an ADR

## Related

Requirements written up in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-07 – AGD-10, acceptance criteria 1–2). The UI half depends on the command result channel tracked separately in doc 20 **CMD-16**.

linear.title: Agent attention is a designated core mechanic that no UI surface exposes
linear.description:
**Verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28.** Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD. Unlike <issue id="addfc33f-54c0-4cbb-94ed-b66aec9bce5b" label="DRG-66" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-66/manual-autonomy-is-non-functional-gateresultqueueforapproval-has-no" /> this is not a broken mechanic — the sim half works correctly. The gap is that it is invisible.

## The design intent

Req 04 \[Resolved Design Decision §1\] designates attention/bandwidth a **core mechanic, not optional**:

> Strategic intent: delegation is a trade-off — one super-agent cannot perfectly command an entire theater.

## It genuinely works

| Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- |
| Load is computed per agent | `Attention/AttentionCalculator.cs` — `Evaluate(budget, memberCount, state)` → `AttentionEvaluation(budget, load, degradation)` |
| Three **graded** degradation tiers | `SlowerReactions` (load > budget), `NarrowedFocus` (> 1.25×), `SimplerDecisions` (> 1.5×) |
| It measurably changes behaviour | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:108-112` — overload multiplies `Traits.ReactionDelay` by 5 |
| It feeds decisions | `AttentionEvaluation` passed into `Decision/DecisionPipeline.cs:13` |
| It is recorded | `attention.Load` / `attention.Budget` written into every `DecisionRecord` |

## The gap

**No C2 projection exposes any of it.** There is no `AttentionProjection`; nothing under `ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/` surfaces load, budget, or degradation tier.

So the operator cannot see that an agent is overloaded, cannot see *how* it is degrading, and cannot make the trade-off the mechanic exists to pose. The player experiences a sluggish agent with no available explanation — the data to explain it is already logged.

## To close

- [ ] Project per-agent load vs budget, sourced from the same `AttentionEvaluation` that gated the decision (do not re-derive in UI — it would diverge from the value that actually applied) — req 04 **AGD-11**
- [ ] Surface the three tiers distinctly, named (**AGD-12**)
- [ ] Raise an alert on tier crossing, attributable to the agent (**AGD-13**, doc 20 **ALR-01/05**)
- [ ] Show projected post-assignment load before committing more units to an agent, so overload is a choice not a discovery (**AGD-14**)
- [ ] Include decision-time attention in the agent explain surface (**AGD-20**) — "the agent was overloaded" is frequently the true answer to "why did it do that"

## Related

Requirements in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-11 – AGD-14, acceptance criteria 3–4). Projection-only work; no sim change, so no determinism risk.

linear.title: Agent attention is a designated core mechanic that no UI surface exposes
linear.description:
**Verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28.** Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD. Unlike <issue id="addfc33f-54c0-4cbb-94ed-b66aec9bce5b" label="DRG-66" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-66/manual-autonomy-is-non-functional-gateresultqueueforapproval-has-no" /> this is not a broken mechanic — the sim half works correctly. The gap is that it is invisible.

## The design intent

Req 04 \[Resolved Design Decision §1\] designates attention/bandwidth a **core mechanic, not optional**:

> Strategic intent: delegation is a trade-off — one super-agent cannot perfectly command an entire theater.

## It genuinely works

| Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- |
| Load is computed per agent | `Attention/AttentionCalculator.cs` — `Evaluate(budget, memberCount, state)` → `AttentionEvaluation(budget, load, degradation)` |
| Three **graded** degradation tiers | `SlowerReactions` (load > budget), `NarrowedFocus` (> 1.25×), `SimplerDecisions` (> 1.5×) |
| It measurably changes behaviour | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:108-112` — overload multiplies `Traits.ReactionDelay` by 5 |
| It feeds decisions | `AttentionEvaluation` passed into `Decision/DecisionPipeline.cs:13` |
| It is recorded | `attention.Load` / `attention.Budget` written into every `DecisionRecord` |

## The gap

**No C2 projection exposes any of it.** There is no `AttentionProjection`; nothing under `ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/` surfaces load, budget, or degradation tier.

So the operator cannot see that an agent is overloaded, cannot see *how* it is degrading, and cannot make the trade-off the mechanic exists to pose. The player experiences a sluggish agent with no available explanation — the data to explain it is already logged.

## To close

- [ ] Project per-agent load vs budget, sourced from the same `AttentionEvaluation` that gated the decision (do not re-derive in UI — it would diverge from the value that actually applied) — req 04 **AGD-11**
- [ ] Surface the three tiers distinctly, named (**AGD-12**)
- [ ] Raise an alert on tier crossing, attributable to the agent (**AGD-13**, doc 20 **ALR-01/05**)
- [ ] Show projected post-assignment load before committing more units to an agent, so overload is a choice not a discovery (**AGD-14**)
- [ ] Include decision-time attention in the agent explain surface (**AGD-20**) — "the agent was overloaded" is frequently the true answer to "why did it do that"

## Related

Requirements in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-11 – AGD-14, acceptance criteria 3–4). Projection-only work; no sim change, so no determinism risk.

linear.title: DRG-236 follow-up: [S125 editor] validate saved drafts against their bound catalog, not the Baltic fixture fallback
linear.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review finding on [PR #701](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/701>) (S125 editor honesty (headless) — save≠export, verb table, workbook contract, binding; <issue id="4e65f999-c537-4646-bdd7-9d3e69dc3f19" label="DRG-236" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-236/slice-g3-validate-mission-and-platform-editor-ux-workflows" /> Slice G3).

`ScenarioSaveExportGate.cs:54` **—** `LiveValidate()` **falls back to the Baltic fixture catalog when no catalog is bound.** A saved draft authored against a different catalog would be validated against Baltic data, producing false passes/failures.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #701)

`SaveDraft` has no production caller yet, so the fallback cannot affect a real save today. Binding the draft's catalog requires the editor composition path, which is outside the headless PR's Surface.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* `LiveValidate()` / `SaveDraft` validate against the draft's bound catalog (resolved from the document's `dbRef`/binding).
* With no bound catalog, the gate reports a stable, actionable finding (e.g. catalog unbound) instead of silently using the Baltic fixture; saving an incomplete draft remains allowed, Export stays gated.
* Tests: draft bound to non-Baltic catalog validates against that catalog; unbound draft yields the finding; Baltic fixture only used in explicit test setup.
* No `CatalogWriteGate` path changes; Excel-primary authoring unchanged.

## Problem

`HindsightSessionFinalizer` builds a one-paragraph string summary and sends it fire-and-forget. There is no structured, citable record of what happened in a run.

## Scope

In `Ai.Host`, a pure projection from `IReadOnlyOrderLog`, `AgentPerformanceAarProjection`, and the authoritative result fields into the frozen evidence DTO.

* Covers chronological entries, decision records, policy denials, engagements, and controller changes.
* Evidence ID is `{fingerprint-prefix}:{SequenceId}`.
* Stable ordering by `SequenceId`.
* A side filter runs inside the projection. Entries the viewing side could not see are dropped unless debrief mode is explicitly set.
* Quantitative summary values (decision count, denials, engagements, objectives ratio) are computed here from the source, never by a model.

This part is framework-neutral and does not need the .NET 11 upgrade.

1. Identical input yields identical ordered evidence.
2. Every fixture's expected evidence-ID list matches exactly.
3. Two-sided fixture: no hidden-side entry appears in player-side output; debrief mode includes them and records the flag.

linear.title: [AI-S2-1] AAR assistant pipeline in the host: prompt build, citation and number validation, explicit failure statuses
linear.description:
## Problem

A model-written after-action summary is only useful if every claim can be traced to evidence and no number is invented.

## Scope

In `Ai.Host`, a pipeline that takes exported evidence and returns a structured result: summary, outcomes, uncertainties, citations.

* The host copies quantitative values from the source report. The model supplies prose and evidence IDs only.
* Evidence text is delimited as data and never concatenated into instructions.
* Validation before publication: reject if any cited ID is absent from the evidence (`RejectedCitation`) or any number in prose disagrees with the report (`RejectedNumber`).
* Timeout, cancellation, malformed output, and unavailable provider each return their explicit status **plus the existing deterministic report**.
* The result is published as an artifact with the full envelope.

Runs entirely on `FakeChatClient` in CI.

## Acceptance criteria

1. All citations resolve on every fixture. Zero fabricated IDs. Zero contradictory numbers.
2. A scripted fake response with a fabricated ID is rejected. Same for a wrong number.
3. Every failure fixture returns its explicit status and the deterministic report.
4. The embedded-instruction fixture does not change behaviour.
5. Replay fingerprints match with the pipeline enabled, disabled, delayed, or failing.
6. No network access in tests.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the evidence projection and Wave 0 integration.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

>>> Agent notes

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host/Aar/**`, tests under `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host.Tests/Aar/**` (new).

linear.title: [AI-S1-2] JSONL evidence writer on .NET 11 with atomic publish and cross-platform determinism
linear.description:
## Problem

Evidence for a long run is large. It should stream to disk, hash identically on Windows and Linux, and never leave a half-written file that looks complete.

## Scope

In `Ai.Host`, write the evidence DTO stream as JSON Lines using `JsonSerializer.SerializeAsyncEnumerable(..., topLevelValues: true)`, a .NET 11 API.

* Source-generated `JsonTypeInfo<T>` for a fixed property order.
* Output is always LF and compact; the API ignores `WriteIndented`.
* Write to a temporary file, then publish atomically through the artifact store.
* Evidence is persisted **before** Hindsight or a provider is asked to process it.
* Record a content hash in the envelope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Round-trip parse equals input for every fixture.
2. Identical input yields byte-identical output on Windows and Linux (compare hashes in CI).
3. Cancellation mid-export leaves no published file; a rerun succeeds.
4. Replay fingerprints match with export enabled, disabled, delayed, or failing.
5. Peak memory recorded for one small and one large log.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the evidence projection and by gate G0 (upgrade PR 2), because the API needs `net11.0`.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

>>> Agent notes

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host/Evidence/Jsonl*.cs`, tests under `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host.Tests/Evidence/**` (new).

The stream-adapter types (`ReadOnlyMemoryStream`, `ReadOnlySequenceStream`, `StringStream`) are opportunistic only; do not adopt them without a profile that shows copies matter.

linear.title: [AI-S2-3] Live evaluation lane: ProjectAegis.Ai.LiveEval, provider adapter, slice 2 go/no-go measurements

Deterministic tests prove the pipeline rejects bad output. They say nothing about whether a real model produces useful, grounded output at an acceptable cost.

## Scope

New project `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.LiveEval/`, **not in** `ProjectAegis.sln`, run on demand.

* One real provider adapter behind the provider abstraction.
* Run the fixture set through the live provider.
* Record per provider: p50 and p95 latency, tokens, cost, groundedness.
* Human-rated usefulness against the deterministic summary.
* `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation` quality evaluators call a judge model, so they run only here, never in CI.

## Go/no-go for default-visible

100% citation resolution and zero numeric contradictions across the fixture set on two consecutive live runs, **and** the owner accepts the measured cost per report.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Results table posted here for each live run, with provider, model, prompt version, and date.
2. Only repository-public fixture content is sent. A Track A-tagged source is refused by test.
3. Credentials come from environment or user-secrets. Nothing secret is committed or logged.
4. The CI gate does not build or run this project.

linear.title: DRG-361 follow-up: [S124 rebrief] refresh Hindsight personality routing after TryRebriefAgent
linear.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review finding on [PR #704](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/704>) (S124 headless Assign Agent + Rebrief success path; <issue id="890865f3-14ca-41b0-aedb-f527fc1daf93" label="DRG-361" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-361/s124-06-w2-del-02-rebrief-success-path" /> S124-06).

## Finding

`DelegationOrchestrator.cs:479` **— Hindsight personality routing is not refreshed after rebrief.** `TryRebriefAgent` swaps the personality preset (traits + slug) and logs `personality.rebrief`, but does not re-call `RegisterAgent`, so Hindsight memory/routing keeps using the old personality slug.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #704)

Hindsight is off in CI and replay, so the stale routing cannot affect tests, goldens, or deterministic replay. Low risk; only matters when Hindsight is enabled in a live session.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* After a successful rebrief, Hindsight routing reflects the new personality (re-call `RegisterAgent` or an equivalent refresh), only when Hindsight is enabled.
* Test with a fake/stub Hindsight client proves the post-rebrief registration uses the new slug; refused rebriefs do not re-register.
* No change to DecisionLog contents or replay hash with Hindsight off; `DelegationBridge` hotpath untouched.

linear.title: [AI-S2-4] Hindsight follow-up: host-side recall adapter and an awaitable finalize beside OnScenarioFinalized
linear.description:
## Problem

`IHindsightMemoryClient` documents retain, recall, and reflect, but exposes only retain and reflect. `HindsightSessionFinalizer.ReflectAarAsync` discards its result and swallows failures, so a completed reflection is never visible to anyone.

The first AAR slice reads the exported evidence file and needs neither fix. This issue is the follow-up.

linear.title: [AI-S5] Optional: generated explanations for AdviceFrame in the Unity UI, and experiment-run reports
linear.description:
## Status

Optional and unscheduled. Schedule only after slices 2 and 3 have shipped. Split into separate UI and report issues at that point.

## Scope

**Advice explanations.** Explain validated `AdviceFrame` facts in plain language.

* Key the generated text to the envelope's existing invocation key (`skillId:tick:time:contactId`) and store it as a host artifact.
* Never write generated text into `SkillEnvelope` or `ReplayProvenance`.
* Discard a response that arrives after the selection or the evidence has changed.
* Preserve the existing stale and unavailable states and the deterministic authority fields.

**Experiment reports.** Describe observed run differences from `ExperimentSeedGridBatch` output. State plainly that doctrine, ROE, and force-ratio IDs label rows without changing simulated behaviour. Use process isolation for parallel batches until shared static state is audited.

**Unity.** Use the Unity-MCP stack (ADR-027) for UI Toolkit wiring and Play Mode checks. Prove behaviour in the headless `PlayModeSmokeHarness` first. If `:8080` is down, stay headless.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Stale-result test: a late response is discarded.
2. Hidden-information test: no opposing-side fact reaches player advice.
3. Authoritative scores and fingerprints match with explanations on and off.
4. Unity smoke evidence for every UI addition, plus a named human Play Mode walk item.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the slice 2 and slice 3 integration issues. Presentation boundary: ADR-010 §2–3, ADR-007, ADR-001.

linear.title: Add GitNexus-informed test selection and baseline-regression policy
linear.description:
## Goal

Select focused Gauntlet checks from changed-code impact while retaining a deliberately scheduled broad regression baseline.

## Acceptance criteria

* Defines test-selection rules from GitNexus impact and capability-manifest mappings.
* Uses conservative fallbacks when impact information is missing or stale.
* Separates fast pull-request checks from full baseline and release evidence.

linear.title: Scenario editor validation gate is unreachable from the UI — TryEnterPlay is dead code
linear.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-26. Found by UX review of the ME-W1 mock against shipped HEAD.

The validation gate is enforced in the core and in the CLI, and is reachable from neither the Unity panel nor the ME-W1 mock. The safety presenter written for the UI layer has no caller.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | An error-severity gate exists for the UI layer | `EditModeController.cs:51-63` — `TryEnterPlay` returns false when `_findings.HasErrorSeverity && !forceConfirmInvalid` |
| 2 | Nothing references it | Window holds only `_session`, `_surface`, `_findings` — `ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs:33-36`. Zero callers of `TryEnterPlay` in the Unity layer |
| 3 | Export gate likewise has no UI caller | `ScenarioExportCommand.Prepare` at `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/ScenarioExportCommand.cs:23` — zero hits for `export`/`publish` across `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/` |
| 4 | No action exists to gate | Shipped button set (`ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs:307-338`): Browse, Open, Load UI Dev Baltic, Save, Rebuild, Refresh Findings, 4 domain buttons, place/RP form. **No Export, Publish, Validate, or Play** |
| 5 | The presenter cannot express the gate anyway | `LiveFindingsPresenter` exposes `HasErrorSeverity` only (`:42-43`) — no per-severity counts, no `CanExport` flag |

## Why this is a defect and not a missing feature

The constraint is real and enforced — `scenario_publish` refuses with `VALIDATION_BLOCKED`, and save-is-never-gated-but-export-is is the correct, deliberate policy. The editor simply has no way to say so. A designer sees a red finding count and learns nothing about what it costs them.

Per the GDD, the differentiator is that the tool never lets you ship something broken silently. Today the editor is silent about the one thing it exists to say.

**Surface:** `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Editor/`, `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/UI/ScenarioEditor/`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/`

## Done when

- [ ] `LiveFindingsPresenter` exposes per-severity counts and a `CanExport` flag sourced from `ScenarioExportCommand.Prepare(...).Allowed` — the view never recomputes the gate
- [ ] Session bar carries a persistent gate state: `EXPORT BLOCKED · N errors` / `READY TO EXPORT`
- [ ] Export / Publish / Sample rendered **disabled with the blocking reason** in tooltip and accessible name — not absent
- [ ] `TryEnterPlay` has a caller, or is deleted with a note saying which gate replaced it
- [ ] Headless presenter test: gate flips with severity, and the blocking reason string is asserted
- [ ] `dotnet test ProjectAegis.sln` suite floor held

## Related

Blocked-by nothing; pairs naturally with the findings-order defect (same presenter, same file).

## Design

linear.title: DRG-236 follow-up: [S125 editor] validate saved drafts against their bound catalog, not the Baltic fixture fallback
linear.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review finding on [PR #701](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/701>) (S125 editor honesty (headless) — save≠export, verb table, workbook contract, binding; <issue id="4e65f999-c537-4646-bdd7-9d3e69dc3f19" label="DRG-236" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-236/slice-g3-validate-mission-and-platform-editor-ux-workflows" /> Slice G3).

## Finding

`ScenarioSaveExportGate.cs:54` **—** `LiveValidate()` **falls back to the Baltic fixture catalog when no catalog is bound.** A saved draft authored against a different catalog would be validated against Baltic data, producing false passes/failures.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #701)

`SaveDraft` has no production caller yet, so the fallback cannot affect a real save today. Binding the draft's catalog requires the editor composition path, which is outside the headless PR's Surface.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* `LiveValidate()` / `SaveDraft` validate against the draft's bound catalog (resolved from the document's `dbRef`/binding).
* With no bound catalog, the gate reports a stable, actionable finding (e.g. catalog unbound) instead of silently using the Baltic fixture; saving an incomplete draft remains allowed, Export stays gated.
* Tests: draft bound to non-Baltic catalog validates against that catalog; unbound draft yields the finding; Baltic fixture only used in explicit test setup.
* No `CatalogWriteGate` path changes; Excel-primary authoring unchanged.

linear.title: Editor findings list sorts by code, not severity — contradicts ADR-008
linear.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-26. Found by UX review of the ME-W1 mock against shipped HEAD.

## Site

`src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/LiveFindingsPresenter.cs:52-55`

```csharp
.Select(f => f.Code)
.OrderBy(c => c, StringComparer.Ordinal)
```

## The contradiction

ADR-008 pins the deterministic findings order as:

`(Severity DESC, Code ASC, MissionId, UnitId, TargetId, Message)`

The presenter implements only the second term. Severity is dropped entirely — it survives as a single boolean `HasErrorSeverity` (`:42-43`).

## Effect

The one finding that blocks export is sorted among the ones that block nothing, by alphabetical accident. Observed in the ME-W1 mock rendering the Baltic Patrol fixture:

| Order | Severity | Code |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | WARN | `MISSION_NO_UNITS` |
| 2 | WARN | `MISSION_NO_UNITS` |
| 3 | **ERROR** | `STRIKE_UNREACHABLE` |
| 4 | WARN | `MISSION_NO_UNITS` |

The blocking error is third of four, at the same visual weight as the rest.

This is a presenter defect, not a determinism defect — `ReportHash` is unaffected, and the current order is stable run-to-run. It is deterministically wrong.

**Surface:** `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/`

## Done when

- [ ] `LiveFindingsPresenter` orders by the full ADR-008 tuple, severity first
- [ ] Sort lives in the presenter, not any view layer
- [ ] Test asserts error-before-warning on a mixed-severity fixture
- [ ] Test asserts byte-identical ordering across two runs (existing determinism assertions extended, not replaced)
- [ ] `dotnet test ProjectAegis.sln` suite floor held

## Design

linear.title: DRG-345 follow-up: [H4-CAPABILITY] add 'generic-only' Warning tier for Patrol/Strike on CLI simulate path
linear.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review finding on [PR #698](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/698>) (<issue id="044990c3-0fab-4227-988a-c3ca7af56e6f" label="DRG-345" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-345/h4-capability-expose-unsupported-mission-roles-before-export-and-play" /> disclose unexecuted mission roles before Export and Play). Related: <issue id="5f3fde68-82d5-4309-8b80-1254f1308065" label="DRG-346" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-346/h4-first-slice-map-edit-validate-save-export-play-using-existing" /> H4 first slice.

## Finding

`MissionRoleCapabilityManifest.cs:103` **labels Patrol/Strike as executed**, but `ScenarioSimulateSampleCommand` never passes missions to `BalticReplayHarness.Run`. On the CLI simulate path, Patrol/Strike missions are therefore effectively generic (units behave without mission-specific execution), so the manifest overstates execution.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #698)

The obvious fix — marking Patrol/Strike unexecuted at **Error** severity — would block Export of every Patrol/Strike scenario, which is worse than the current overstatement. The right fix needs a new intermediate tier, which is a contract change beyond #698's scope.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* Manifest gains a **generic-only** tier evaluated per execution backend (CLI simulate vs session/Play), surfaced as a **Warning** finding with a stable code.
* Patrol/Strike on the CLI simulate path produce the generic-only Warning; Export and Play are **not** blocked; Tanker/AEW/EW unexecuted Errors unchanged.
* Disclosure text in validation UI/briefing states the role runs as generic behavior on that backend; UI does not invent sim authority.
* Deterministic role-policy fixtures + UI projection tests cover executed / generic-only / unexecuted; saving incomplete drafts still allowed.
* If `ScenarioSimulateSampleCommand` is later changed to pass missions, the tier flips to executed via the manifest (no hard-coded role lists in UI). ReplayGolden hash untouched.

linear.title: [AI-S3-2] Slice 3 integration: provider mode on mission_plan_suggest, proposal diff, manifest update
linear.description:
## Problem

Provider-backed authoring exists in the host but users reach mission suggestions through the `mission_plan_suggest` verb, which only knows keywords.

## Scope

Coordinator-only shared-file edits, in one PR:

* Add an opt-in provider mode to `mission_plan_suggest` (for example a `--provider` flag). Keyword mode stays the default and the fallback.
* Show a diff of the proposed operations before anything is applied. Applying is a separate, explicit step through the existing mission verbs.
* `tools/mission-editor/mcp-tools.json` and `McpToolsManifestTests` updated for the new argument.
* CLI `README.md` updated.

CLI behaviour ships before any editor control.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Without the flag, output is byte-identical to today. `MissionPlanSuggestCommandTests` pass unmodified.
2. With the flag and the fake client, a fixture request yields a validated draft and a diff.
3. A stale scenario revision is refused with a clear message.
4. Applied operations carry the `ai` provenance tag and the label required by the ADR-015 outcome.
5. Full gate script green.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the provider-backed authoring issue. Held with it until ADR-015 is decided.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

linear.title: [AI-S3-1] Provider-backed mission authoring in the host: typed proposed operations, validation, idempotency
linear.description:
## Problem

`MissionPlanSuggestCommand` matches keywords and emits fixture IDs (`u1`, `hostile-1`) with hard-coded coordinates. `AiAuthoringServices.NlScaffold` is a deterministic keyword stub. Neither can draft a plan against the scenario that is actually open.

## Scope

In `Ai.Host`, a provider-backed authoring path that returns the same result shape as `AiAuthoringServices.NlScaffold`.

* Input to the model: allowed unit and target IDs from the open scenario, supported mission types, catalog references, the authoring schema.
* Output converted to typed proposed operations on the `Propose` lane. Nothing reaches `Submit` without a human.
* Run `ScenarioValidationEngine` on the proposed result before showing anything.
* Each proposal carries an idempotency key (a retry cannot apply twice) and the scenario edit version (a stale proposal is refused).
* Every applied operation carries a `ProvenanceTag` with `Source = "ai"`.

`AiAuthoringServices` lives in `ProjectAegis.Data`, a `netstandard2.1` shared project. **No provider code or AI package goes there.** The keyword stubs stay as the fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every fixture yields a valid draft or actionable diagnostics.
2. Covered: unknown IDs, ambiguous request, unsupported role, duplicate operation, stale revision.
3. Retrying an accepted proposal does not apply twice.
4. `StubScopePinTests` and `MissionPlanSuggestCommandTests` pass **unmodified**.
5. Valid-draft rate and human correction count measured against the keyword baseline.

## Dependencies

Blocked by Wave 0 integration and the ADR-015 decision. Held until the owner decides ADR-015.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

>>> Agent notes

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host/Authoring/**`, tests under `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host.Tests/Authoring/**` (new).

Read-only: `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/AiAuthoringServices.cs`, `ScenarioDocumentEditor.cs`, `ScenarioManifest.cs`, `ScenarioEditVersionGuard.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Validation/ScenarioValidationEngine.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Skills/SkillIds.cs`.

GitNexus flagged the validation engine and the editor as high-impact hubs on an older index. Use their public APIs only; run impact before any edit to them (none expected).

>>>

linear.title: [AI-S3-2] Slice 3 integration: provider mode on mission_plan_suggest, proposal diff, manifest update
linear.description:
## Problem

Provider-backed authoring exists in the host but users reach mission suggestions through the `mission_plan_suggest` verb, which only knows keywords.

## Scope

Coordinator-only shared-file edits, in one PR:

* Add an opt-in provider mode to `mission_plan_suggest` (for example a `--provider` flag). Keyword mode stays the default and the fallback.
* Show a diff of the proposed operations before anything is applied. Applying is a separate, explicit step through the existing mission verbs.
* `tools/mission-editor/mcp-tools.json` and `McpToolsManifestTests` updated for the new argument.
* CLI `README.md` updated.

CLI behaviour ships before any editor control.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Without the flag, output is byte-identical to today. `MissionPlanSuggestCommandTests` pass unmodified.
2. With the flag and the fake client, a fixture request yields a validated draft and a diff.
3. A stale scenario revision is refused with a clear message.
4. Applied operations carry the `ai` provenance tag and the label required by the ADR-015 outcome.
5. Full gate script green.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the provider-backed authoring issue. Held with it until ADR-015 is decided.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

>>> Agent notes

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): `src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli/{Program.cs,MissionPlanSuggestCommand.cs,README.md}`, `tools/mission-editor/mcp-tools.json`, `src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli.Tests/McpToolsManifestTests.cs`.

linear.title: [AI-DEC-1] Owner decision: ADR-015 labelling of agent-authored scenario content
linear.description:
## Decision needed

`docs/architecture/adr-015-agent-authored-scenario-transparency.md` is still **Proposed**. Its target decision date was 2026-09-01. Resolution owner is Design.

The ADR leans toward labelling agent-authored or agent-assisted scenarios in multiplayer and briefing surfaces, backed by the existing provenance record.

## Why it blocks

Slice 3 (provider-backed mission authoring) is the first feature that produces model-authored scenario content. It cannot ship until the labelling rule is decided. Slices 1, 2, and 4 do not depend on this.

## Done when

ADR-015 is Accepted or Rejected, and the outcome is recorded here.

linear.title: [AI-S4-2] Feed retrieved evidence into PlatformDesignAssistant briefs through new write-gate Propose overloads
linear.description:
**Reservation (Decision CMANO successor):**

`DRG-748 [CMA-22] EXCLUSIVE Surface src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host/Catalog/** NEW + src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host.Tests/Catalog/** NEW + src/ProjectAegis.Data/WriteGate/CatalogWriteGate.cs ADDITIVE new public Propose* and Approve* overloads ONLY | claimed-by: bc-8b675e88-977c-571c-b04f-73d9ac9338bf | reserved-by: Decision (CMANO successor) | fences: offline/fake only; no paid provider calls; no *.[db3-redacted]; Track A refused; retrieved docs are evidence not instructions; existing CatalogWriteGate method bodies and src/ProjectAegis.Data.Tests/WriteGate/** unmodified; IWriteGate.cs out of surface; no production DB approve; draft PR only; no merge without drg; do not start DRG-746 or Slice 5; CRITICAL extend-only`

---

## Problem

`PlatformDesignAssistant` drafts from catalog data and relative scaling. If the retrieval pilot passes its gate, retrieved public evidence can inform those drafts, with citations.

**Only start this if the retrieval pilot passed the owner's margin.** If it failed, cancel this issue.

## Scope

* Feed retrieved evidence into `PlatformDesignAssistant` briefs and the existing deterministic validators.
* Stage batches through the write gate for human approval, using **new** `Propose*` overloads only. No existing write path changes.
* Generated platform values remain proposed values, each with provenance and stated assumptions.
* Retrieved documents are evidence, never instructions. Provider tools are restricted to the current operation.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every proposed value cites a resolvable source with hash and revision.
2. A changed source revision invalidates dependent proposals.
3. Viewing-side isolation holds.
4. Embedded-instruction fixtures are rejected.
5. A Track A-tagged source is refused. No `*.[db3-redacted]` anywhere.
6. Existing `CatalogWriteGate` tests pass unmodified. Nothing is written without human approval.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the retrieval pilot and its gate result.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

>>> Agent notes

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host/Catalog/**` (new); additive overloads only in the write-gate area.

`CatalogWriteGate` is a hard invariant: extend-only, and GitNexus marks it CRITICAL. The catalog cluster is single-writer. Run impact with `summaryOnly` on `CatalogWriteGate` upstream before any edit and get a CMANO Surface stamp. Read ADR-006 and ADR-013 first.

>>>

It is a proposed requirements delta so the project can decide whether swarms are in charter, which phase, and which existing docs they amend. Git is SoT. Depends on research: [Drone Swarm Platforms — Research (2026-08-09)](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df81428f39e8423877957b) --- # Proposed requirement index | ID | Requirement | Priority | Phase | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SWARM-01 | Swarm as first-class platform type | P0 | A | | SWARM-02 | Aggregate integrity state (droneCount) | P0 | A | | SWARM-03 | Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold | P0 | A | | SWARM-04 | Combat DPS/ISR scale with living drones | P0 | A | | SWARM-05 | Single selection / OOB node | P0 | A | | SWARM-06 | Headless logged swarm intents | P0 | A | | SWARM-07 | Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT | P0 | A | | SWARM-08 | At least one hard counter interaction | P0 | A | | SWARM-09 | Map integrity + density readout | P0 | A | | SWARM-10 | Modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin | P1 | B | | SWARM-11 | Host / mothership link | P1 | B | | SWARM-12 | LinkState connected/degraded/lost | P1 | B | | SWARM-13 | Regen near host/base (logistics-gated) | P1 | B | | SWARM-14 | C2 mode + integrity panel fields | P1 | B | | SWARM-15 | Doctrine / WRA for expend and auto-engage | P1 | B | | SWARM-16 | Formations: cloud, wall, spear, orbit | P2 | C | | SWARM-17 | Multi-axis auto-split assault | P2 | C | | SWARM-18 | EMP / jam soft-kill effects | P2 | C | | SWARM-19 | Expend / kamikaze pulse (authorized) | P2 | C | | SWARM-20 | Mission types for swarm tasking | P2 | C | | SWARM-21 | Catalog + Platform Editor authoring | P1 | B/C | | SWARM-22 | Scenario editor place/configure swarm | P1 | B | | SWARM-23 | Agent delegation compatibility | P1 | B | | SWARM-24 | Replay: orders + integrity deltas | P0 | A | | SWARM-25 | Performance / render LOD caps | P0 | A | | SWARM-26 | Contact classification for swarms | P1 | B | | SWARM-27 | Split / merge swarm platforms | P3 | N | | SWARM-28 | Per-member full physics SoT | P3 | N / Won't for MVP | | SWARM-29 | True multi-static ISR mesh | P3 | N | | SWARM-30 | Full MUM-T package with manned flight leads | P3 | N | --- # Phase A — Must ship for MVP ## SWARM-01 — Swarm is a first-class platform type \[P0\] Requirement. The catalog and sim shall support a platform type (or type flag) representing a drone/UAS swarm that can be instantiated as a side-owned unit alongside ships, aircraft, and facilities. Why. Without a platform type, swarms are either fake groups of N aircraft (micro hell, wrong logistics) or pure VFX. Acceptance. A scenario can spawn at least one swarm unit; it appears in OOB and accepts selection. ## SWARM-02 — Aggregate integrity \[P0\] Requirement. A swarm unit shall expose droneCount / maxDrones (or equivalent pool HP that maps 1:1 to count). Destruction of the platform occurs when integrity reaches zero. Acceptance. Damage events reduce count; UI/projections show remaining integrity; at 0 the unit is destroyed/removed per normal unit death rules. ## SWARM-03 — Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold \[P0\] Requirement. The unit shall accept at least Move (plot/course or mission point), Attack (engage target/auto), and Hold (loiter/station) without requiring selection of individual drones. Acceptance. Headless commands exist; C2 can issue them; swarm centroid follows / engages accordingly. ## SWARM-04 — Effects scale with living drones \[P0\] Requirement. Offensive output and sensor effectiveness shall scale with living drone count (monotonic; exact curve is a tuning knob). Acceptance. Full swarm detects/engages more effectively than a half-depleted swarm under identical geometry; golden or unit tests lock the curve. ## SWARM-05 — Single selection node \[P0\] Requirement. Selection, map symbol, and OOB entry treat the swarm as one unit. Per-drone selection is out of scope for Phase A. Acceptance. Clicking the swarm selects one unit id; multi-select behaves like any other unit. ## SWARM-06 — Headless logged intents \[P0\] Requirement. Per ADR-010 patterns, swarm orders shall be headless commands that produce order-log rows (or equivalent deterministic intents), not UI-only gestures. Acceptance. CLI/MCP or existing command path can move/attack a swarm; replay consumes the same intents. ## SWARM-07 — Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT \[P0\] Requirement. Detection, fire, and damage resolution shall use aggregate swarm state, not non-deterministic per-drone physics, as the source of truth. Acceptance. Same scenario + seed → same integrity timeline; cosmetic member layout may be seeded but must not drive outcomes. ## SWARM-08 — Hard counter interaction \[P0\] Requirement. At least one weapon/system class (e.g. area AA / flak / CIWS profile) shall be demonstrably effective at shredding swarm integrity faster than point-fire against a conventional airframe of similar cost band. Acceptance. Documented test scenario where swarm dies to area AA while surviving longer against single-target fire of equal nominal DPS. ## SWARM-09 — Map integrity + density readout \[P0\] Requirement. Map and/or unit panel shall show remaining integrity (count or bar) and a density/affiliation-safe symbol distinct from a single light aircraft where feasible. Acceptance. Player can read swarm health without opening a deep inspector; color alone is not the only channel (CMD-12 alignment). ## SWARM-24 — Replay integrity \[P0\] Requirement. Replay/fixtures shall reconstruct swarm orders and integrity-affecting events. Member cosmetics need not be bit-identical if seeded consistently. Acceptance. Golden replay or world-hash path includes swarm integrity deltas. ## SWARM-25 — Performance caps \[P0\] Requirement. Logical drone count and rendered member count shall be independently capped; Phase A combat must remain aggregate so large logical counts do not imply O(n) engagement work per pulse. Acceptance. Profiled scenario with design-max swarms meets project frame/pulse budgets (state numbers when landed in REQ NFR). --- # Phase B — Modes, host, C2, authoring ## SWARM-10 — Operational modes \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall support modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin. Mode changes are orders (logged). Acceptance. Mode is visible in projection; behavior differs in at least movement posture and engagement aggressiveness. ## SWARM-11 — Host / mothership \[P1\] Requirement. A swarm may designate a host unit (ship/vehicle/aircraft/base). Screen mode prefers orbiting the host. Host loss triggers doctrine last-order. Acceptance. Scenario can bind hostId; Screen keeps swarm near host; host death produces a defined autonomous reaction. ## SWARM-12 — LinkState \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall track linkState ∈ \{connected, degraded, lost\} driven by range, jam, and host/comms rules consistent with project comms degradation themes. Acceptance. Lost link blocks or delays new player orders per doctrine; panel shows cause (CMD-17 pattern: unknown-with-reason, not blank). ## SWARM-13 — Regeneration \[P1\] Requirement. Near a valid host/base with stores, swarm may regenerate drones over time up to maxDrones, subject to logistics rules. Acceptance. Without stores, regen does not occur; with stores, count climbs on a documented rate. ## SWARM-14 — C2 panel fields \[P1\] Requirement. Selected swarm unit panel shows: mode, integrity (count/max), energy/endurance if modelled, host, linkState, and primary sensor/weapon summary. Acceptance. Fields update live; missing telemetry uses explicit unknown reasons when link lost. ## SWARM-15 — Doctrine / WRA \[P1\] Requirement. Doctrine shall control auto-engage posture and whether expend (if present) is authorized. WRA classification for swarm munitions/target classes shall be expressible. Acceptance. Hold-fire prevents assault shots; authorized expend is the only path to SWARM-19 when that ships. ## SWARM-21 — Catalog + Platform Editor \[P1\] Requirement. Authors can define swarm catalog entries: maxDrones, sensors, weapons/munition class, speed/endurance bands, default mode, host constraints. Acceptance. Platform Editor / PDA path can create a valid swarm db entry consumed by sim. ## SWARM-22 — Scenario editor \[P1\] Requirement. Scenario editor can place swarms, set initial count ≤ max, assign side/host/mission. Acceptance. Round-trip save/load preserves swarm fields; validation catches count > max and missing catalog refs. ## SWARM-23 — Agent delegation \[P1\] Requirement. Delegated agents may issue the same intent orders as humans to swarm units; per-axis or unit-level delegation badges apply as for other units. Acceptance. Agent can task swarm assault/screen without UI; order log attributes actor correctly. ## SWARM-26 — Contact classification \[P1\] Requirement. Hostile swarms as contacts expose classification that can distinguish swarm/UAS cloud from single airframe when sensors allow, with confidence (CMD-29 alignment). Acceptance. Contact panel/projection can show swarm-class label when identified; misclassification possible at low quality. --- # Phase C — Depth ## SWARM-16 — Formations \[P2\] Cloud, wall/screen, spear, orbit as soft constraints on member layout and engagement geometry. ## SWARM-17 — Multi-axis auto-split \[P2\] Assault may split logical mass across approach axes against a single high-value target when doctrine allows. ## SWARM-18 — EMP / jam soft-kill \[P2\] EMP scatters/freezes mode switches temporarily; jam degrades linkState and order latency. ## SWARM-19 — Expend pulse \[P2\] Authorized order spends N drones for a burst strike; irreversible; logged. ## SWARM-20 — Mission integration \[P2\] Patrol / support / strike mission types can assign swarms with swarm-appropriate default modes. --- # Phase N / Won't for MVP ## SWARM-27 — Split / merge \[P3\] Split one swarm platform into two; merge compatible swarms. High UX and identity cost — defer. ## SWARM-28 — Per-member physics SoT \[P3 / Won't MVP\] Individual drone bodies as engagement authority. Conflicts with SWARM-07; only if product fantasy demands it and replay strategy is redesigned. ## SWARM-29 — Multi-static ISR mesh \[P3\] True distributed sensing geometry beyond scaled aggregate quality. ## SWARM-30 — Full MUM-T packages \[P3\] Manned flight leads with organic swarms as a package type — after host + air ops maturity. --- # Proposed amendments to existing requirements (if accepted) | Existing | Amendment | | --- | --- | | Entity / unit model (M2 / related REQ) | Add swarm platform flag, integrity fields, hostId, linkState, mode | | REQ-18 Combat Domains | Clarify Air vs new UAS-swarm aspect; damage model for integrity pools | | Sensors / doc 15 | Aggregate ISR scaling; contact class for swarms | | Weapons / doc 14 | Area-AA vs swarm; expend salvo; CIWS interaction notes | | Logistics / REQ-16 | Regen stores; host magazine coupling | | Comms / doc 19 | LinkState for swarm C2 | | REQ-20 C2 UI | Panel fields (SWARM-14); map density; no per-drone micro | | CMD-24 Air Ops | Decision: shared window vs Swarm Ops | | Replay / fixtures | Integrity deltas in golden paths | | Platform Editor / doc 21 | Authoring schema for swarm entries | | doc 01 Project Overview | Charter check: are swarms in scope for air/naval interaction? | --- # Suggested starter tuning (non-normative) | Knob | Starter | | --- | --- | | maxDrones | 40 logical | | renderMembers | 24 cap | | dpsPerDrone | tune vs soft targets | | regen | 1 drone / 1.5s near host if stores | | scatter cooldown | 8s | | armorClass | light-air | --- # Acceptance criteria — Phase A done when 1. Swarm platform spawns, selects, moves, attacks as one unit 2. Losing drones weakens sensors/weapons measurably 3. At least one hard counter shreds integrity faster than point fire 4. Orders are headless + logged; replay/hash stable 5. Map/panel show integrity without per-drone UI 6. Performance caps documented and met in a stress scenario --- # Owner triage (2026-08-09) — DECIDED Closed by: delegated decision (owner → Grok Build) · Linear [DRG-84](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-84) · Workflow [H8](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df818fb428ff449ffe1cb3) | # | Question | Decision | | --- | --- | --- | | T1 | Charter — in scope under doc 01 air/naval now? | Yes — Phase A now. linear.description:
## Parent

<issue id="36a153d9-59db-4f92-b703-954b99ef1426" label="DRG-83" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-83/swarm-drone-swarm-platforms-epic-phase-a-c" /> · Phase A · SWARM-01, SWARM-02, SWARM-05, SWARM-21 (schema portion)

## Goal

Introduce catalog/platform flags and fields for swarm platforms: `isSwarm` (or type), `maxDrones`, default sensors/weapons refs, armorClass light-air. Units instantiate with `droneCount`/`maxDrones`.

## Surface

`Surface: src/ProjectAegis.Data/** ; catalog schema / platform presets ; related unit factory paths under Data only — NOT Sim engagement, NOT Unity UI`

## ACs

- [X] Catalog entry for at least one generic swarm platform loads (`uas-swarm-generic`, max 40)
- [X] Scenario can reference swarm platform id without broken refs
- [X] Unit spawn exposes integrity fields on sim unit model (`SwarmUnitIntegrity` / `SwarmUnitFactory`)
- [X] Platform Editor / PDA can round-trip new fields or documented gap filed → [PE gap](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/drgamtd/drg-86-swarm-a1-catalog-entity-schema-for-swarm-platforms/production/qa/swarm-a1-pe-pda-gap-2026-08-09.md>)

## Implementation (Wave 2 AGENT×1 serial)

* PR: <pull-request id="7ea94b1e-a8e4-4815-b9c3-52fcce646687" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#413" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featcatalog-swarm-a1-catalog-schema-generic-swarm-preset-drg-86-b1cfd884987f" />
* Branch: `drgamtd/drg-86-swarm-a1-catalog-entity-schema-for-swarm-platforms` @ e80a1db
* Migration `012_swarm_platform.sql` · `CatalogSwarmPlatform` · seed bootstrap · Data.Tests 719/719
* Evidence: `production/qa/swarm-a1-catalog-entity-schema-2026-08-09.md`

## Dependencies

Blocked-by: SWARM-01 (<issue id="ee41c04a-8ea9-4807-a12a-a9697bc8f230" label="DRG-85" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-85/swarm-01-land-swarm-requirements-into-game-requirements-corpus" />) — Done. Blocks <issue id="da6cd288-89c5-45c3-880e-e8f0b1933b0d" label="DRG-87" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-87/swarm-a2-swarmcontroller-mvp-integrity-moveattackhold-headless-orders" />.

## Gate

- [X] `dotnet build ProjectAegis.sln` — 0 errors / 0 warnings (agent)
- [X] `dotnet test` Data.Tests 719/719; Sim Catalog|Baltic 137; Delegation Catalog|Baltic 51
- [X] Touched nothing outside Surface (+ migrations, tests, production/qa)
- [X] Evidence under `production/qa/`

Phase A — Must ship for MVP ## SWARM-01 — Swarm is a first-class platform type \[P0\] Requirement. The catalog and sim shall support a platform type (or type flag) representing a drone/UAS swarm that can be instantiated as a side-owned unit alongside ships, aircraft, and facilities. Why. Without a platform type, swarms are either fake groups of N aircraft (micro hell, wrong logistics) or pure VFX. Acceptance. A scenario can spawn at least one swarm unit; it appears in OOB and accepts selection. ## SWARM-02 — Aggregate integrity \[P0\] Requirement. A swarm unit shall expose droneCount / maxDrones (or equivalent pool HP that maps 1:1 to count). Destruction of the platform occurs when integrity reaches zero. Acceptance. Damage events reduce count; UI/projections show remaining integrity; at 0 the unit is destroyed/removed per normal unit death rules. ## SWARM-03 — Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold \[P0\] Requirement. The unit shall accept at least Move (plot/course or mission point), Attack (engage target/auto), and Hold (loiter/station) without requiring selection of individual drones. Acceptance. Headless commands exist; C2 can issue them; swarm centroid follows / engages accordingly. ## SWARM-04 — Effects scale with living drones \[P0\] Requirement. Offensive output and sensor effectiveness shall scale with living drone count (monotonic; exact curve is a tuning knob). Acceptance. Full swarm detects/engages more effectively than a half-depleted swarm under identical geometry; golden or unit tests lock the curve. ## SWARM-05 — Single selection node \[P0\] Requirement. Selection, map symbol, and OOB entry treat the swarm as one unit. Per-drone selection is out of scope for Phase A. Acceptance. Clicking the swarm selects one unit id; multi-select behaves like any other unit. ## SWARM-06 — Headless logged intents \[P0\] Requirement. Per ADR-010 patterns, swarm orders shall be headless commands that produce order-log rows (or equivalent deterministic intents), not UI-only gestures. Acceptance. CLI/MCP or existing command path can move/attack a swarm; replay consumes the same intents. ## SWARM-07 — Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT \[P0\] Requirement. Detection, fire, and damage resolution shall use aggregate swarm state, not non-deterministic per-drone physics, as the source of truth. Acceptance. Same scenario + seed → same integrity timeline; cosmetic member layout may be seeded but must not drive outcomes. ## SWARM-08 — Hard counter interaction \[P0\] Requirement. At least one weapon/system class (e.g. area AA / flak / CIWS profile) shall be demonstrably effective at shredding swarm integrity faster than point-fire against a conventional airframe of similar cost band. Acceptance. Documented test scenario where swarm dies to area AA while surviving longer against single-target fire of equal nominal DPS. ## SWARM-09 — Map integrity + density readout \[P0\] Requirement. Map and/or unit panel shall show remaining integrity (count or bar) and a density/affiliation-safe symbol distinct from a single light aircraft where feasible. Acceptance. Player can read swarm health without opening a deep inspector; color alone is not the only channel (CMD-12 alignment). ## SWARM-24 — Replay integrity \[P0\] Requirement. Replay/fixtures shall reconstruct swarm orders and integrity-affecting events. Member cosmetics need not be bit-identical if seeded consistently. Acceptance. Golden replay or world-hash path includes swarm integrity deltas. ## SWARM-25 — Performance caps \[P0\] Requirement. Logical drone count and rendered member count shall be independently capped; Phase A combat must remain aggregate so large logical counts do not imply O(n) engagement work per pulse. Acceptance. Profiled scenario with design-max swarms meets project frame/pulse budgets (state numbers when landed in REQ NFR). --- # Phase B — Modes, host, C2, authoring ## SWARM-10 — Operational modes \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall support modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin. Mode changes are orders (logged). Acceptance. Mode is visible in projection; behavior differs in at least movement posture and engagement aggressiveness. ## SWARM-11 — Host / mothership \[P1\] Requirement. A swarm may designate a host unit (ship/vehicle/aircraft/base). Screen mode prefers orbiting the host. Host loss triggers doctrine last-order. Acceptance. Scenario can bind hostId; Screen keeps swarm near host; host death produces a defined autonomous reaction. ## SWARM-12 — LinkState \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall track linkState ∈ \{connected, degraded, lost\} driven by range, jam, and host/comms rules consistent with project comms degradation themes. Acceptance. Lost link blocks or delays new player orders per doctrine; panel shows cause (CMD-17 pattern: unknown-with-reason, not blank). ## SWARM-13 — Regeneration \[P1\] Requirement. Near a valid host/base with stores, swarm may regenerate drones over time up to maxDrones, subject to logistics rules. Acceptance. Without stores, regen does not occur; with stores, count climbs on a documented rate. ## SWARM-14 — C2 panel fields \[P1\] Requirement. Selected swarm unit panel shows: mode, integrity (count/max), energy/endurance if modelled, host, linkState, and primary sensor/weapon summary. Acceptance. Fields update live; missing telemetry uses explicit unknown reasons when link lost. ## SWARM-15 — Doctrine / WRA \[P1\] Requirement. Doctrine shall control auto-engage posture and whether expend (if present) is authorized. WRA classification for swarm munitions/target classes shall be expressible. Acceptance. Hold-fire prevents assault shots; authorized expend is the only path to SWARM-19 when that ships. ## SWARM-21 — Catalog + Platform Editor \[P1\] Requirement. Authors can define swarm catalog entries: maxDrones, sensors, weapons/munition class, speed/endurance bands, default mode, host constraints. Acceptance. Platform Editor / PDA path can create a valid swarm db entry consumed by sim. ## SWARM-22 — Scenario editor \[P1\] Requirement. Scenario editor can place swarms, set initial count ≤ max, assign side/host/mission. Acceptance. Round-trip save/load preserves swarm fields; validation catches count > max and missing catalog refs. ## SWARM-23 — Agent delegation \[P1\] Requirement. Delegated agents may issue the same intent orders as humans to swarm units; per-axis or unit-level delegation badges apply as for other units. Acceptance. Agent can task swarm assault/screen without UI; order log attributes actor correctly. ## SWARM-26 — Contact classification \[P1\] Requirement. Hostile swarms as contacts expose classification that can distinguish swarm/UAS cloud from single airframe when sensors allow, with confidence (CMD-29 alignment). Acceptance. Contact panel/projection can show swarm-class label when identified; misclassification possible at low quality. --- # Phase C — Depth ## SWARM-16 — Formations \[P2\] Cloud, wall/screen, spear, orbit as soft constraints on member layout and engagement geometry. ## SWARM-17 — Multi-axis auto-split \[P2\] Assault may split logical mass across approach axes against a single high-value target when doctrine allows. ## SWARM-18 — EMP / jam soft-kill \[P2\] EMP scatters/freezes mode switches temporarily; jam degrades linkState and order latency. ## SWARM-19 — Expend pulse \[P2\] Authorized order spends N drones for a burst strike; irreversible; logged. ## SWARM-20 — Mission integration \[P2\] Patrol / support / strike mission types can assign swarms with swarm-appropriate default modes. --- # Phase N / Won't for MVP ## SWARM-27 — Split / merge \[P3\] Split one swarm platform into two; merge compatible swarms. Swarm platform spawns, selects, moves, attacks as one unit 2. Losing drones weakens sensors/weapons measurably 3. At least one hard counter shreds integrity faster than point fire 4. Orders are headless + logged; replay/hash stable 5. Map/panel show integrity without per-drone UI 6. Performance caps documented and met in a stress scenario --- # Owner triage (2026-08-09) — DECIDED Closed by: delegated decision (owner → Grok Build) · Linear [DRG-84](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-84) · Workflow [H8](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df818fb428ff449ffe1cb3) | # | Question | Decision | | --- | --- | --- | | T1 | Charter — in scope under doc 01 air/naval now? | Yes — Phase A now. Core platform type under air/naval interaction; not deferred to Phase N fiction. | | T2 | Corpus shape | New Game-Requirements/requirements/NN-Drone-Swarm-Platforms.md (next free NN on land) plus amendment pointer bullets on entity model, weapons/14, sensors/15, logistics/16, combat domains/18, C2 UI/20. | | T3 | Air Ops vs Swarm Ops | Phase A: reuse existing unit panel / Air Ops surfaces. Phase B: dedicated Swarm Ops panel fields (SWARM-14). | | T4 | Phase A catalog | Abstract generic only — 1–2 generic swarm presets; national exemplars Phase B+. | | T5 | Boundary vs [DRG-47](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-47) | Core air domain owns SWARM-01…26 delivery. Only SWARM-27…30 (split/merge, per-member SoT, multi-static mesh, full MUM-T) sit near REQ-09/10 speculative. | | Delivery | Who owns? | Epic [DRG-83](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-83) · milestone H8 — Drone Swarm Platforms. | Land path: [DRG-85](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-85) Done via [PR #412](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/412). Linear: DRG-84 Done → DRG-85 Done → DRG-86 Todo. ### Former open questions All five open questions above are resolved by this triage. Do not re-open without a new ADR / milestone note. --- # Provenance Research basis: sibling page Drone Swarm Platforms — Research (2026-08-09).
