Depends on research: [Drone Swarm Platforms — Research (2026-08-09)](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df81428f39e8423877957b) --- # Proposed requirement index | ID | Requirement | Priority | Phase | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SWARM-01 | Swarm as first-class platform type | P0 | A | | SWARM-02 | Aggregate integrity state (droneCount) | P0 | A | | SWARM-03 | Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold | P0 | A | | SWARM-04 | Combat DPS/ISR scale with living drones | P0 | A | | SWARM-05 | Single selection / OOB node | P0 | A | | SWARM-06 | Headless logged swarm intents | P0 | A | | SWARM-07 | Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT | P0 | A | | SWARM-08 | At least one hard counter interaction | P0 | A | | SWARM-09 | Map integrity + density readout | P0 | A | | SWARM-10 | Modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin | P1 | B | | SWARM-11 | Host / mothership link | P1 | B | | SWARM-12 | LinkState connected/degraded/lost | P1 | B | | SWARM-13 | Regen near host/base (logistics-gated) | P1 | B | | SWARM-14 | C2 mode + integrity panel fields | P1 | B | | SWARM-15 | Doctrine / WRA for expend and auto-engage | P1 | B | | SWARM-16 | Formations: cloud, wall, spear, orbit | P2 | C | | SWARM-17 | Multi-axis auto-split assault | P2 | C | | SWARM-18 | EMP / jam soft-kill effects | P2 | C | | SWARM-19 | Expend / kamikaze pulse (authorized) | P2 | C | | SWARM-20 | Mission types for swarm tasking | P2 | C | | SWARM-21 | Catalog + Platform Editor authoring | P1 | B/C | | SWARM-22 | Scenario editor place/configure swarm | P1 | B | | SWARM-23 | Agent delegation compatibility | P1 | B | | SWARM-24 | Replay: orders + integrity deltas | P0 | A | | SWARM-25 | Performance / render LOD caps | P0 | A | | SWARM-26 | Contact classification for swarms | P1 | B | | SWARM-27 | Split / merge swarm platforms | P3 | N | | SWARM-28 | Per-member full physics SoT | P3 | N / Won't for MVP | | SWARM-29 | True multi-static ISR mesh | P3 | N | | SWARM-30 | Full MUM-T package with manned flight leads | P3 | N | --- # Phase A — Must ship for MVP ## SWARM-01 — Swarm is a first-class platform type \[P0\] Requirement. The catalog and sim shall support a platform type (or type flag) representing a drone/UAS swarm that can be instantiated as a side-owned unit alongside ships, aircraft, and facilities. Why. Without a platform type, swarms are either fake groups of N aircraft (micro hell, wrong logistics) or pure VFX. Acceptance. A scenario can spawn at least one swarm unit; it appears in OOB and accepts selection. ## SWARM-02 — Aggregate integrity \[P0\] Requirement. A swarm unit shall expose droneCount / maxDrones (or equivalent pool HP that maps 1:1 to count). Destruction of the platform occurs when integrity reaches zero. Acceptance. Damage events reduce count; UI/projections show remaining integrity; at 0 the unit is destroyed/removed per normal unit death rules. ## SWARM-03 — Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold \[P0\] Requirement. The unit shall accept at least Move (plot/course or mission point), Attack (engage target/auto), and Hold (loiter/station) without requiring selection of individual drones. Acceptance. Headless commands exist; C2 can issue them; swarm centroid follows / engages accordingly. ## SWARM-04 — Effects scale with living drones \[P0\] Requirement. Offensive output and sensor effectiveness shall scale with living drone count (monotonic; exact curve is a tuning knob). Acceptance. Full swarm detects/engages more effectively than a half-depleted swarm under identical geometry; golden or unit tests lock the curve. ## SWARM-05 — Single selection node \[P0\] Requirement. Selection, map symbol, and OOB entry treat the swarm as one unit. Per-drone selection is out of scope for Phase A. Acceptance. Clicking the swarm selects one unit id; multi-select behaves like any other unit. ## SWARM-06 — Headless logged intents \[P0\] Requirement. Per ADR-010 patterns, swarm orders shall be headless commands that produce order-log rows (or equivalent deterministic intents), not UI-only gestures. Acceptance. CLI/MCP or existing command path can move/attack a swarm; replay consumes the same intents. ## SWARM-07 — Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT \[P0\] Requirement. Detection, fire, and damage resolution shall use aggregate swarm state, not non-deterministic per-drone physics, as the source of truth. Acceptance. Same scenario + seed → same integrity timeline; cosmetic member layout may be seeded but must not drive outcomes. ## SWARM-08 — Hard counter interaction \[P0\] Requirement. At least one weapon/system class (e.g. area AA / flak / CIWS profile) shall be demonstrably effective at shredding swarm integrity faster than point-fire against a conventional airframe of similar cost band. Acceptance. Documented test scenario where swarm dies to area AA while surviving longer against single-target fire of equal nominal DPS. ## SWARM-09 — Map integrity + density readout \[P0\] Requirement. Map and/or unit panel shall show remaining integrity (count or bar) and a density/affiliation-safe symbol distinct from a single light aircraft where feasible. Acceptance. Player can read swarm health without opening a deep inspector; color alone is not the only channel (CMD-12 alignment). ## SWARM-24 — Replay integrity \[P0\] Requirement. Replay/fixtures shall reconstruct swarm orders and integrity-affecting events. Member cosmetics need not be bit-identical if seeded consistently. Acceptance. Golden replay or world-hash path includes swarm integrity deltas. ## SWARM-25 — Performance caps \[P0\] Requirement. Logical drone count and rendered member count shall be independently capped; Phase A combat must remain aggregate so large logical counts do not imply O(n) engagement work per pulse. Acceptance. Profiled scenario with design-max swarms meets project frame/pulse budgets (state numbers when landed in REQ NFR). --- # Phase B — Modes, host, C2, authoring ## SWARM-10 — Operational modes \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall support modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin. Mode changes are orders (logged). Acceptance. Mode is visible in projection; behavior differs in at least movement posture and engagement aggressiveness. ## SWARM-11 — Host / mothership \[P1\] Requirement. A swarm may designate a host unit (ship/vehicle/aircraft/base). Screen mode prefers orbiting the host. Host loss triggers doctrine last-order. Acceptance. Scenario can bind hostId; Screen keeps swarm near host; host death produces a defined autonomous reaction. ## SWARM-12 — LinkState \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall track linkState ∈ \{connected, degraded, lost\} driven by range, jam, and host/comms rules consistent with project comms degradation themes. Acceptance. Lost link blocks or delays new player orders per doctrine; panel shows cause (CMD-17 pattern: unknown-with-reason, not blank). ## SWARM-13 — Regeneration \[P1\] Requirement. Near a valid host/base with stores, swarm may regenerate drones over time up to maxDrones, subject to logistics rules. Acceptance. Without stores, regen does not occur; with stores, count climbs on a documented rate. ## SWARM-14 — C2 panel fields \[P1\] Requirement. Selected swarm unit panel shows: mode, integrity (count/max), energy/endurance if modelled, host, linkState, and primary sensor/weapon summary. Acceptance. Fields update live; missing telemetry uses explicit unknown reasons when link lost. ## SWARM-15 — Doctrine / WRA \[P1\] Requirement. Doctrine shall control auto-engage posture and whether expend (if present) is authorized. WRA classification for swarm munitions/target classes shall be expressible. Acceptance. Hold-fire prevents assault shots; authorized expend is the only path to SWARM-19 when that ships. ## SWARM-21 — Catalog + Platform Editor \[P1\] Requirement. Authors can define swarm catalog entries: maxDrones, sensors, weapons/munition class, speed/endurance bands, default mode, host constraints. Acceptance. Platform Editor / PDA path can create a valid swarm db entry consumed by sim. ## SWARM-22 — Scenario editor \[P1\] Requirement. Scenario editor can place swarms, set initial count ≤ max, assign side/host/mission. Acceptance. Round-trip save/load preserves swarm fields; validation catches count > max and missing catalog refs. ## SWARM-23 — Agent delegation \[P1\] Requirement. Delegated agents may issue the same intent orders as humans to swarm units; per-axis or unit-level delegation badges apply as for other units. Acceptance. Agent can task swarm assault/screen without UI; order log attributes actor correctly. ## SWARM-26 — Contact classification \[P1\] Requirement. Hostile swarms as contacts expose classification that can distinguish swarm/UAS cloud from single airframe when sensors allow, with confidence (CMD-29 alignment). Acceptance. Contact panel/projection can show swarm-class label when identified; misclassification possible at low quality. --- # Phase C — Depth ## SWARM-16 — Formations \[P2\] Cloud, wall/screen, spear, orbit as soft constraints on member layout and engagement geometry. ## SWARM-17 — Multi-axis auto-split \[P2\] Assault may split logical mass across approach axes against a single high-value target when doctrine allows. ## SWARM-18 — EMP / jam soft-kill \[P2\] EMP scatters/freezes mode switches temporarily; jam degrades linkState and order latency. ## SWARM-19 — Expend pulse \[P2\] Authorized order spends N drones for a burst strike; irreversible; logged. ## SWARM-20 — Mission integration \[P2\] Patrol / support / strike mission types can assign swarms with swarm-appropriate default modes. --- # Phase N / Won't for MVP ## SWARM-27 — Split / merge \[P3\] Split one swarm platform into two; merge compatible swarms. High UX and identity cost — defer. ## SWARM-28 — Per-member physics SoT \[P3 / Won't MVP\] Individual drone bodies as engagement authority. Conflicts with SWARM-07; only if product fantasy demands it and replay strategy is redesigned. ## SWARM-29 — Multi-static ISR mesh \[P3\] True distributed sensing geometry beyond scaled aggregate quality. ## SWARM-30 — Full MUM-T packages \[P3\] Manned flight leads with organic swarms as a package type — after host + air ops maturity. --- # Proposed amendments to existing requirements (if accepted) | Existing | Amendment | | --- | --- | | Entity / unit model (M2 / related REQ) | Add swarm platform flag, integrity fields, hostId, linkState, mode | | REQ-18 Combat Domains | Clarify Air vs new UAS-swarm aspect; damage model for integrity pools | | Sensors / doc 15 | Aggregate ISR scaling; contact class for swarms | | Weapons / doc 14 | Area-AA vs swarm; expend salvo; CIWS interaction notes | | Logistics / REQ-16 | Regen stores; host magazine coupling | | Comms / doc 19 | LinkState for swarm C2 | | REQ-20 C2 UI | Panel fields (SWARM-14); map density; no per-drone micro | | CMD-24 Air Ops | Decision: shared window vs Swarm Ops | | Replay / fixtures | Integrity deltas in golden paths | | Platform Editor / doc 21 | Authoring schema for swarm entries | | doc 01 Project Overview | Charter check: are swarms in scope for air/naval interaction? | --- # Suggested starter tuning (non-normative) | Knob | Starter | | --- | --- | | maxDrones | 40 logical | | renderMembers | 24 cap | | dpsPerDrone | tune vs soft targets | | regen | 1 drone / 1.5s near host if stores | | scatter cooldown | 8s | | armorClass | light-air | --- # Acceptance criteria — Phase A done when 1. Swarm platform spawns, selects, moves, attacks as one unit 2. Losing drones weakens sensors/weapons measurably 3. At least one hard counter shreds integrity faster than point fire 4. Orders are headless + logged; replay/hash stable 5. Map/panel show integrity without per-drone UI 6. Performance caps documented and met in a stress scenario --- # Owner triage (2026-08-09) — DECIDED Closed by: delegated decision (owner → Grok Build) · Linear [DRG-84](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-84) · Workflow [H8](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df818fb428ff449ffe1cb3) | # | Question | Decision | | --- | --- | --- | | T1 | Charter — in scope under doc 01 air/naval now? | Yes — Phase A now. Core platform type under air/naval interaction; not deferred to Phase N fiction. | | T2 | Corpus shape | New Game-Requirements/requirements/NN-Drone-Swarm-Platforms.md (next free NN on land) plus amendment pointer bullets on entity model, weapons/14, sensors/15, logistics/16, combat domains/18, C2 UI/20. | | T3 | Air Ops vs Swarm Ops | Phase A: reuse existing unit panel / Air Ops surfaces. Phase B: dedicated Swarm Ops panel fields (SWARM-14). | | T4 | Phase A catalog | Abstract generic only — 1–2 generic swarm presets; national exemplars Phase B+. | | T5 | Boundary vs [DRG-47](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-47) | Core air domain owns SWARM-01…26 delivery. Only SWARM-27…30 (split/merge, per-member SoT, multi-static mesh, full MUM-T) sit near REQ-09/10 speculative. | | Delivery | Who owns? | Epic [DRG-83](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-83) · milestone H8 — Drone Swarm Platforms. | Land path: [DRG-85](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-85) Done via [PR #412](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/412). Linear: DRG-84 Done → DRG-85 Done → DRG-86 Todo. ### Former open questions All five open questions above are resolved by this triage. Do not re-open without a new ADR / milestone note. --- # Provenance Research basis: sibling page Drone Swarm Platforms — Research (2026-08-09). Full swarm detects/engages more effectively than a half-depleted swarm under identical geometry; golden or unit tests lock the curve. ## SWARM-05 — Single selection node \[P0\] Requirement. Selection, map symbol, and OOB entry treat the swarm as one unit. Per-drone selection is out of scope for Phase A. Acceptance. Clicking the swarm selects one unit id; multi-select behaves like any other unit. ## SWARM-06 — Headless logged intents \[P0\] Requirement. Per ADR-010 patterns, swarm orders shall be headless commands that produce order-log rows (or equivalent deterministic intents), not UI-only gestures. Acceptance. CLI/MCP or existing command path can move/attack a swarm; replay consumes the same intents. ## SWARM-07 — Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT \[P0\] Requirement. Detection, fire, and damage resolution shall use aggregate swarm state, not non-deterministic per-drone physics, as the source of truth. Acceptance. Same scenario + seed → same integrity timeline; cosmetic member layout may be seeded but must not drive outcomes. ## SWARM-08 — Hard counter interaction \[P0\] Requirement. At least one weapon/system class (e.g. area AA / flak / CIWS profile) shall be demonstrably effective at shredding swarm integrity faster than point-fire against a conventional airframe of similar cost band. Acceptance. Documented test scenario where swarm dies to area AA while surviving longer against single-target fire of equal nominal DPS. ## SWARM-09 — Map integrity + density readout \[P0\] Requirement. Map and/or unit panel shall show remaining integrity (count or bar) and a density/affiliation-safe symbol distinct from a single light aircraft where feasible. Acceptance. Player can read swarm health without opening a deep inspector; color alone is not the only channel (CMD-12 alignment). ## SWARM-24 — Replay integrity \[P0\] Requirement. Replay/fixtures shall reconstruct swarm orders and integrity-affecting events. Member cosmetics need not be bit-identical if seeded consistently. Acceptance. Golden replay or world-hash path includes swarm integrity deltas. ## SWARM-25 — Performance caps \[P0\] Requirement. Logical drone count and rendered member count shall be independently capped; Phase A combat must remain aggregate so large logical counts do not imply O(n) engagement work per pulse. Acceptance. Profiled scenario with design-max swarms meets project frame/pulse budgets (state numbers when landed in REQ NFR). --- # Phase B — Modes, host, C2, authoring ## SWARM-10 — Operational modes \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall support modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin. Mode changes are orders (logged). Acceptance. A swarm may designate a host unit (ship/vehicle/aircraft/base). Screen mode prefers orbiting the host. Host loss triggers doctrine last-order. Acceptance. Scenario can bind hostId; Screen keeps swarm near host; host death produces a defined autonomous reaction. ## SWARM-12 — LinkState \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall track linkState ∈ \{connected, degraded, lost\} driven by range, jam, and host/comms rules consistent with project comms degradation themes. Acceptance. Lost link blocks or delays new player orders per doctrine; panel shows cause (CMD-17 pattern: unknown-with-reason, not blank). ## SWARM-13 — Regeneration \[P1\] Requirement. Near a valid host/base with stores, swarm may regenerate drones over time up to maxDrones, subject to logistics rules. Acceptance. Without stores, regen does not occur; with stores, count climbs on a documented rate. ## SWARM-14 — C2 panel fields \[P1\] Requirement. Selected swarm unit panel shows: mode, integrity (count/max), energy/endurance if modelled, host, linkState, and primary sensor/weapon summary. Acceptance. Fields update live; missing telemetry uses explicit unknown reasons when link lost. ## SWARM-15 — Doctrine / WRA \[P1\] Requirement. Hold-fire prevents assault shots; authorized expend is the only path to SWARM-19 when that ships. ## SWARM-21 — Catalog + Platform Editor \[P1\] Requirement. Authors can define swarm catalog entries: maxDrones, sensors, weapons/munition class, speed/endurance bands, default mode, host constraints. Acceptance. Platform Editor / PDA path can create a valid swarm db entry consumed by sim. ## SWARM-22 — Scenario editor \[P1\] Requirement. Scenario editor can place swarms, set initial count ≤ max, assign side/host/mission. Acceptance. Round-trip save/load preserves swarm fields; validation catches count > max and missing catalog refs. ## SWARM-23 — Agent delegation \[P1\] Requirement. Delegated agents may issue the same intent orders as humans to swarm units; per-axis or unit-level delegation badges apply as for other units. Acceptance. Agent can task swarm assault/screen without UI; order log attributes actor correctly. ## SWARM-26 — Contact classification \[P1\] Requirement. Contact panel/projection can show swarm-class label when identified; misclassification possible at low quality. --- # Phase C — Depth ## SWARM-16 — Formations \[P2\] Cloud, wall/screen, spear, orbit as soft constraints on member layout and engagement geometry. ## SWARM-17 — Multi-axis auto-split \[P2\] Assault may split logical mass across approach axes against a single high-value target when doctrine allows. ## SWARM-18 — EMP / jam soft-kill \[P2\] EMP scatters/freezes mode switches temporarily; jam degrades linkState and order latency. ## SWARM-19 — Expend pulse \[P2\] Authorized order spends N drones for a burst strike; irreversible; logged. ## SWARM-20 — Mission integration \[P2\] Patrol / support / strike mission types can assign swarms with swarm-appropriate default modes. --- # Phase N / Won't for MVP ## SWARM-27 — Split / merge \[P3\] Split one swarm platform into two; merge compatible swarms. High UX and identity cost — defer. ## SWARM-28 — Per-member physics SoT \[P3 / Won't MVP\] Individual drone bodies as engagement authority. Conflicts with SWARM-07; only if product fantasy demands it and replay strategy is redesigned. ## SWARM-29 — Multi-static ISR mesh \[P3\] True distributed sensing geometry beyond scaled aggregate quality. ## SWARM-30 — Full MUM-T packages \[P3\] Manned flight leads with organic swarms as a package type — after host + air ops maturity. --- # Proposed amendments to existing requirements (if accepted) | Existing | Amendment | | --- | --- | | Entity / unit model (M2 / related REQ) | Add swarm platform flag, integrity fields, hostId, linkState, mode | | REQ-18 Combat Domains | Clarify Air vs new UAS-swarm aspect; damage model for integrity pools | | Sensors / doc 15 | Aggregate ISR scaling; contact class for swarms | | Weapons / doc 14 | Area-AA vs swarm; expend salvo; CIWS interaction notes | | Logistics / REQ-16 | Regen stores; host magazine coupling | | Comms / doc 19 | LinkState for swarm C2 | | REQ-20 C2 UI | Panel fields (SWARM-14); map density; no per-drone micro | | CMD-24 Air Ops | Decision: shared window vs Swarm Ops | | Replay / fixtures | Integrity deltas in golden paths | | Platform Editor / doc 21 | Authoring schema for swarm entries | | doc 01 Project Overview | Charter check: are swarms in scope for air/naval interaction? | --- # Suggested starter tuning (non-normative) | Knob | Starter | | --- | --- | | maxDrones | 40 logical | | renderMembers | 24 cap | | dpsPerDrone | tune vs soft targets | | regen | 1 drone / 1.5s near host if stores | | scatter cooldown | 8s | | armorClass | light-air | --- # Acceptance criteria — Phase A done when 1. Phase A — Must ship for MVP ## SWARM-01 — Swarm is a first-class platform type \[P0\] Requirement. The catalog and sim shall support a platform type (or type flag) representing a drone/UAS swarm that can be instantiated as a side-owned unit alongside ships, aircraft, and facilities. Why. Without a platform type, swarms are either fake groups of N aircraft (micro hell, wrong logistics) or pure VFX. Acceptance. A scenario can spawn at least one swarm unit; it appears in OOB and accepts selection. ## SWARM-02 — Aggregate integrity \[P0\] Requirement. A swarm unit shall expose droneCount / maxDrones (or equivalent pool HP that maps 1:1 to count). Destruction of the platform occurs when integrity reaches zero. Acceptance. Damage events reduce count; UI/projections show remaining integrity; at 0 the unit is destroyed/removed per normal unit death rules. ## SWARM-03 — Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold \[P0\] Requirement. The unit shall accept at least Move (plot/course or mission point), Attack (engage target/auto), and Hold (loiter/station) without requiring selection of individual drones. Acceptance. Headless commands exist; C2 can issue them; swarm centroid follows / engages accordingly. ## SWARM-04 — Effects scale with living drones \[P0\] Requirement. Offensive output and sensor effectiveness shall scale with living drone count (monotonic; exact curve is a tuning knob). Acceptance. Full swarm detects/engages more effectively than a half-depleted swarm under identical geometry; golden or unit tests lock the curve. ## SWARM-05 — Single selection node \[P0\] Requirement. Selection, map symbol, and OOB entry treat the swarm as one unit. Per-drone selection is out of scope for Phase A. Acceptance. Clicking the swarm selects one unit id; multi-select behaves like any other unit. ## SWARM-06 — Headless logged intents \[P0\] Requirement. Per ADR-010 patterns, swarm orders shall be headless commands that produce order-log rows (or equivalent deterministic intents), not UI-only gestures. Acceptance. CLI/MCP or existing command path can move/attack a swarm; replay consumes the same intents. ## SWARM-07 — Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT \[P0\] Requirement. Detection, fire, and damage resolution shall use aggregate swarm state, not non-deterministic per-drone physics, as the source of truth. Acceptance. Same scenario + seed → same integrity timeline; cosmetic member layout may be seeded but must not drive outcomes. ## SWARM-08 — Hard counter interaction \[P0\] Requirement. At least one weapon/system class (e.g. area AA / flak / CIWS profile) shall be demonstrably effective at shredding swarm integrity faster than point-fire against a conventional airframe of similar cost band. Acceptance. Documented test scenario where swarm dies to area AA while surviving longer against single-target fire of equal nominal DPS. ## SWARM-09 — Map integrity + density readout \[P0\] Requirement. Map and/or unit panel shall show remaining integrity (count or bar) and a density/affiliation-safe symbol distinct from a single light aircraft where feasible. Acceptance. Player can read swarm health without opening a deep inspector; color alone is not the only channel (CMD-12 alignment). ## SWARM-24 — Replay integrity \[P0\] Requirement. Replay/fixtures shall reconstruct swarm orders and integrity-affecting events. Member cosmetics need not be bit-identical if seeded consistently. Acceptance. Golden replay or world-hash path includes swarm integrity deltas. ## SWARM-25 — Performance caps \[P0\] Requirement. Logical drone count and rendered member count shall be independently capped; Phase A combat must remain aggregate so large logical counts do not imply O(n) engagement work per pulse. Acceptance. Profiled scenario with design-max swarms meets project frame/pulse budgets (state numbers when landed in REQ NFR). --- # Phase B — Modes, host, C2, authoring ## SWARM-10 — Operational modes \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall support modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin. Mode changes are orders (logged). Acceptance. Mode is visible in projection; behavior differs in at least movement posture and engagement aggressiveness. ## SWARM-11 — Host / mothership \[P1\] Requirement. A swarm may designate a host unit (ship/vehicle/aircraft/base). Screen mode prefers orbiting the host. Host loss triggers doctrine last-order. Acceptance. Scenario can bind hostId; Screen keeps swarm near host; host death produces a defined autonomous reaction. ## SWARM-12 — LinkState \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall track linkState ∈ \{connected, degraded, lost\} driven by range, jam, and host/comms rules consistent with project comms degradation themes. Acceptance. Lost link blocks or delays new player orders per doctrine; panel shows cause (CMD-17 pattern: unknown-with-reason, not blank). ## SWARM-13 — Regeneration \[P1\] Requirement. Near a valid host/base with stores, swarm may regenerate drones over time up to maxDrones, subject to logistics rules. Acceptance. Without stores, regen does not occur; with stores, count climbs on a documented rate. ## SWARM-14 — C2 panel fields \[P1\] Requirement. Selected swarm unit panel shows: mode, integrity (count/max), energy/endurance if modelled, host, linkState, and primary sensor/weapon summary. Acceptance. Fields update live; missing telemetry uses explicit unknown reasons when link lost. ## SWARM-15 — Doctrine / WRA \[P1\] Requirement. Doctrine shall control auto-engage posture and whether expend (if present) is authorized. WRA classification for swarm munitions/target classes shall be expressible. Acceptance. Hold-fire prevents assault shots; authorized expend is the only path to SWARM-19 when that ships. ## SWARM-21 — Catalog + Platform Editor \[P1\] Requirement. Authors can define swarm catalog entries: maxDrones, sensors, weapons/munition class, speed/endurance bands, default mode, host constraints. Acceptance. Platform Editor / PDA path can create a valid swarm db entry consumed by sim. ## SWARM-22 — Scenario editor \[P1\] Requirement. Scenario editor can place swarms, set initial count ≤ max, assign side/host/mission. Acceptance. Round-trip save/load preserves swarm fields; validation catches count > max and missing catalog refs. ## SWARM-23 — Agent delegation \[P1\] Requirement. Delegated agents may issue the same intent orders as humans to swarm units; per-axis or unit-level delegation badges apply as for other units. Acceptance. Agent can task swarm assault/screen without UI; order log attributes actor correctly. ## SWARM-26 — Contact classification \[P1\] Requirement. Hostile swarms as contacts expose classification that can distinguish swarm/UAS cloud from single airframe when sensors allow, with confidence (CMD-29 alignment). Acceptance. Contact panel/projection can show swarm-class label when identified; misclassification possible at low quality. --- # Phase C — Depth ## SWARM-16 — Formations \[P2\] Cloud, wall/screen, spear, orbit as soft constraints on member layout and engagement geometry. ## SWARM-17 — Multi-axis auto-split \[P2\] Assault may split logical mass across approach axes against a single high-value target when doctrine allows. ## SWARM-18 — EMP / jam soft-kill \[P2\] EMP scatters/freezes mode switches temporarily; jam degrades linkState and order latency. ## SWARM-19 — Expend pulse \[P2\] Authorized order spends N drones for a burst strike; irreversible; logged. ## SWARM-20 — Mission integration \[P2\] Patrol / support / strike mission types can assign swarms with swarm-appropriate default modes. --- # Phase N / Won't for MVP ## SWARM-27 — Split / merge \[P3\] Split one swarm platform into two; merge compatible swarms. High UX and identity cost — defer. ## SWARM-28 — Per-member physics SoT \[P3 / Won't MVP\] Individual drone bodies as engagement authority. Conflicts with SWARM-07; only if product fantasy demands it and replay strategy is redesigned. ## SWARM-29 — Multi-static ISR mesh \[P3\] True distributed sensing geometry beyond scaled aggregate quality. ## SWARM-30 — Full MUM-T packages \[P3\] Manned flight leads with organic swarms as a package type — after host + air ops maturity. --- # Proposed amendments to existing requirements (if accepted) | Existing | Amendment | | --- | --- | | Entity / unit model (M2 / related REQ) | Add swarm platform flag, integrity fields, hostId, linkState, mode | | REQ-18 Combat Domains | Clarify Air vs new UAS-swarm aspect; damage model for integrity pools | | Sensors / doc 15 | Aggregate ISR scaling; contact class for swarms | | Weapons / doc 14 | Area-AA vs swarm; expend salvo; CIWS interaction notes | | Logistics / REQ-16 | Regen stores; host magazine coupling | | Comms / doc 19 | LinkState for swarm C2 | | REQ-20 C2 UI | Panel fields (SWARM-14); map density; no per-drone micro | | CMD-24 Air Ops | Decision: shared window vs Swarm Ops | | Replay / fixtures | Integrity deltas in golden paths | | Platform Editor / doc 21 | Authoring schema for swarm entries | | doc 01 Project Overview | Charter check: are swarms in scope for air/naval interaction? | --- # Suggested starter tuning (non-normative) | Knob | Starter | | --- | --- | | maxDrones | 40 logical | | renderMembers | 24 cap | | dpsPerDrone | tune vs soft targets | | regen | 1 drone / 1.5s near host if stores | | scatter cooldown | 8s | | armorClass | light-air | --- # Acceptance criteria — Phase A done when 1. linear.title: Show doctrine/ROE/WRA inheritance source and effective value per unit, with reset-to-inherited
linear.description:
## Problem

Authority and ROE state is projected (<issue id="09fd8608-86ec-4243-888d-7dd0f126a8d2" label="DRG-182" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-182/project-command-authority-and-rules-of-engagement-state" />, <issue id="62f19a5c-38c2-44cb-ad50-c2e2ba23b291" label="DRG-209" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-209/slice-a-headless-authority-and-roe-projection" />), and WRA salvo-remaining shows on weapon chrome (<issue id="b052e2f4-59ae-43a4-850f-ae28460de62f" label="DRG-259" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-259/c2-02-wra-salvo-remaining-on-weapon-chrome" />). But the player cannot see *where* a unit's effective doctrine, ROE, or WRA value comes from (side, mission, group, or unit override), or reset an override back to inherited. In CMO this inheritance view is the main way a player finds out why a unit held fire or fired unexpectedly.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3.3.12: every doctrine option has an "inherited" setting. A unit follows its side's doctrine, or its mission's doctrine if assigned to one, and buttons reset it to the inherited default. Doctrine, EMCON, and WRA are separate tabs. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>)
* CMO manual §6.3.8: side doctrine/ROE/WRA is set at the top level and "flows down to mission and then groups/units". The WRA tab lists every weapon the side uses. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="9cb22a1c-4d7a-499d-ba6d-44462898cedd" label="DRG-321" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-321/jev-vs3-roe-noul-facade-accept-coordinationcommandbridge" /> (ROE Noul + façade Accept) is about AI-assisted ROE suggestions, not showing inheritance. No issue covers per-level provenance or reset.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `DoctrineInheritanceProjection` gives, for each selected unit and each doctrine/ROE/WRA field: the effective value, the source level (Side/Mission/Group/Unit), and the overridden parent value if there is one.
* Reset-to-inherited is sent as a command through the command façade and recorded in the order log. It is never a UI-side state mutation.
* The unit panel shows an override marker and a source badge for each field, and the WRA rows show target-type × quantity × range using the existing <issue id="b052e2f4-59ae-43a4-850f-ae28460de62f" label="DRG-259" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-259/c2-02-wra-salvo-remaining-on-weapon-chrome" /> chrome.
* The engagement explanation (<issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />) can cite the doctrine source level when doctrine is the refusal reason.
* Tests cover inherited, mission-overridden, and unit-overridden fields, and the reset round-trip under replay.

Source: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

* **Links:** authority/ROE projections [DRG-182](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-182>), [DRG-209](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-209>); WRA chrome [DRG-259](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-259>); explanation [DRG-168](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168>) (C2 guide in <pull-request id="b80cd6c2-4f2a-4e86-b255-054abcbe5ec6" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#759" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/docsc2-reconcile-both-documentation-stacks-and-canonical-guides-e1c12e5af761" />); not a duplicate of [DRG-321](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-321>). ADR-010 command façade.
* **Dependencies:** <issue id="62f19a5c-38c2-44cb-ad50-c2e2ba23b291" label="DRG-209" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-209/slice-a-headless-authority-and-roe-projection" /> (Slice C must not edit Skills/ until it lands).
* **Fences (from rubric H3/H5):** headless projection first; source-fence test (no UnityEngine/MonoBehaviour/ApplyOrder/DecisionLog write/SimulationSession/DelegationBridge refs); replay hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged, no ReplayGolden re-bless; any visible UI change gets a named [DRG-208](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208>) Play Mode walk item (human gate).

## Approved recommendation follow-through — 2026-10-30

User instruction: “proceed with your recommendations” following the game-mechanics/UX review. [Delivery plan](<https://app.notion.com/p/409f7cb4e4df815bbccfe465326584cc?pvs=204>). Baseline main 570a7f843ebffaa0ec9f2a3d9a7871d0354adc51. Product direction is authorized; no runtime delivery, passing tests, current-head owner acceptance, or protected-method waiver is asserted.

Source correction: DoctrineInheritanceProjection already exists. Extend it and its binder/tests; do not introduce a duplicate projection.

At main 570a7f84, ScenarioPolicyProfile.ResolveUnitPolicy resolves unit override, then mission, then friendly/opposing default. The existing projection carries a single source label; this is not proof of a complete per-field Side/Mission/Group/Unit cascade.

Acceptance refinement:

* Each supported displayed source/effective value matches the authoritative resolver.
* Unsupported source levels/fields are explicit; do not invent Group inheritance.
* Reset-to-inherited requires a real domain command, resulting-policy validation and replayable evidence. No direct UI dictionary mutation.
* Extend current explanation wording to cite the same authoritative source.

linear.title: Multi-target manual weapon allocation plan with per-weapon can-fire reasons
linear.description:
## Problem

The attack-options menu (<issue id="edefdae9-4a5b-49dc-ba94-cc0d4a461203" label="DRG-262" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262/c2-05-attack-options-menu-preview-parity" />) previews one shooter against one target. There is no way to build a manual allocation plan across several selected targets and shooters: N weapons per target, with a per-weapon "OK, can fire" or a specific reason it can't. CMO's manual allocation dialog (Shift+F1) is the main player tool for coordinated strikes and for learning weapon limits.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3 (Engage Target(s) Manual): drag-select multiple targets, pick an attacker, and see suitable weapons grouped by type. Legal weapons that are outside firing parameters show the reason in red; valid ones show "OK - Can fire". You allocate a quantity per target, and allocations show both per attacker and per target. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>) and [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-3-shortcut-buttons-and-windows/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-3-shortcut-buttons-and-windows/>)
* CMO combat chapter: manual assignment is "a very effective method of getting good feedback on weaponry limitations", because the crew runs an exhaustive checklist of conditions. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="edefdae9-4a5b-49dc-ba94-cc0d4a461203" label="DRG-262" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262/c2-05-attack-options-menu-preview-parity" /> is single-target preview parity, <issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" /> covers abort codes in the engage explanation, <issue id="0f26c476-2643-4cb9-b689-d068770f58bd" label="DRG-172" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-172/add-threat-assessment-and-weapon-recommendation" /> covers recommendations, and <issue id="8d85d519-5cec-4c0a-a35a-63206eb9d6cc" label="DRG-224" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224/slice-b-headless-magazine-and-salvo-employment-ledger" /> is the employment ledger. None covers a multi-target allocation plan.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `AllocationPlanProjection` takes {shooters\[\], targets\[\], allocations\[\]} and returns, for each (shooter, weapon, target): Can-fire, or a domain `FireAbortReason` code reused from <issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />. It also returns per-target and per-shooter totals and the remaining magazine count from the <issue id="8d85d519-5cec-4c0a-a35a-63206eb9d6cc" label="DRG-224" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224/slice-b-headless-magazine-and-salvo-employment-ledger" /> ledger.
* Committing a plan sends ordinary engage commands through the command façade. The projection itself never fires and does not touch the DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath.
* The UI lists allocations by attacker and by target. Reasons use the same text source as <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />/<issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />.
* Over-allocation beyond the magazine is rejected with a reason before commit.
* Tests cover a 2×3 plan, a mixed can-fire/abort result, an over-allocation reject, and replay determinism of the committed orders.

Source: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

* **Links:** attack options [DRG-262](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262>), abort codes [DRG-265](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265>) (C2 guide in <pull-request id="b80cd6c2-4f2a-4e86-b255-054abcbe5ec6" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#759" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/docsc2-reconcile-both-documentation-stacks-and-canonical-guides-e1c12e5af761" />), recommendations [DRG-172](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-172>), employment ledger [DRG-224](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224>), explanation [DRG-168](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168>). ADR-010 command façade.
* **Size note:** headless `AllocationPlanProjection` and the UI may ship as two PRs (\~400 changed lines is guidance); the AC above already separates them.
* **Fences (from rubric H3/H5):** headless projection first; source-fence test (no UnityEngine/MonoBehaviour/ApplyOrder/DecisionLog write/SimulationSession/DelegationBridge refs); replay hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged, no ReplayGolden re-bless; any visible UI change gets a named [DRG-208](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208>) Play Mode walk item (human gate).

Surface (CMANO stamp 2026-10-29, main 3bcfbb7b): src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/AllocationPlanProjection.cs (+types, new); tests: src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/AllocationPlanProjectionTests.cs (new), AttackMenuPanelBinderTests.cs, UnitDetailPanelBinderAttackMenuTests.cs; UI PR: src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/AttackMenuPanelBinder.cs, src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Presentation/AttackOptionsPreviewBinder.cs, unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/RightUnitPanelHost.cs. Read-only: EngageAttackOptions.cs, EngageAttackOrderResolver.cs, ThreatAssessment/WeaponRecommendation.cs. Constraints: preview-only; no order issue via CMD-31 (no TryIssuePlayerCommand or TryEnqueueAttackOption), so the "commit sends engage commands" AC is out of scope; no new method on DelegationBridge.GetAttackMenuOptions; no ReplayGolden re-bless.

linear.title: Explain target-location ambiguity vs weapon tolerance (area-of-uncertainty) in engage explanation
linear.description:
## Problem

The engagement explanation (<issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />) and contact provenance (<issue id="fc4092be-a4ee-4268-8ecb-27f647c14bf2" label="DRG-180" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-180/surface-contact-provenance-confidence-freshness-and-comms-state" />) show contact confidence, but not *positional* ambiguity relative to what a given weapon can tolerate. In CMO a frequent cause of "why won't it fire?" is that the contact's area of uncertainty is larger than the weapon's downrange or cross-range tolerance, scaled by an ambiguity doctrine (Ignore / Optimistic / Pessimistic). Players need to see that on the map and in the refusal text.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual: an ambiguous contact is one with an uncertainty area. With doctrine set to "Optimistic", the uncertainty must be under 3× the weapon tolerance before launch; with "Pessimistic", under 1×. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>)
* CMO combat chapter: the refusal reads "target's downrange ambiguity (X nm) is larger than … the weapon's acceptable limit (Y nm)", e.g. a ±10 nm contact against a 2 nm weapon limit. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="421c7902-2fda-47b4-8329-0603014f8fd7" label="DRG-385" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-385/asw-05-passive-bearing-only-tracking" /> (passive bearing-only tracking) adds uncertainty on the sim side. No presentation issue compares uncertainty with weapon tolerance.

## Acceptance criteria

* The headless explanation DTO adds, for each (weapon, contact): downrange and cross-range ambiguity, the weapon tolerance, the active ambiguity doctrine level, and pass/fail. All of it is read from existing contact and weapon data, with no new sim truth.
* The refusal text uses the CMO-style numbers ("ambiguity X nm > limit Y nm"), and the wording shares one source with <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />/<issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />.
* The map draws the contact's area-of-uncertainty ellipse from the projection, and hiding it is a declutter option (<issue id="c8b79a30-0b7e-4f3f-a4b0-0b22320a67b1" label="DRG-176" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176/set-combat-picture-performance-and-declutter-budgets" /> budget).
* Tests cover a contact inside tolerance, inside 3× (Optimistic passes, Pessimistic fails), and outside, all with replay-stable output.

Source: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

* **Links:** explanation [DRG-168](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168>), provenance [DRG-180](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-180>), abort wording [DRG-265](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265>), passive tracking [DRG-385](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-385>), declutter [DRG-176](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176>).
* **Dependencies:** the ellipse declutter toggle references the <issue id="c8b79a30-0b7e-4f3f-a4b0-0b22320a67b1" label="DRG-176" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176/set-combat-picture-performance-and-declutter-budgets" /> budget, which is not yet defined; the headless DTO and refusal text do not depend on it.
* **Fences (from rubric H3/H5):** headless projection first; source-fence test (no UnityEngine/MonoBehaviour/ApplyOrder/DecisionLog write/SimulationSession/DelegationBridge refs); replay hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged, no ReplayGolden re-bless; any visible UI change gets a named [DRG-208](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208>) Play Mode walk item (human gate).

## Approved recommendation follow-through — 2026-10-30

User instruction: “proceed with your recommendations” following the game-mechanics/UX review. [Delivery plan](<https://app.notion.com/p/409f7cb4e4df815bbccfe465326584cc?pvs=204>). Baseline main 570a7f843ebffaa0ec9f2a3d9a7871d0354adc51. Product direction is authorized; no runtime delivery, passing tests, current-head owner acceptance, or protected-method waiver is asserted.

Source-contract prerequisite discovered during follow-through: ContactProvenanceState at main 570a7f84 has identification confidence, freshness/age and comms flags, but no downrange/cross-range ambiguity or weapon tolerance. This establishes a gap in that DTO, not proof that no other domain provider exists.

Before numeric UI work:

* Identify authoritative producer fields, units, unknown representation and observation time for both contact uncertainty and weapon tolerance.
* If absent, scope a Sim-owned capability/provider dependency; never manufacture values in presentation.
* Reconcile ambiguity doctrine/multipliers with Aegis's actual resolver. Reference-product 1x/3x examples are not an implemented Aegis contract.
* Missing dimensions remain Unknown; no ellipse from identity confidence.
* Keep shooter/weapon/contact/time correlation; historical refusal must not borrow future facts.
* The ellipse still depends on <issue id="c8b79a30-0b7e-4f3f-a4b0-0b22320a67b1" label="DRG-176" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176/set-combat-picture-performance-and-declutter-budgets" /> declutter budgets.

<issue id="119b2d7c-9bde-4b90-a81d-702fa8307b1c" label="DRG-271" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-271/c2-17-stale-datalink-contact-icons-and-queued-order-badge" /> can deliver existing information-quality badges independently. linear.title: ECCM columns SQLite persistence (DRG-386 follow-up from #713)
linear.description:
Follow-up deferred from [PR #713](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/713>) (merged `3f5ae73f`; DRG-379/386/390), listed under "Follow-ups (not in this PR)".

`CatalogSensorBinding.RadarScanType`, `FrequencyAgile` and `RadarTechGeneration` are read and validated from catalog JSON (`CatalogRadarScanTypes.Validate`). But `CatalogJsonImporter.WriteSqlite`'s `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO sensor` doesn't write them, and `SqliteCatalogReader` returns the defaults (empty / false / 0). So a SQLite-backed catalog gets no ECCM jam adjustment.

## Scope

* New extend-only migration under `assets/data/catalog/migrations` adding `radar_scan_type`, `frequency_agile`, `radar_tech_generation` to `sensor` (and to `sensor_quarantine` if quarantine rows round-trip).
* `CatalogJsonImporter` (sensor and quarantine inserts) writes the columns; `SqliteCatalogReader` maps them.
* Round-trip test: JSON → SQLite → reader equals the JSON reader result and passes `CatalogRadarScanTypes.Validate`.

## Constraints

* `CatalogWriteGate` **writes are hard-no.** `InsertStagingSensor` / `catalog_staging_sensor` and `CatalogQuarantinePromoter.InsertSensor` don't carry these columns. Extending the staged write path is out of scope and needs a CMANO Surface stamp plus owner GO as a separate item.
* Check whether `CatalogSnapshotHasher` output changes. Replay hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged; no ReplayGolden re-bless.

Design notes: `docs/engineering/los-eccm-offgrid.md`.

linear.title: Fuel drains ~60× too fast in Play Mode — hardcoded deltaSeconds vs 1/60 host cadence
linear.description:
**LIVE defect**, not latent. Every link verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-24.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Play Mode host ticks at 1/60 s | `SimplePlayModeSimHost.cs:23` — `simTimeStep = 1f/60f`; `:108` `Update()`; `:123` `_simTime += simTimeStep`; `:124` `bridgeHost.RunTick(this, this)` |
| 2 | Host forwards to the bridge | `DelegationBridgeHost.cs:158` — `Bridge.Tick(snapshot, sink)` |
| 3 | Bridge drains a **full second** every call | `DelegationBridge.cs:378` — `_fuelTimeline.Drain(simTick, snapshot.SimTime, 1.0, unitIds)` |
| 4 | Drain is unconditional | `FuelLedger.cs:29-40` — `remaining -= burnRate * deltaSeconds`, no gating |

**Result: \~60× fuel over-drain** whenever a fuel-burn scenario runs through the Play Mode host.

## Fix direction (landed on PR)

Pass real elapsed delta into `Drain` via `_lastFuelSimTime` on `EmitFuelTransitions` only (ADR-020 Decision 1; CRITICAL hub localized).

## PRs

| PR | Status |
| -- | -- |
| **#437** `drgamtd/drg-50-fuel-playmode-delta-main` | **Active land path** |
| #406 | Superseded (docs/patch only) |
| #407 | Superseded (CONFLICTING) |

## Local verification (2026-08-09)

linear.title: Battle graphics: weapons firing, shooter–target tracks, telemetry, effects (presentation)
linear.description:
## Goal

Render the combat-event contract as a readable **battle graphic** between units: weapons firing, shooter–target tracking, weapon telemetry, and bounded weapon effects. **Presentation-only** (ADR-010 / presentation wall). Bind existing combat-event projection ([DRG-165](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165>)); do not invent a second combat-fact source.

## User story

As a player, I want to see engagements between units on the combat picture so I can tell who is shooting whom, with what family, and where the weapon is in its lifecycle — without leaving the map for a separate 3D tool.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missile, gun, and laser (or energy) engagements are distinguishable without color alone
- [ ] Each engagement shows shooter, target, weapon family, and lifecycle state at tactical zoom
- [ ] Shooter→target track / allocation geometry is visible when facts exist (Command analog: targeting / illumination vectors; salvo allocation between attacker and contact)
- [ ] In-flight / in-progress weapons show track or trail telemetry from projection (heading/path enough for BVR readability; not cinematic-only)
- [ ] Fire / launch and terminal effects are short-lived and budgeted; salvos/bursts aggregate at operational zoom (declutter)
- [ ] Tooltip or detail chrome supplies the readable text equivalent (accessibility)
- [ ] Replay-stable: presentation consumes projection only; no silent ReplayGolden re-bless
- [ ] Hard-no: MapPlaceholderPanelHost / GlobeMapProductHost overlay nits, DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath, CatalogWriteGate writes, SimulationSession, CMD-31/32/34

## Command / CMO reference notes (research 2026-09-22)

Use as *reference vocabulary*, not pixel-copy:

1. **Native map** — Zoomable globe with units, contacts, courses, range rings, weapon allocation UI (Engage Auto F1 / Manual Shift+F1). Manual: [https://ftp.matrixgames.com/pub/CommandModernOperations/CMO%20manual%20EBOOK.pdf](<https://ftp.matrixgames.com/pub/CommandModernOperations/CMO%20manual%20EBOOK.pdf>)
2. **Salvo allocation facts** — Lua `ScenEdit_WeaponAllocation(attacker, contact, side)` returns salvos between attacker↔contact. Aegis exposes equivalent via <issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" /> projection, not Lua.
3. **Map vectors** — Community/docs cite green targeting / red illumination vectors in Map Settings as 2D engagement geometry cues.
4. **3D / Tacview** — CMO streams real-time 3D via Tacview Advanced for missile trails / corkscrew BVR geometry ambiguous top-down. Matrix UI+Tacview article + Tacview↔CMO setup (attachments).
5. **Altitude / pin-cushion** — Optional true-altitude poles for aerospace — nice-to-have, not MVP.

**Product stance:** Strong **2D combat-picture** graphic first (Command-native map readability). Optional later 3D/Tacview-like view is out of MVP unless Play Mode proves 2D insufficient for BVR.

## Surface (GitNexus stamp — CMANO 2026-09-22)

Index: laptop `cmano-clone` @ `4190fb1` (GitNexus impact on `CombatEvent` / `CombatEventProjection` / `CombatPresentationFrame`).

linear.description:

reserved-by: Decision (CMANO successor) · claimed-by: bc-47f0bddd-7ca0-587a-b9cf-9501840d21cf · Surface: Evidence/\*\* + Host/Host.Tests csproj ProjectReference widen

Fences: no `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/` source edits; no `OnScenarioFinalized` change; no paid providers; no <issue id="e7e53ecd-9226-43e0-bf4a-87e657fd2a28" label="DRG-743" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-743/ai-s1-2-jsonl-evidence-writer-on-net-11-with-atomic-publish-and-cross" /> JSONL this reservation; no sln/csproj/Program.cs.

---

## Problem

`HindsightSessionFinalizer` builds a one-paragraph string summary and sends it fire-and-forget. There is no structured, citable record of what happened in a run.

## Scope

In `Ai.Host`, a pure projection from `IReadOnlyOrderLog`, `AgentPerformanceAarProjection`, and the authoritative result fields into the frozen evidence DTO.

* Covers chronological entries, decision records, policy denials, engagements, and controller changes.
* Evidence ID is `{fingerprint-prefix}:{SequenceId}`.
* Stable ordering by `SequenceId`.
* A side filter runs inside the projection. Entries the viewing side could not see are dropped unless debrief mode is explicitly set.
* Quantitative summary values (decision count, denials, engagements, objectives ratio) are computed here from the source, never by a model.

This part is framework-neutral and does not need the .NET 11 upgrade.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Identical input yields identical ordered evidence.
2. Every fixture's expected evidence-ID list matches exactly.
3. Two-sided fixture: no hidden-side entry appears in player-side output; debrief mode includes them and records the flag.
4. The order log is not mutated; fingerprint before equals fingerprint after.
5. `OnScenarioFinalized` is not changed.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the Contracts and Fixtures issues.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

linear.title: [NET11-D] Compatibility fixtures: corrupt-CRC scenario package test and net10/net11 replay comparison
linear.description:
## Problem

Two .NET 11 behaviour changes touch code this repository depends on, and neither has a test today.

* ZIP: CRC32 is now validated on read, and async open loads entries eagerly. `AegisScenarioPackage` uses `ZipFile.OpenAsync` and `OpenReadAsync`, so a corrupt package now fails at open instead of at entry read.
* Runtime numerics: `Math.Round(value, digits)` is now correctly rounded, and unchecked float-to-small-integer casts saturate. Replay determinism needs direct proof.

## Scope

1. Add one corrupt-CRC scenario package fixture and a test that asserts the failure is reported cleanly through both the sync and async paths. The test must pass on `net10.0` and `net11.0`.
2. Run the replay comparison experiment: with SDK 11 installed, temporarily multi-target the replay test project to `net10.0;net11.0` on a throwaway branch and compare fingerprints from one commit on one machine. Report the result. Do not merge the multi-target change.
3. Confirm by analyzer or search that Sim, Delegation, and Data contain no unchecked float-to-`byte`/`short`/`char` casts. A pattern search found none.

New test files only. Can start now.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Corrupt-package test green on the current target.
2. Replay comparison result posted here: fingerprints equal, or the first differing tick identified.
3. Cast audit result posted here.
4. Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged. No golden re-bless.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

>>> Agent notes

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): new fixture and test under `src/ProjectAegis.Data.Tests/Scenario/`. Read-only: `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/AegisScenarioPackage.cs`, `AegisScenarioPackage.Async.cs`.

`Math.Round(value, digits)` call sites outside tick paths: `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Validation/Rules/ValidationRules.cs` (lines near 286 and 356), `src/ProjectAegis.Data/PlatformAssistant/PlatformRelativeScaler.cs`. Check that their existing tests cover a midpoint value.

>>>

linear.title: Source MessageLogProjection combat lines from the CombatEvent contract, not the decision log
linear.description:
## Problem

`MessageLogProjection` still builds its launch, abort, and outcome lines straight from the order/decision log (`OrderLogEntryKind.Engagement` / `EngagementOutcome` payloads). It does not read the <issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" /> `CombatEvent` contract. That leaves the message log as a second combat-fact path, which breaks <issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" />'s rule that combat events are the only combat-fact source for presentation.

## Evidence

* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MessageLogProjection.cs` on main: lines \~47–61 switch on `EngagementOutcomeRecord` / `EngagementRecord` ("Unit … launched engagement …", "Engagement aborted: {AbortReasonCode}"), and `ProjectCombatOutcome` (\~175–211) formats Kill/Intercept/Hit/Miss directly.
* Consumers: `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Bridge/MessageLogBridge.cs` (`MessageLogProjection.Project(log)` and `Project(bridge.GetLiveOrderLogView())`).
* PR [drgaciw/cmano-clone#696](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featcombat-drg-165-combat-event-contract-consumes-slice-a-04ba3acac253>) (<issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" />) fixed only `CombatPresentationFrameBridge` (see `docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-06-drg-165-combat-event-contract-audit.md`). It did not touch `MessageLogProjection`. PR [drgaciw/cmano-clone#700](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-card-drg-353354355-contact-card-hardening-drg-322-attack-283b8d44d493>) also did not touch it.
* Overlap: the abort/refusal wording here overlaps <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" /> refusal text. Agree on one refusal-text source before changing either. Related: <issue id="741eb9d4-8afc-499f-a722-1cfde01cae70" label="DRG-376" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-376/bind-live-hud-to-messagelogbridgeprojectlive-delegationbridgehostcs649" /> (live HUD binding to `MessageLogBridge.ProjectLive`).
* This change needs its own Surface (CMANO to scope it later). It is not part of <issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" />.

## Acceptance criteria

* Combat launch, refusal/abort, and terminal-outcome message-log lines come from `CombatEventSnapshot` (via `CombatEventLogProjection`), not from `.Engagements` / `.EngagementOutcomes` reads.
* Refusal wording matches the <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" /> refusal text, or the divergence is written down.
* A source-fence test (like `Frame_bridge_reads_combat_facts_only_through_the_combat_event_contract`) covers `MessageLogProjection`.
* Replay goldens stay unchanged, or any change is explained.

Source: Project Aegis room 2026-10-07 (SliceB/SliceC/Hygiene)

Because the live path passes already-filtered entries, delegation fog is preserved without bridge changes. Keep message categories stable (`WEAPON_LAUNCH`, `ENGAGE_ABORT`, `KILL_CONFIRMED`, `INTERCEPT_SUCCESS`, `HIT`, `MISS`) because `CombatDomainActivityTags`, `CombatDomainsHotTickTracker`, `AlertSeverityMap` and `MessageLogCategoryClassMap` key on them. linear.title: Message log raw-text view and deterministic after-action text export
linear.description:
## Problem

The after-action ledger (<issue id="9b776f75-8294-4519-9e52-85f656fd4a3a" label="DRG-218" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-218/slice-c-headless-after-action-ledger" />) and the timeline (<issue id="8741c4c5-8d30-4157-a995-0818ca5171d1" label="DRG-171" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-171/add-combat-timeline-and-after-action-review" />) exist, but there is no plain chronological text view of the message log and no export file for after-action analysis or bug reports. CMO offers an interactive categorized view, a raw-text view, and "print to file" (AALog.txt). Aegis testers and players need a deterministic text artifact they can diff between replays.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3.1.7: in a separate window, the message log toggles between the interactive categorized view and a "raw text" view (detailed messages in chronological order). [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>)
* CMO manual §6.3.11: Message Log → "print to file" writes AALog.Txt "for after action analysis of the game mechanics". [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="8741c4c5-8d30-4157-a995-0818ca5171d1" label="DRG-171" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-171/add-combat-timeline-and-after-action-review" /> (timeline/AAR UI) and <issue id="9b776f75-8294-4519-9e52-85f656fd4a3a" label="DRG-218" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-218/slice-c-headless-after-action-ledger" /> (headless AAR ledger) do not cover a text export or a raw view. <issue id="082c1311-1fd2-4dcf-bef4-ac6765044ab9" label="DRG-402" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-402/source-messagelogprojection-combat-lines-from-the-combatevent-contract" /> changes the source of the combat lines.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `MessageLogTextExport` renders the projected log (after <issue id="082c1311-1fd2-4dcf-bef4-ac6765044ab9" label="DRG-402" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-402/source-messagelogprojection-combat-lines-from-the-combatevent-contract" />, combat lines come from CombatEvent) as stable plain text: sim time, category, subject id, message.
* Two replays of the same (scenario, seed) produce byte-identical exports, checked by a golden test.
* The UI toggles between the categorized and raw views and has an export action that writes to a user path. Export is read-only and never mutates sim state.
* The export works under AttachReplayViewer.

Source: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

linear.title: Per-category message-log notification policy (log / pause / map balloon / drop to 1x)
linear.description:
## Problem

The message log has no per-category notification policy. In CMO, each message type (new contact, weapon launch, weapon endgame, unit lost, fuel, etc.) can be set to: show in the log, raise a pop-up that pauses the sim, show a balloon on the map at the subject, and drop time compression to 1x. Without this, a player running at high time compression can miss a hostile launch or a lost unit until well after it happens. Aegis has pause and acceleration (<issue id="33bfdfcc-aeed-49b3-b9a5-e2dd6df86193" label="DRG-14" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-14/implement-sim-clock-time-acceleration-and-pause" />) and a message log (<issue id="082c1311-1fd2-4dcf-bef4-ac6765044ab9" label="DRG-402" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-402/source-messagelogprojection-combat-lines-from-the-combatevent-contract" />, <issue id="1a498761-2ae0-4eec-b4ef-ac1a72a91cca" label="DRG-268" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-268/c2-13-message-log-click-unit-explain-deep-link" />), but nothing links log categories to attention or time-control behavior.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual, Game Options → Message Log: per message type, "Show on Message Log", "Raise Pop-Up" (pauses the game), "Show Balloon" (on the map at the subject's location), and "Timescale X1" (drop from acceleration to 1x). [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-9-drop-down-menus/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-9-drop-down-menus/>)
* CMO manual §3.1.7: the log is split into categories that can be minimized or emphasized, so routine messages don't bury critical ones. Hovering a message highlights its subject on the map. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>)
* Player feedback asks for exactly this per-type control, including keeping time running while still being notified. [https://steamcommunity.com/app/1076160/discussions/0/2573194192006749192/](<https://steamcommunity.com/app/1076160/discussions/0/2573194192006749192/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="1a498761-2ae0-4eec-b4ef-ac1a72a91cca" label="DRG-268" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-268/c2-13-message-log-click-unit-explain-deep-link" /> covers click → unit deep-link, and <issue id="082c1311-1fd2-4dcf-bef4-ac6765044ab9" label="DRG-402" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-402/source-messagelogprojection-combat-lines-from-the-combatevent-contract" /> covers sourcing combat lines from CombatEvent. Neither covers category policy or time-control escalation.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `MessageCategoryPolicy` projection maps each message category to {Log, Pause, Balloon, DropToRealTime}. Defaults are data-driven, not hardcoded.
* When a matching message arrives, the projection emits an attention intent. Pause and 1x requests go through the existing command/time façade as player-visible requests. The projection never calls sim internals directly, and the change does not touch the DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath or SimulationSession.
* The UI binds only to the projection. A settings panel edits the policy, and balloon markers anchor to the message subject.
* Replay is deterministic: under AttachReplayViewer, policy-driven pauses are suppressed or reported but never change the order log.
* Tests cover the default mapping, a user override, and the no-op under replay.

linear.title: [AI-S2-1] AAR assistant pipeline in the host: prompt build, citation and number validation, explicit failure statuses
linear.description:
## Problem

A model-written after-action summary is only useful if every claim can be traced to evidence and no number is invented.

## Scope

In `Ai.Host`, a pipeline that takes exported evidence and returns a structured result: summary, outcomes, uncertainties, citations.

* The host copies quantitative values from the source report. The model supplies prose and evidence IDs only.
* Evidence text is delimited as data and never concatenated into instructions.
* Validation before publication: reject if any cited ID is absent from the evidence (`RejectedCitation`) or any number in prose disagrees with the report (`RejectedNumber`).
* Timeout, cancellation, malformed output, and unavailable provider each return their explicit status **plus the existing deterministic report**.
* The result is published as an artifact with the full envelope.

Runs entirely on `FakeChatClient` in CI.

## Acceptance criteria

1. All citations resolve on every fixture. Zero fabricated IDs. Zero contradictory numbers.
2. A scripted fake response with a fabricated ID is rejected. Same for a wrong number.
3. Every failure fixture returns its explicit status and the deterministic report.
4. The embedded-instruction fixture does not change behaviour.
5. Replay fingerprints match with the pipeline enabled, disabled, delayed, or failing.
6. No network access in tests.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the evidence projection and Wave 0 integration.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host/Aar/**`, tests under `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host.Tests/Aar/**` (new).

linear.title: [AI-S1-2] JSONL evidence writer on .NET 11 with atomic publish and cross-platform determinism
linear.description:
## Problem

Evidence for a long run is large. It should stream to disk, hash identically on Windows and Linux, and never leave a half-written file that looks complete.

## Scope

In `Ai.Host`, write the evidence DTO stream as JSON Lines using `JsonSerializer.SerializeAsyncEnumerable(..., topLevelValues: true)`, a .NET 11 API.

* Source-generated `JsonTypeInfo<T>` for a fixed property order.
* Output is always LF and compact; the API ignores `WriteIndented`.
* Write to a temporary file, then publish atomically through the artifact store.
* Evidence is persisted **before** Hindsight or a provider is asked to process it.
* Record a content hash in the envelope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Round-trip parse equals input for every fixture.
2. Identical input yields byte-identical output on Windows and Linux (compare hashes in CI).
3. Cancellation mid-export leaves no published file; a rerun succeeds.
4. Replay fingerprints match with export enabled, disabled, delayed, or failing.
5. Peak memory recorded for one small and one large log.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the evidence projection and by gate G0 (upgrade PR 2), because the API needs `net11.0`.

linear.title: [H6] Product decision: save-load only vs multiplayer for H6
linear.description:
## Context

H6 bundles two things of very different size:

* **Save/load** is single-player and fits the deterministic core. The GDD already specifies it (`design/gdd/simulation-core-time.md`: "Save/load restores simTick, scenarioSeed, RNG stream counters (checkpoint + log tail)").
* **Multiplayer** is excluded from v1 in `design/gdd/game-concept.md` ("Out (v1): full multiplayer") and in `production/stage.txt`. The roadmap calls it "out of single-player deploy model". It would change the deploy model, store copy (`production/release/store/store-page-draft.md`: "Singleplayer focus"), and the `DelegationBridge` order-injection path.

This is an **owner decision**. It is not engineering work.

## Decision options

1. Save/load only, and multiplayer stays out of v1. This is the smallest ADR and the least bridge exposure.
2. Save/load now, with multiplayer as a separate later horizon (for example H9) behind its own ADR.
3. Save/load + multiplayer together. That needs a netcode model (deterministic lockstep vs server-authoritative), a v1 scope change, and store/FAQ changes.

## Questions the owner must answer

- [ ] Save/load: manual save slots, autosave, or both? Mid-engagement saves allowed?
- [ ] Must saves survive a build or catalog update, or only the same build and same catalog snapshot?
- [ ] Is multiplayer in or out of H6? If in: co-op or adversarial, LAN or online, turn/lockstep or real time?
- [ ] Is a `DelegationBridge` / `SimulationSession` **product waiver** acceptable, or must the design be zero-touch?

## Entry gate

This story **is** the "product confirmation" half of the H6 gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The decision is recorded as a comment here and in the Notion H4–H6 intake page
- [ ] The H6 ADR story is updated with the chosen option
- [ ] If multiplayer is out, the H6 epic is renamed or scoped to save/load and the `cmano-clone` H6 milestone note is updated after GO

Surface: none (decision only)

## Start condition

**Nothing is started until the owner gives GO.** This issue stays in Backlog and no agent is dispatched.

2026-09-30 user authorized all review recommendations: use **save first / multiplayer separate and later** as the roadmap planning direction. Keep manual/autosave, retention, cross-build compatibility and architecture constraints as explicit decision questions. Record owner approval of the eventual product/ADR package separately; this planning update does not claim implementation or close the issue.

linear.title: [H6] Read-only spike: replay-to-tick resume feasibility + mutable session-state inventory
linear.description:
## Context

A save model that keeps `DelegationBridge` and `SimulationSession` untouched depends on one thing: whether a session can be rebuilt by deterministically re-simulating `(scenario, seed, catalog snapshot, order log)` up to a tick through existing public APIs. The facts this rests on:

* `docs/engineering/determinism-and-replay.md`: `(scenario, seed)` gives an identical order log. `SeededRng` is a pure function of `(seed, domain, entityId, simTick, drawIndex)`.
* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs` and `ReplayCheckpoint`: hashes only, so they can verify a resume but cannot restore one.
* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/BalticReplayHarness.cs`: an existing headless re-simulation driver.
* `SimulationSession` holds non-deterministic or UI-driven state that a save must capture: clock pause and acceleration (`SetTimeAccelerationFactor`), `WatchAttentionQueue`, `WatchAutoPauseGate`, direct-control state, and queued human orders.

## Task (read-only)

1. Inventory every piece of mutable session state that is **not** reproducible from `(scenario, seed, order log)`.
2. Estimate replay-to-tick cost for a long session. Use existing perf evidence such as `production/qa/swarm-a6-replay-performance-caps-2026-08-09.md` and batch-replay numbers.
3. List which existing public APIs a replay driver would call, and confirm none of them is a `DelegationBridge.Tick` / `SimulationSession` hotpath edit.
4. Write findings as input for the H6 ADR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Brief written under `production/agentic/` (or a scratch doc linked here), with a verified/unverified split
- [ ] State inventory table: field, owner type, reproducible yes/no
- [ ] Clear feasible / not-feasible verdict for a zero-touch replay-to-tick save
- [ ] **Zero** edits to `src/`, `unity/`, `tests/regression/`
