Evidence identity: The 2026-09-30 refresh cited a local checkout at C:\Users\dgorn\cmano-clone\cmano-clone, HEAD 4190fb1b49cd15775b6b995b7c245d73828cd7a2, with uncommitted changes. As of 2026-11-20 that SHA is not on origin (absent from a fetched clone and from GitHub), and uncommitted working-tree changes cannot be pinned. Published main SHAs: last main tip at the time of the refresh, [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, 2:40 PM CDT, #681), which this page already named as a separate target; current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b) (2026-11-17, 7:16 PM CT). Blob links that previously used 4190fb1b now point at the same paths on [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd). Refreshed against main 1902dc12 because 4190fb1b was never pushed (ruling: Decision, 2026-11-20). Planning completion does not grant product acceptance. --- ## Overview The headless simulation supplies authoritative execution; the player prepares the scenario, begins execution, delegates orders, and inspects outcomes. This page describes the implemented session/tick contract and distinguishes it from proposed session restoration. UI reads projections and submits intent through approved command seams; it does not own the simulation clock or world state. The main orchestration source is [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs); delegation is [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs). GitNexus path-qualified context calls against this exact checkout corroborated both classes, plus ReplayCheckpointStore and the delegation SeededRng. Same-name sibling indexes are not interchangeable; graph results corroborate source navigation, not runtime proof. ## Player Fantasy Command a theater at the pace needed to understand events: plan before execution, pause to inspect attention and constraints, accelerate quiet periods, then see why delegated or human orders executed or were withheld. Outcomes remain reproducible for a fixed build and input sequence. Pause freezes the interactive simulation clock; it must not be presented as a guarantee that all orchestration queues and logs stop changing. ## Detailed Rules 1. Planning versus execution. SimulationSession.Tick and TickHeadless return false in Planning before running the session. BeginExecution changes the orchestrator phase; its initial Planning-to-Executing transition appends a mode-change record. The session does not infer readiness from elapsed calendar time. 2. Outer delegation call. RunExecutingTick calls Orchestrator.Tick once with the supplied ObservedState. The orchestrator drains approved orders, evaluates active agents, and drains agent/human issued queues into ExecutedOrders. It derives its order tick from the observed SimTime; this is distinct from the pipeline clock. 3. Interactive pause. The pause check occurs after the orchestrator call. A paused executing session may therefore drain queues or emit decision/denial records while its simulation clock does not advance. Tick returns true for the executing call even when paused; that return value alone does not prove a new simulation tick. 4. Engagement and cadence. An unpaused call selects Engage orders, applies communications and salvo/deconfliction gates, enqueues requests, and calls Sim.TickOnce in RealTime mode. It logs the initial results and applies damage handling, then performs acceleration-factor-minus-one extra pipeline steps. Delegation, result logging/damage handling, and the final logistics FSM call are not repeated for every extra step by this method. Do not describe acceleration as a whole-session tick repeated uniformly. 5. Headless execution. TickHeadless selects HeadlessBatch, bypassing the pipeline pause gate while retaining the pause flag. In Planning it still returns false. Watch attention can require acknowledgement or explicit override through TryResumeSim; legacy ResumeSim bypasses that watch gate. 6. Verification checkpoints. [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs) appends strictly increasing checkpoint ticks and finds the latest at/before a requested tick. [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpoint.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpoint.cs) contains SimTick, WorldHash, LogFingerprint, and LastSequenceId. These are verification metadata, not a serialized restorable session. ## Formulas - Clock time is SimClock.SimTime = SimTick * FixedDeltaSeconds; default delta is 1/60 second. Acceleration changes the number of fixed steps, not the delta. See [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Time/SimClock.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Time/SimClock.cs). - For an executing, unpaused session call with factor F, the pipeline advances 1 + max(0, F - 1) steps. F is clamped to 1–256. The session owns this outer acceleration loop; direct pipeline Accelerated mode separately uses F steps. See [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SimTickPipeline.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SimTickPipeline.cs). - Delegation [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/SeededRng.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/SeededRng.cs) initializes state from global seed XOR salted agent identity, substitutes 1 for zero, applies xorshift updates (13, 7, 17), then returns (state & 0xFFFFFF) / 0x1000000. Reproducibility requires the same seed, salt, and draw order. - The separate [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SeededRng.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SeededRng.cs) uses seed/domain/entity/tick/draw-index hashing. Its masked uint division can include the endpoint 1.0; the two RNG contracts must not be conflated. ## Edge Cases - Calling Tick during Planning is rejected even when headless execution was requested. - Paused execution is not queue immutability; distinguish observed order time, orchestration effects, and pipeline tick progression in diagnostics. - Repeating a checkpoint tick or recording an earlier tick is ignored; an empty/before-first lookup returns no checkpoint. - A hash checkpoint cannot reconstruct pending events, RNG state, engagements, resources, or authority-bearing mission state. - Proposed RPL-29–31 require same-build/scenario/catalog/policy uninterrupted-versus-restored equality and non-mutating corrupt/incompatible-load failure. These contracts, [DRG-348](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-348) and [DRG-349](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-349), are gated backlog work; save/resume and multiplayer are not established by replay goldens. ## Dependencies The [cmano-clone project](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9) links requirements 03/08/17, ADR-001 simulation boundary, ADR-003 order log, ADR-004 tick pipeline, and presentation ADR-010 sections 2–3 plus ADR-007. DelegationBridge remains zero-touch. Scenario policy, catalog, seed and ordered input identities are required context for deterministic comparisons. S122–S127 delivery follows evidence gates; [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208) remains owner Play Mode acceptance. ## Tuning Knobs Fixed delta and clock factor are existing implementation settings; factor bounds 1–256 are code constraints, not newly accepted product performance targets. Scenario-policy values govern gameplay tuning. Checkpoint frequency is chosen by the harness/caller, not persisted as a save/resume contract. Any cadence or performance change needs profiling, criterion-specific evidence and current upstream impact analysis before symbol edits; no parameter changes are authorized by this page. ## Acceptance Criteria These are review/verification criteria, not fresh execution results or owner signoff. - CS-01: verify Planning calls do not advance the pipeline; BeginExecution exposes the documented phase/log transition. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionPhaseTests. - CS-02: verify paused interactive clock remains unchanged while separately inspecting approved/human queue and log behavior; do not accept only the Tick boolean. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionClockControlsTests; queue/log coverage must be checked explicitly. - CS-03: compare factors 1 and greater than 1 against the documented outer/inner cadence; confirm fixed delta does not stretch. Existing clock tests are candidate mappings, not proof of uniform subsystem acceleration. - CS-04: verify headless pause override and watch acknowledgement/override behavior. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionWatchAttentionTests. - CS-05: repeat identical build/input/seed runs and compare state/order fingerprints; retain Baltic v2 hash 17144800277401907079. Use [AGENTS.md](http://AGENTS.md) standing gates and the six canonical replay cases; recorded counts must identify revision and local delta. - CS-06: review checkpoint metadata honesty and keep RPL-29–31 proposed until schema/feasibility/ADR and differential restore tests exist. - CS-07: collect criterion-level SHA/build/local delta/scenario/catalog/policy/test-layer/result evidence and an explicit owner decision under proposed VER-07.3–6. This draft and source inspection satisfy neither Editor coverage nor owner acceptance.

linear.title: [H6] Product decision: save-load only vs multiplayer for H6
linear.description:
## Context

H6 bundles two things of very different size:

* **Save/load** is single-player and fits the deterministic core. The GDD already specifies it (`design/gdd/simulation-core-time.md`: "Save/load restores simTick, scenarioSeed, RNG stream counters (checkpoint + log tail)").
* **Multiplayer** is excluded from v1 in `design/gdd/game-concept.md` ("Out (v1): full multiplayer") and in `production/stage.txt`. The roadmap calls it "out of single-player deploy model". It would change the deploy model, store copy (`production/release/store/store-page-draft.md`: "Singleplayer focus"), and the `DelegationBridge` order-injection path.

This is an **owner decision**. It is not engineering work.

## Decision options

1. Save/load only, and multiplayer stays out of v1. This is the smallest ADR and the least bridge exposure.
2. Save/load now, with multiplayer as a separate later horizon (for example H9) behind its own ADR.
3. Save/load + multiplayer together. That needs a netcode model (deterministic lockstep vs server-authoritative), a v1 scope change, and store/FAQ changes.

## Questions the owner must answer

- [ ] Save/load: manual save slots, autosave, or both? Mid-engagement saves allowed?
- [ ] Must saves survive a build or catalog update, or only the same build and same catalog snapshot?
- [ ] Is multiplayer in or out of H6? If in: co-op or adversarial, LAN or online, turn/lockstep or real time?
- [ ] Is a `DelegationBridge` / `SimulationSession` **product waiver** acceptable, or must the design be zero-touch?

## Entry gate

This story **is** the "product confirmation" half of the H6 gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The decision is recorded as a comment here and in the Notion H4–H6 intake page
- [ ] The H6 ADR story is updated with the chosen option
- [ ] If multiplayer is out, the H6 epic is renamed or scoped to save/load and the `cmano-clone` H6 milestone note is updated after GO

Surface: none (decision only)

## Start condition

**Nothing is started until the owner gives GO.** This issue stays in Backlog and no agent is dispatched.

2026-09-30 user authorized all review recommendations: use **save first / multiplayer separate and later** as the roadmap planning direction. Keep manual/autosave, retention, cross-build compatibility and architecture constraints as explicit decision questions. Record owner approval of the eventual product/ADR package separately; this planning update does not claim implementation or close the issue.

linear.title: [H6-SAVE-SLICE] Prove deterministic same-build save and resume before multiplayer
linear.description:
Owner: drg amtd. Proposed RPL-29–31; blocked by save contract and H6 product/ADR/spike decisions. No sprint dates assigned.

Acceptance: continuous N+M-tick run equals N-tick save/restore plus M-tick run for world hash, order log sequence/content and replay fingerprint using same build/catalog/scenario/seed. Include pending engagements/orders/triggers and corrupt/incompatible payload fixtures; failed restore leaves original session unchanged. Save-before-multiplayer boundary is explicit. Runtime implementation follows approved contract and GitNexus impact analysis; DelegationBridge zero-touch invariant preserved.

## Save/resume delivery alignment — 2026-10-30

Follow [DRG-348's contract draft](<https://app.notion.com/p/409f7cb4e4df81f59f6afed203c1d04f?pvs=204>) and the [command-experience delivery plan](<https://app.notion.com/p/409f7cb4e4df815bbccfe465326584cc?pvs=204>). The user authorized proceeding with the recommendations; ADR-029 already supplies the accepted save direction. <issue id="d224a671-afb7-4ea8-bf7e-84279249c710" label="DRG-348" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-348/h6-save-contract-define-complete-same-buildcatalog-save-resume-state" /> remains incomplete and is still the implementation dependency. Existing dependency relations are retained.

Extend the proof matrix beyond final-world hashes: compare journal order/results, log sequence/content and replay fingerprints at restoration and future boundaries. Include at least three interruption points (before approval, with a delayed order, during engagement/resource change), accelerated clocks, same-tick inputs, traits/rebrief, control handoff, pending salvo overrides, and unknown/omitted journal commands. Validate build/catalog/scenario identity and full catalog coverage. Rejection, cancellation and failed writes must preserve the active session or previous save slot as applicable.

Restore into an isolated world/snapshot/order-sink/bridge candidate, verify replay, then swap consistently and expose the paused session. Share the existing stepper; do not fork RunCore or assume ReplayCheckpointStore can hydrate. Journal the new alert-policy/control/doctrine commands when introduced. Optional external-provider replay must use captured inputs rather than live calls.

No runtime implementation, tests, performance result, owner acceptance or protected-method waiver is claimed. Development laptop is offline; required GitNexus impact is unavailable. Keep Backlog until the contract and execution prerequisites are satisfied.

linear.title: [H6] Product decision: save-load only vs multiplayer for H6
linear.description:
## Context

H6 bundles two things of very different size:

* **Save/load** is single-player and fits the deterministic core. The GDD already specifies it (`design/gdd/simulation-core-time.md`: "Save/load restores simTick, scenarioSeed, RNG stream counters (checkpoint + log tail)").
* **Multiplayer** is excluded from v1 in `design/gdd/game-concept.md` ("Out (v1): full multiplayer") and in `production/stage.txt`. The roadmap calls it "out of single-player deploy model". It would change the deploy model, store copy (`production/release/store/store-page-draft.md`: "Singleplayer focus"), and the `DelegationBridge` order-injection path.

This is an **owner decision**. It is not engineering work.

## Decision options

1. Save/load only, and multiplayer stays out of v1. This is the smallest ADR and the least bridge exposure.
2. Save/load now, with multiplayer as a separate later horizon (for example H9) behind its own ADR.
3. Save/load + multiplayer together. That needs a netcode model (deterministic lockstep vs server-authoritative), a v1 scope change, and store/FAQ changes.

## Questions the owner must answer

- [ ] Save/load: manual save slots, autosave, or both? Mid-engagement saves allowed?
- [ ] Must saves survive a build or catalog update, or only the same build and same catalog snapshot?
- [ ] Is multiplayer in or out of H6? If in: co-op or adversarial, LAN or online, turn/lockstep or real time?
- [ ] Is a `DelegationBridge` / `SimulationSession` **product waiver** acceptable, or must the design be zero-touch?

## Entry gate

This story **is** the "product confirmation" half of the H6 gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The decision is recorded as a comment here and in the Notion H4–H6 intake page
- [ ] The H6 ADR story is updated with the chosen option
- [ ] If multiplayer is out, the H6 epic is renamed or scoped to save/load and the `cmano-clone` H6 milestone note is updated after GO

Surface: none (decision only)

## Start condition

**Nothing is started until the owner gives GO.** This issue stays in Backlog and no agent is dispatched.

2026-09-30 user authorized all review recommendations: use **save first / multiplayer separate and later** as the roadmap planning direction. Keep manual/autosave, retention, cross-build compatibility and architecture constraints as explicit decision questions. Record owner approval of the eventual product/ADR package separately; this planning update does not claim implementation or close the issue.

linear.title: [H6-SAVE-SLICE] Prove deterministic same-build save and resume before multiplayer
linear.description:
Owner: drg amtd. Proposed RPL-29–31; blocked by save contract and H6 product/ADR/spike decisions. No sprint dates assigned.

Acceptance: continuous N+M-tick run equals N-tick save/restore plus M-tick run for world hash, order log sequence/content and replay fingerprint using same build/catalog/scenario/seed. Include pending engagements/orders/triggers and corrupt/incompatible payload fixtures; failed restore leaves original session unchanged. Save-before-multiplayer boundary is explicit. Runtime implementation follows approved contract and GitNexus impact analysis; DelegationBridge zero-touch invariant preserved.

## Save/resume delivery alignment — 2026-10-30

Follow [DRG-348's contract draft](<https://app.notion.com/p/409f7cb4e4df81f59f6afed203c1d04f?pvs=204>) and the [command-experience delivery plan](<https://app.notion.com/p/409f7cb4e4df815bbccfe465326584cc?pvs=204>). The user authorized proceeding with the recommendations; ADR-029 already supplies the accepted save direction. <issue id="d224a671-afb7-4ea8-bf7e-84279249c710" label="DRG-348" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-348/h6-save-contract-define-complete-same-buildcatalog-save-resume-state" /> remains incomplete and is still the implementation dependency. Existing dependency relations are retained.

Extend the proof matrix beyond final-world hashes: compare journal order/results, log sequence/content and replay fingerprints at restoration and future boundaries. Include at least three interruption points (before approval, with a delayed order, during engagement/resource change), accelerated clocks, same-tick inputs, traits/rebrief, control handoff, pending salvo overrides, and unknown/omitted journal commands. Validate build/catalog/scenario identity and full catalog coverage. Rejection, cancellation and failed writes must preserve the active session or previous save slot as applicable.

Restore into an isolated world/snapshot/order-sink/bridge candidate, verify replay, then swap consistently and expose the paused session. Share the existing stepper; do not fork RunCore or assume ReplayCheckpointStore can hydrate. Journal the new alert-policy/control/doctrine commands when introduced. Optional external-provider replay must use captured inputs rather than live calls.

No runtime implementation, tests, performance result, owner acceptance or protected-method waiver is claimed. Development laptop is offline; required GitNexus impact is unavailable. Keep Backlog until the contract and execution prerequisites are satisfied.

`CommsGridRegistry.ReportPosition(unitId, simTick, lat, lon)` exists and freezes reports while a unit is off grid, but only tests call it (`CommsGridRegistryTests`, `OffGridCommandFacadeTests`). linear.title: Source MessageLogProjection combat lines from the CombatEvent contract, not the decision log
linear.description:
## Problem

`MessageLogProjection` still builds its launch, abort, and outcome lines straight from the order/decision log (`OrderLogEntryKind.Engagement` / `EngagementOutcome` payloads). It does not read the <issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" /> `CombatEvent` contract. That leaves the message log as a second combat-fact path, which breaks <issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" />'s rule that combat events are the only combat-fact source for presentation.

## Evidence

* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MessageLogProjection.cs` on main: lines \~47–61 switch on `EngagementOutcomeRecord` / `EngagementRecord` ("Unit … launched engagement …", "Engagement aborted: {AbortReasonCode}"), and `ProjectCombatOutcome` (\~175–211) formats Kill/Intercept/Hit/Miss directly.
* Consumers: `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Bridge/MessageLogBridge.cs` (`MessageLogProjection.Project(log)` and `Project(bridge.GetLiveOrderLogView())`).
* PR [drgaciw/cmano-clone#696](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featcombat-drg-165-combat-event-contract-consumes-slice-a-04ba3acac253>) (<issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" />) fixed only `CombatPresentationFrameBridge` (see `docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-06-drg-165-combat-event-contract-audit.md`). It did not touch `MessageLogProjection`. PR [drgaciw/cmano-clone#700](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-card-drg-353354355-contact-card-hardening-drg-322-attack-283b8d44d493>) also did not touch it.
* Overlap: the abort/refusal wording here overlaps <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" /> refusal text. Agree on one refusal-text source before changing either. Related: <issue id="741eb9d4-8afc-499f-a722-1cfde01cae70" label="DRG-376" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-376/bind-live-hud-to-messagelogbridgeprojectlive-delegationbridgehostcs649" /> (live HUD binding to `MessageLogBridge.ProjectLive`).
* This change needs its own Surface (CMANO to scope it later). It is not part of <issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" />.

## Acceptance criteria

* Combat launch, refusal/abort, and terminal-outcome message-log lines come from `CombatEventSnapshot` (via `CombatEventLogProjection`), not from `.Engagements` / `.EngagementOutcomes` reads.
* Refusal wording matches the <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" /> refusal text, or the divergence is written down.
* A source-fence test (like `Frame_bridge_reads_combat_facts_only_through_the_combat_event_contract`) covers `MessageLogProjection`.
* Replay goldens stay unchanged, or any change is explained.

Source: Project Aegis room 2026-10-07 (SliceB/SliceC/Hygiene)

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

Surface: `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MessageLogProjection.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/MessageLogProjectionTests.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/MessageLogCombatEventSourceFenceTests.cs` (new).

Scope notes: `MessageLogProjection.Project(IReadOnlyList<OrderLogEntry>)` builds a bounded `DecisionLog` from the supplied entries (same pattern as `CombatPresentationFrameBridge.Build`) and reads launch / abort / terminal-outcome lines from `CombatEventLogProjection.Build(...)` (same assembly). Because the live path passes already-filtered entries, delegation fog is preserved without bridge changes. Keep message categories stable (`WEAPON_LAUNCH`, `ENGAGE_ABORT`, `KILL_CONFIRMED`, `INTERCEPT_SUCCESS`, `HIT`, `MISS`) because `CombatDomainActivityTags`, `CombatDomainsHotTickTracker`, `AlertSeverityMap` and `MessageLogCategoryClassMap` key on them. Existing tests in `MessageLogLiveBindingTests.cs`, `MessageLogCategoryClassMapTests.cs`, `CombatDomainsHotTickTrackerTests.cs` and `AlertSeverityMapTests.cs` must pass without edits. Refusal wording: reuse the DRG-168 text read-only or document the divergence in the PR. If a shared refusal-text helper has to be extracted from `EngagementExplanationProjection.cs`, stop and wait for #710 to merge; CMANO then re-stamps.

Read-only, do not edit: `CombatEventLogProjection.cs`, `EngagementExplanationProjection.cs` (owner draft #710); `MessageLogBridge.cs`, `DelegationBridgeHost.cs`, `MessageLogLiveBridgeTests.cs` (DRG-376). `BalticReplayHarness` fingerprints hash the decision log, not message text, so ReplayGolden should not move; any golden change must be explained, never silently re-blessed.

Surface stamped by CMANO 2026-10-07 (main 3f5ae73f). Owner lane: SliceB (first SliceB story while DRG-403 is on hold:owner-go). Not reserved.

linear.title: Message log raw-text view and deterministic after-action text export
linear.description:
## Problem

The after-action ledger (<issue id="9b776f75-8294-4519-9e52-85f656fd4a3a" label="DRG-218" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-218/slice-c-headless-after-action-ledger" />) and the timeline (<issue id="8741c4c5-8d30-4157-a995-0818ca5171d1" label="DRG-171" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-171/add-combat-timeline-and-after-action-review" />) exist, but there is no plain chronological text view of the message log and no export file for after-action analysis or bug reports. CMO offers an interactive categorized view, a raw-text view, and "print to file" (AALog.txt). Aegis testers and players need a deterministic text artifact they can diff between replays.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3.1.7: in a separate window, the message log toggles between the interactive categorized view and a "raw text" view (detailed messages in chronological order). [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>)
* CMO manual §6.3.11: Message Log → "print to file" writes AALog.Txt "for after action analysis of the game mechanics". [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="8741c4c5-8d30-4157-a995-0818ca5171d1" label="DRG-171" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-171/add-combat-timeline-and-after-action-review" /> (timeline/AAR UI) and <issue id="9b776f75-8294-4519-9e52-85f656fd4a3a" label="DRG-218" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-218/slice-c-headless-after-action-ledger" /> (headless AAR ledger) do not cover a text export or a raw view. <issue id="082c1311-1fd2-4dcf-bef4-ac6765044ab9" label="DRG-402" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-402/source-messagelogprojection-combat-lines-from-the-combatevent-contract" /> changes the source of the combat lines.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `MessageLogTextExport` renders the projected log (after <issue id="082c1311-1fd2-4dcf-bef4-ac6765044ab9" label="DRG-402" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-402/source-messagelogprojection-combat-lines-from-the-combatevent-contract" />, combat lines come from CombatEvent) as stable plain text: sim time, category, subject id, message.
* Two replays of the same (scenario, seed) produce byte-identical exports, checked by a golden test.
* The UI toggles between the categorized and raw views and has an export action that writes to a user path. Export is read-only and never mutates sim state.
* The export works under AttachReplayViewer.

Source: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

linear.title: DRG-231 follow-up: [SYM-MIL] preserve naval type icon + MIL SIDC through map/Cesium symbology projection; immutable SymbolKeyRegistry.All
linear.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review findings on [PR #694](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/694>) (S126 MIL-only symbology subset — canonical keys, profile switch, disclaimer; <issue id="a657c027-6658-4623-97d1-eba4b527acb2" label="DRG-231" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-231/sym-mil-01-military-tactical-symbology-ntds-app-6-mil-std-2525" /> SYM-MIL-01).

## Findings

1. `SymbologyProjection.cs:63` **— combatant vs unknown look identical in projected map rows.** The naval type icon is not preserved when rows are projected, so a classified combatant and an unknown contact render the same glyph.
2. **Cesium path re-parses MIL SIDC into the legacy ground glyph.** `CesiumBillboardProjection` takes the military SIDC produced by the MIL profile and re-parses it into the legacy ground glyph, losing domain/type on the globe.
3. `SymbolKeyRegistry.All` **exposes a castable array.** Callers can cast the exposed collection back to an array and mutate the registry. Expose `Array.AsReadOnly(...)` / an immutable collection instead.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #694)

`SymbologyProjection.Apply` has no non-test caller yet, so none of these affect a shipped surface today. **Must be done before the map consumes the MIL profile.**

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* Projected map rows preserve the naval/domain type icon; a combatant and an unknown contact of the same platform type produce distinguishable symbols (test covers both).
* `CesiumBillboardProjection` consumes the MIL SIDC / canonical key directly (no re-parse into the legacy ground glyph); test proves a naval MIL SIDC stays naval on the Cesium path.
* `SymbolKeyRegistry.All` returns a read-only/immutable collection; a test proves it cannot be cast to a mutable array and mutated.
* Observer-safe unknown fallback (MIL-AC) unchanged; ReplayGolden / Baltic v2 hashes untouched; projection stays presentation-only.

linear.title: CombatVfxProjection runs every tick but its frame is never rendered (dead path)
linear.description:
## Problem

`DelegationBridgeHost` calls `CombatVfxProjection.Project(DecisionLog, LastMapSymbols, SimTime)` on every tick and stores the result in `LastCombatVfx`. Nothing renders that frame. The work costs time on every tick, and it is also another decision-log combat-fact path outside the `CombatEvent` contract.

## Evidence

* `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/DelegationBridgeHost.cs` \~L666: `LastCombatVfx = CombatVfxProjection.Project(...)`.
* The only runtime reader is `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/MapPlaceholderPanelHost.cs` (\~L489/L507). It uses `LastCombatVfx` only as a dirty-check reference. `ApplyTransientCombatVfx()` (\~L357) draws through `_combatView.Bind(DisplayCombatFrame, …)`, not the VFX frame.
* `MapCanvasTransientEffectsRenderer.Sync(CombatVfxFrame)` exists, but GitHub code search finds no runtime code that creates it or calls it. Only its contract tests use it.
* Neither PR [drgaciw/cmano-clone#696](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featcombat-drg-165-combat-event-contract-consumes-slice-a-04ba3acac253>) (<issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" />) nor PR [drgaciw/cmano-clone#700](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-card-drg-353354355-contact-card-hardening-drg-322-attack-283b8d44d493>) touched these files.

## Acceptance criteria

* Make a decision: either remove `CombatVfxProjection` and `MapCanvasTransientEffectsRenderer` from the tick path, or wire them in properly, sourced from `CombatEventSnapshot`.
* If removed: the dirty check in `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` keys off the combat frame it actually renders. Dead tests and docs (`docs/engineering/combat-vfx-projection.md`) are updated.
* No per-tick projection runs without a consumer.
* Replay goldens and PlayMode smoke stay green.

Source: Project Aegis room 2026-10-07 (SliceB/SliceC/Hygiene)

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

**Surface (CMANO 2026-10-14, main 254d2c96):** `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/DelegationBridgeHost.cs` (only `LastCombatVfx` property L92 and the `CombatVfxProjection.Project` call \~L666), `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/MapPlaceholderPanelHost.cs` (only the `LastCombatVfx` dirty-check refs \~L586/L604), `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/CombatVfxProjection.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/CombatVfxProjectionTests.cs`, `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/MapCanvasTransientEffectsRenderer.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Map/MapCanvasTransientEffectsRendererContractTests.cs`, `docs/engineering/combat-vfx-projection.md`.

linear.title: Show doctrine/ROE/WRA inheritance source and effective value per unit, with reset-to-inherited
linear.description:
## Problem

Authority and ROE state is projected (<issue id="09fd8608-86ec-4243-888d-7dd0f126a8d2" label="DRG-182" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-182/project-command-authority-and-rules-of-engagement-state" />, <issue id="62f19a5c-38c2-44cb-ad50-c2e2ba23b291" label="DRG-209" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-209/slice-a-headless-authority-and-roe-projection" />), and WRA salvo-remaining shows on weapon chrome (<issue id="b052e2f4-59ae-43a4-850f-ae28460de62f" label="DRG-259" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-259/c2-02-wra-salvo-remaining-on-weapon-chrome" />). But the player cannot see *where* a unit's effective doctrine, ROE, or WRA value comes from (side, mission, group, or unit override), or reset an override back to inherited. In CMO this inheritance view is the main way a player finds out why a unit held fire or fired unexpectedly.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3.3.12: every doctrine option has an "inherited" setting. A unit follows its side's doctrine, or its mission's doctrine if assigned to one, and buttons reset it to the inherited default. Doctrine, EMCON, and WRA are separate tabs. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>)
* CMO manual §6.3.8: side doctrine/ROE/WRA is set at the top level and "flows down to mission and then groups/units". The WRA tab lists every weapon the side uses. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="9cb22a1c-4d7a-499d-ba6d-44462898cedd" label="DRG-321" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-321/jev-vs3-roe-noul-facade-accept-coordinationcommandbridge" /> (ROE Noul + façade Accept) is about AI-assisted ROE suggestions, not showing inheritance. No issue covers per-level provenance or reset.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `DoctrineInheritanceProjection` gives, for each selected unit and each doctrine/ROE/WRA field: the effective value, the source level (Side/Mission/Group/Unit), and the overridden parent value if there is one.
* Reset-to-inherited is sent as a command through the command façade and recorded in the order log. It is never a UI-side state mutation.
* The unit panel shows an override marker and a source badge for each field, and the WRA rows show target-type × quantity × range using the existing <issue id="b052e2f4-59ae-43a4-850f-ae28460de62f" label="DRG-259" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-259/c2-02-wra-salvo-remaining-on-weapon-chrome" /> chrome.
* The engagement explanation (<issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />) can cite the doctrine source level when doctrine is the refusal reason.
* Tests cover inherited, mission-overridden, and unit-overridden fields, and the reset round-trip under replay.

Source: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

* **Links:** authority/ROE projections [DRG-182](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-182>), [DRG-209](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-209>); WRA chrome [DRG-259](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-259>); explanation [DRG-168](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168>) (C2 guide in <pull-request id="b80cd6c2-4f2a-4e86-b255-054abcbe5ec6" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#759" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/docsc2-reconcile-both-documentation-stacks-and-canonical-guides-e1c12e5af761" />); not a duplicate of [DRG-321](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-321>). linear.title: Manual autonomy is non-functional — GateResult.QueueForApproval has no product consumer
linear.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28. Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD.

## The contradiction

Req 04 defines autonomy level **Manual** as:

> **Manual** — Agent suggests actions only; player must approve (`HUMAN_IN_LOOP`)

There is no approval path. The suggestion is computed, logged, and discarded.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | The gate models an approval outcome | `Orchestration/AutonomyGate.cs:7` — `GateResult(bool ExecuteNow, bool QueueForApproval, bool Rejected, FireAbortReason PolicyDenialReason)` |
| 2 | Manual autonomy sets it | `AutonomyGate.cs:29` — `AutonomyLevel.Manual => new GateResult(playerApproved, !playerApproved, false)` |
| 3 | The caller hardcodes no approval | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:141` — `gate.Evaluate(Autonomy, order, playerApproved: false)` |
| 4 | Only two branches are handled | `AgentController.cs:142-158` — `if (gateResult.Rejected && ...)` logs a denial; `if (gateResult.ExecuteNow)` issues. `QueueForApproval` **is never read** |
| 5 | Nothing else consumes it | Repo-wide grep for `QueueForApproval` outside its declaration returns only `AutonomyGateTests.cs` (3 assertions) |

## Effect

At **Manual** autonomy — and at **Assisted** with a high-risk order — the agent runs its full decision pipeline, appends a `DecisionRecord` (chosen action, candidate set, rationale, attention load/budget, RNG draw), and the resulting order is then **silently dropped**. The player is never asked. The unit does nothing.

The decision *record* survives in the order log, so a replay shows the agent deciding and no order following — which reads as an engine bug rather than a missing feature.

## Why it matters beyond the one level

`HUMAN_IN_LOOP` is the autonomy tier that makes lethal delegation defensible (req 13: full-auto lethal engagement requires explicit opt-in per mission phase). The tier below full-auto currently does nothing at all.

## To close

- [ ] Retain approval-gated orders as durable pending items bound to unit + agent + originating `DecisionRecord` (req 04 **AGD-07**)
- [ ] Approve/reject path, both logged, so an AAR distinguishes *proposed and refused* from *never proposed* (**AGD-08**)
- [ ] Tick-based expiry, identical at 1× and 60× compression — must not vary with frame rate, to preserve replay determinism (**AGD-09**)
- [ ] Surface the backlog with alert priority (**AGD-10**, doc 20 **ALR-01**)
- [ ] Determinism: `ReplayGolden` held; Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged or golden-updated with an ADR

## Related

Requirements written up in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-07 – AGD-10, acceptance criteria 1–2). The UI half depends on the command result channel tracked separately in doc 20 **CMD-16**.

linear.title: Multi-target manual weapon allocation plan with per-weapon can-fire reasons
linear.description:
## Problem

The attack-options menu (<issue id="edefdae9-4a5b-49dc-ba94-cc0d4a461203" label="DRG-262" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262/c2-05-attack-options-menu-preview-parity" />) previews one shooter against one target. There is no way to build a manual allocation plan across several selected targets and shooters: N weapons per target, with a per-weapon "OK, can fire" or a specific reason it can't. CMO's manual allocation dialog (Shift+F1) is the main player tool for coordinated strikes and for learning weapon limits.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3 (Engage Target(s) Manual): drag-select multiple targets, pick an attacker, and see suitable weapons grouped by type. Legal weapons that are outside firing parameters show the reason in red; valid ones show "OK - Can fire". You allocate a quantity per target, and allocations show both per attacker and per target. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>) and [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-3-shortcut-buttons-and-windows/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-3-shortcut-buttons-and-windows/>)
* CMO combat chapter: manual assignment is "a very effective method of getting good feedback on weaponry limitations", because the crew runs an exhaustive checklist of conditions. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="edefdae9-4a5b-49dc-ba94-cc0d4a461203" label="DRG-262" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262/c2-05-attack-options-menu-preview-parity" /> is single-target preview parity, <issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" /> covers abort codes in the engage explanation, <issue id="0f26c476-2643-4cb9-b689-d068770f58bd" label="DRG-172" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-172/add-threat-assessment-and-weapon-recommendation" /> covers recommendations, and <issue id="8d85d519-5cec-4c0a-a35a-63206eb9d6cc" label="DRG-224" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224/slice-b-headless-magazine-and-salvo-employment-ledger" /> is the employment ledger. None covers a multi-target allocation plan.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `AllocationPlanProjection` takes {shooters\[\], targets\[\], allocations\[\]} and returns, for each (shooter, weapon, target): Can-fire, or a domain `FireAbortReason` code reused from <issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />. It also returns per-target and per-shooter totals and the remaining magazine count from the <issue id="8d85d519-5cec-4c0a-a35a-63206eb9d6cc" label="DRG-224" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224/slice-b-headless-magazine-and-salvo-employment-ledger" /> ledger.
* Committing a plan sends ordinary engage commands through the command façade. The projection itself never fires and does not touch the DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath.
* The UI lists allocations by attacker and by target. Reasons use the same text source as <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />/<issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />.
* Over-allocation beyond the magazine is rejected with a reason before commit.
* Tests cover a 2×3 plan, a mixed can-fire/abort result, an over-allocation reject, and replay determinism of the committed orders.

Source: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

linear.title: Explain target-location ambiguity vs weapon tolerance (area-of-uncertainty) in engage explanation
linear.description:
## Problem

The engagement explanation (<issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />) and contact provenance (<issue id="fc4092be-a4ee-4268-8ecb-27f647c14bf2" label="DRG-180" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-180/surface-contact-provenance-confidence-freshness-and-comms-state" />) show contact confidence, but not *positional* ambiguity relative to what a given weapon can tolerate. In CMO a frequent cause of "why won't it fire?" is that the contact's area of uncertainty is larger than the weapon's downrange or cross-range tolerance, scaled by an ambiguity doctrine (Ignore / Optimistic / Pessimistic). Players need to see that on the map and in the refusal text.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual: an ambiguous contact is one with an uncertainty area. With doctrine set to "Optimistic", the uncertainty must be under 3× the weapon tolerance before launch; with "Pessimistic", under 1×. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>)
* CMO combat chapter: the refusal reads "target's downrange ambiguity (X nm) is larger than … the weapon's acceptable limit (Y nm)", e.g. a ±10 nm contact against a 2 nm weapon limit. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="421c7902-2fda-47b4-8329-0603014f8fd7" label="DRG-385" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-385/asw-05-passive-bearing-only-tracking" /> (passive bearing-only tracking) adds uncertainty on the sim side. No presentation issue compares uncertainty with weapon tolerance.

## Acceptance criteria

* The headless explanation DTO adds, for each (weapon, contact): downrange and cross-range ambiguity, the weapon tolerance, the active ambiguity doctrine level, and pass/fail. All of it is read from existing contact and weapon data, with no new sim truth.
* The refusal text uses the CMO-style numbers ("ambiguity X nm > limit Y nm"), and the wording shares one source with <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />/<issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />.
* The map draws the contact's area-of-uncertainty ellipse from the projection, and hiding it is a declutter option (<issue id="c8b79a30-0b7e-4f3f-a4b0-0b22320a67b1" label="DRG-176" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176/set-combat-picture-performance-and-declutter-budgets" /> budget).
* Tests cover a contact inside tolerance, inside 3× (Optimistic passes, Pessimistic fails), and outside, all with replay-stable output.

Source: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

* **Links:** explanation [DRG-168](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168>), provenance [DRG-180](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-180>), abort wording [DRG-265](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265>), passive tracking [DRG-385](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-385>), declutter [DRG-176](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176>).
* **Dependencies:** the ellipse declutter toggle references the <issue id="c8b79a30-0b7e-4f3f-a4b0-0b22320a67b1" label="DRG-176" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176/set-combat-picture-performance-and-declutter-budgets" /> budget, which is not yet defined; the headless DTO and refusal text do not depend on it.
* **Fences (from rubric H3/H5):** headless projection first; source-fence test (no UnityEngine/MonoBehaviour/ApplyOrder/DecisionLog write/SimulationSession/DelegationBridge refs); replay hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged, no ReplayGolden re-bless; any visible UI change gets a named [DRG-208](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208>) Play Mode walk item (human gate).

## Approved recommendation follow-through — 2026-10-30

User instruction: “proceed with your recommendations” following the game-mechanics/UX review. [Delivery plan](<https://app.notion.com/p/409f7cb4e4df815bbccfe465326584cc?pvs=204>). Baseline main 570a7f843ebffaa0ec9f2a3d9a7871d0354adc51. Product direction is authorized; no runtime delivery, passing tests, current-head owner acceptance, or protected-method waiver is asserted.

Source-contract prerequisite discovered during follow-through: ContactProvenanceState at main 570a7f84 has identification confidence, freshness/age and comms flags, but no downrange/cross-range ambiguity or weapon tolerance. This establishes a gap in that DTO, not proof that no other domain provider exists.

Before numeric UI work:

* Identify authoritative producer fields, units, unknown representation and observation time for both contact uncertainty and weapon tolerance.
* If absent, scope a Sim-owned capability/provider dependency; never manufacture values in presentation.
* Reconcile ambiguity doctrine/multipliers with Aegis's actual resolver. Reference-product 1x/3x examples are not an implemented Aegis contract.
* Missing dimensions remain Unknown; no ellipse from identity confidence.
* Keep shooter/weapon/contact/time correlation; historical refusal must not borrow future facts.
* The ellipse still depends on <issue id="c8b79a30-0b7e-4f3f-a4b0-0b22320a67b1" label="DRG-176" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176/set-combat-picture-performance-and-declutter-budgets" /> declutter budgets.

linear.title: Manual autonomy is non-functional — GateResult.QueueForApproval has no product consumer
linear.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28. Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD.

## The contradiction

Req 04 defines autonomy level **Manual** as:

> **Manual** — Agent suggests actions only; player must approve (`HUMAN_IN_LOOP`)

There is no approval path. The suggestion is computed, logged, and discarded.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | The gate models an approval outcome | `Orchestration/AutonomyGate.cs:7` — `GateResult(bool ExecuteNow, bool QueueForApproval, bool Rejected, FireAbortReason PolicyDenialReason)` |
| 2 | Manual autonomy sets it | `AutonomyGate.cs:29` — `AutonomyLevel.Manual => new GateResult(playerApproved, !playerApproved, false)` |
| 3 | The caller hardcodes no approval | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:141` — `gate.Evaluate(Autonomy, order, playerApproved: false)` |
| 4 | Only two branches are handled | `AgentController.cs:142-158` — `if (gateResult.Rejected && ...)` logs a denial; `if (gateResult.ExecuteNow)` issues. `QueueForApproval` **is never read** |
| 5 | Nothing else consumes it | Repo-wide grep for `QueueForApproval` outside its declaration returns only `AutonomyGateTests.cs` (3 assertions) |

## Effect

At **Manual** autonomy — and at **Assisted** with a high-risk order — the agent runs its full decision pipeline, appends a `DecisionRecord` (chosen action, candidate set, rationale, attention load/budget, RNG draw), and the resulting order is then **silently dropped**. The player is never asked. The unit does nothing.

The decision *record* survives in the order log, so a replay shows the agent deciding and no order following — which reads as an engine bug rather than a missing feature.

## Why it matters beyond the one level

`HUMAN_IN_LOOP` is the autonomy tier that makes lethal delegation defensible (req 13: full-auto lethal engagement requires explicit opt-in per mission phase). The tier below full-auto currently does nothing at all.

## To close

- [ ] Retain approval-gated orders as durable pending items bound to unit + agent + originating `DecisionRecord` (req 04 **AGD-07**)
- [ ] Approve/reject path, both logged, so an AAR distinguishes *proposed and refused* from *never proposed* (**AGD-08**)
- [ ] Tick-based expiry, identical at 1× and 60× compression — must not vary with frame rate, to preserve replay determinism (**AGD-09**)
- [ ] Surface the backlog with alert priority (**AGD-10**, doc 20 **ALR-01**)
- [ ] Determinism: `ReplayGolden` held; Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged or golden-updated with an ADR

## Related

Requirements written up in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-07 – AGD-10, acceptance criteria 1–2). The UI half depends on the command result channel tracked separately in doc 20 **CMD-16**.

notion.title: 🎛️ Main Game Window — Proposed C2 UI Requirements (CMD-16…CMD-28)
notion.note:
[🎛️ Main Game Window — Proposed C2 UI Requirements (CMD-16…CMD-28)] — Status: Draft | Status: Draft — for owner triage — Source: 20-Command-And-Control-UI.md — Matched: | CMD-16 | Persistent unit-order toolbar | P1 | Only context menus are specified | ; ## CMD-16 — Persistent unit-order toolbar \[P1\] --- Type: Requirements proposal — amendments to REQ-20, not a replacement Status: Draft — for owner triage Date: 2026-07-26 Canonical home: Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md — if accepted, these land there, not here Method: Reference-product analysis (CMO v1.01 build 1121.8 main window) diffed against existing Aegis specs Related Linear Milestone: H1 — C2 Runtime Depth ## Read this first — what this is not The main game window is already specified, and specified well. Before proposing anything I read: - Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md — 202 lines, CMD-01…CMD-15, layout zones, NFRs, acceptance criteria, phased delivery, and an honest per-row status column - design/ux/c2-command-post.md — 175-line UX spec with wireframe, zone sizes, state table, interaction map, data sources - design/gdd/command-and-control-ui.md, docs/architecture/adr-007-c2-map-presentation.md REQ-20 is explicitly derived from the CMO manual (Ch 3–4, §6.2–7, §6.9, §1.3, §10.1) — the same product this analysis looks at. So a fresh "UX/UI requirements" page would duplicate it and create a competing source of truth, which the wiki's own rule forbids. What follows is only the delta: things visible in the reference product that neither REQ-20 nor the UX spec currently requires. Eight proposals, numbered to continue REQ-20's scheme. ## Already covered — do not re-file these So the next reader doesn't repeat the analysis: REQ-20 already requires persistent layout zones (CMD-01), UI Toolkit stack (CMD-02), headless command-driven binding (CMD-03), top bar with time/compression/pause (CMD-04), message log with sequence deep-link (CMD-05), map symbol picture (CMD-06), map↔OOB↔panel selection sync (CMD-07), doctrine inheritance panel (CMD-08), delegation badges (CMD-09), context menus (CMD-10), intent preview / FireAbort explain (CMD-11), colorblind-safe affiliation and keyboard focus (CMD-12), and defers the product globe, multitasker, and 5k@60 to Phase N (CMD-13–15). --- # Proposed requirements | ID | Requirement | Priority | Why it is missing today | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CMD-17 | Unknown-due-to-comms as a first-class display state | P0 | Sim models it; UI has no representation | | CMD-19 | Per-axis manual / auto delegation control | P0 | Delegation specified at unit granularity only | | CMD-20 | Map scale bar + camera altitude readout | P0 | Not mentioned in any spec | | CMD-21 | Selected-unit sensor / weapon envelope rings | P0 | At risk of deferring with Phase N EW overlays | | CMD-18 | Domain-appropriate discrete alt / depth / throttle presets | P1 | Alt/speed specified as data, not as commands | | CMD-16 | Persistent unit-order toolbar | P1 | Only context menus are specified | | CMD-22 | Zulu / local / remaining scenario time | P1 | "Time" specified without disambiguation | | CMD-23 | Collapsible non-primary zones | P2 | Zones specified as fixed-height and always present | --- ## CMD-17 — Unknown-due-to-comms is a first-class display state \[P0\] Requirement. Where a unit's telemetry is unavailable because the unit is out of comms, the UI shall render an explicit unknown state that names the cause, visually distinct from zero, blank, and last-known-value. Reference evidence. The unit panel shows Course: XXX, Speed: XXX, Altitude: XXX, and Status: UNKNOWN (Out of comms). The submarine is selected and on the map — the player simply cannot talk to it. Why this is the most important item here. Aegis already models comms degradation (docs/engineering/comms-degradation-runtime.md, requirements doc 19), and REQ-20 mentions a COMMS legend — but nothing specifies how a panel renders data it cannot obtain. A blank field reads as "no data / UI bug." XXX (Out of comms) reads as "the link is down" — which is a tactical fact the player must act on. Getting this wrong silently converts a modelled game system into an apparent defect. Must also settle: whether last-known values are shown with an age stamp ("Course 270 · 4m stale") or suppressed entirely. These are different games — the first supports dead reckoning, the second forces reacquisition. ## CMD-19 — Per-axis manual / auto delegation \[P0\] Requirement. Each independently commandable axis (depth/altitude, throttle, EMCON, sensors) shall expose its own manual-versus-automatic control, and its current mode shall be readable without opening a menu. Reference evidence. The unit panel carries a separate Manual | Set Auto pair for Alt and for Throttle — two axes, two independent autonomy switches. Why it matters for Aegis specifically. REQ-20's CMD-09 models delegation at unit granularity — a badge reading human, agent, or mixed. But "mixed" is exactly the interesting case and the badge cannot express it: a unit may be under agent speed control while the human holds depth, or running autonomous EMCON under manual maneuvering. Agent delegation is this project's stated differentiator, and the control surface for it is currently coarser than the reference product's. This likely also implies a projection change — per-axis autonomy state has to reach the panel. ## CMD-20 — Map scale and camera altitude \[P0\] Requirement. The map shall persistently display a distance scale in nautical miles and the current camera altitude. Reference evidence. A nautical-mile scale bar sits bottom-right; Camera Alt: 867550m sits in the status line. Why. Range is the primary spatial judgement in this genre — every engagement decision is "can I reach it, can it reach me." A theater map without a scale cannot support that read. Neither REQ-20 nor the UX spec mentions a scale indicator; this looks like a simple omission rather than a decision, which is why it is worth filing explicitly. ## CMD-21 — Selected-unit envelope rings \[P0\] Requirement. On selection, the map shall render the unit's sensor and weapon envelopes as visually distinguishable range rings. Reference evidence. The selected submarine carries several concentric rings in distinct colours — detection and engagement envelopes read at a glance. Why file it separately. REQ-20 defers "full EW overlay product layers" to Phase N. Own-unit envelope rings are not an EW overlay — they are the baseline read that makes a selection meaningful. The risk is that the baseline gets deferred along with the advanced feature because both are described as "overlays." This requirement exists to prevent that bundling. ## CMD-18 — Domain-appropriate discrete presets \[P1\] Requirement. Altitude/depth and throttle shall be commandable as named doctrinal states appropriate to the platform's domain, not solely as numeric entry. Reference evidence. The submarine panel offers depth as Surface · Periscope depth · Shallow · Just over the layer · Just under the layer · As deep as possible, and throttle as Stop · Creep · Cruise · Full · Flank. Why. "Just under the layer" is not a depth — it is a thermocline-relative acoustic decision whose numeric value changes with water conditions. The named command carries tactical intent that a number cannot, and it is the correct unit of delegation to an agent. Likewise Creep is a quieting decision, not a speed. REQ-20 lists "alt/speed" as panel data; this proposes it as a command vocabulary. Open: preset sets differ per domain (subsurface / air / surface / ground) and need a catalog source rather than hardcoding. ## CMD-16 — Persistent unit-order toolbar \[P1\] Requirement. The main window shall present a persistent toolbar exposing primary unit-order actions for the current selection, in addition to context menus. Reference evidence. Twelve always-visible order groups: Auto/Manual Engage Target, Plot Course, Throttle & Altitude, Formation Editor, Magazines, Aircraft Operations, Boat Operations, Mounts & Weapons, Sensors, Systems & Damage, Unit/Group Doctrine, Mission Editor. Why. REQ-20's CMD-10 specifies context menus, and neither its zone table nor the UX spec's wireframe includes a toolbar. Context-menu-only means every one of a dozen order verbs is discoverable exclusively by right-clicking the correct object — a heavy discovery burden for new players and a lot of hidden surface for a command post. The reference product provides both paths deliberately. Caveat, from this session's reviews: a flat wall of twelve buttons is itself a legibility problem. Adopt the redundancy, not the layout — group by domain and reflect selection context. ## CMD-22 — Zulu, local, and remaining time \[P1\] Requirement. The top bar shall display scenario date, Zulu time, local time, and remaining scenario duration. Reference evidence. Time: Monday, October 9, 2000 · Zulu: 11:00:00 · Local: 14:00:00 · 1 d to go. Why. REQ-20's CMD-04 specifies "time" without disambiguation, and the UX spec wireframes a single TIME 00:42:10. Zulu-versus-local is doctrinal in coalition operations and drives day/night reasoning; remaining-duration frames session pacing. Cheap to add, awkward to retrofit once the top bar is dense. Also observed: the reference offers time compression as time-per-step (15 sec / 1 min / 5 min / 15 min) alongside a multiplier. Aegis specifies multipliers only (1x 4x 8x, hotkeys 1–4). Those are different mental models — worth a deliberate choice rather than an inherited one. ## CMD-23 — Collapsible non-primary zones \[P2\] Requirement. Message log and left drawer shall be collapsible to a title affordance, with state persisted across sessions. Reference evidence. The message log is collapsed to a title bar with an expand control, returning its area to the map. Why. The UX spec fixes the bottom log at 120px and REQ-20 treats zones as always-present. Over multi-hour sessions the map is the scarce resource, and the log matters intensely but intermittently. --- ## CMD-24 — Air Operations window \[P1, phased\] Requirement.
