notion.title: 🎛️ Main Game Window — Proposed C2 UI Requirements (CMD-16…CMD-28)
notion.note:
[🎛️ Main Game Window — Proposed C2 UI Requirements (CMD-16…CMD-28)] — Status: Draft | Status: Draft — for owner triage — Source: 20-Command-And-Control-UI.md — Matched: ## CMD-24 — Air Operations window \[P1, phased\] ; - CMD-24.1 — Cross-host aggregation. List air assets across all units in the current selection, grouped by type and host with counts (12x F/ --- Type: Requirements proposal — amendments to REQ-20, not a replacement Status: Draft — for owner triage Date: 2026-07-26 Canonical home: Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md — if accepted, these land there, not here Method: Reference-product analysis (CMO v1.01 build 1121.8 main window) diffed against existing Aegis specs Related Linear Milestone: H1 — C2 Runtime Depth ## Read this first — what this is not The main game window is already specified, and specified well. Before proposing anything I read: - Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md — 202 lines, CMD-01…CMD-15, layout zones, NFRs, acceptance criteria, phased delivery, and an honest per-row status column - design/ux/c2-command-post.md — 175-line UX spec with wireframe, zone sizes, state table, interaction map, data sources - design/gdd/command-and-control-ui.md, docs/architecture/adr-007-c2-map-presentation.md REQ-20 is explicitly derived from the CMO manual (Ch 3–4, §6.2–7, §6.9, §1.3, §10.1) — the same product this analysis looks at. So a fresh "UX/UI requirements" page would duplicate it and create a competing source of truth, which the wiki's own rule forbids. What follows is only the delta: things visible in the reference product that neither REQ-20 nor the UX spec currently requires. Eight proposals, numbered to continue REQ-20's scheme. ## Already covered — do not re-file these So the next reader doesn't repeat the analysis: REQ-20 already requires persistent layout zones (CMD-01), UI Toolkit stack (CMD-02), headless command-driven binding (CMD-03), top bar with time/compression/pause (CMD-04), message log with sequence deep-link (CMD-05), map symbol picture (CMD-06), map↔OOB↔panel selection sync (CMD-07), doctrine inheritance panel (CMD-08), delegation badges (CMD-09), context menus (CMD-10), intent preview / FireAbort explain (CMD-11), colorblind-safe affiliation and keyboard focus (CMD-12), and defers the product globe, multitasker, and 5k@60 to Phase N (CMD-13–15). --- # Proposed requirements | ID | Requirement | Priority | Why it is missing today | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CMD-17 | Unknown-due-to-comms as a first-class display state | P0 | Sim models it; UI has no representation | | CMD-19 | Per-axis manual / auto delegation control | P0 | Delegation specified at unit granularity only | | CMD-20 | Map scale bar + camera altitude readout | P0 | Not mentioned in any spec | | CMD-21 | Selected-unit sensor / weapon envelope rings | P0 | At risk of deferring with Phase N EW overlays | | CMD-18 | Domain-appropriate discrete alt / depth / throttle presets | P1 | Alt/speed specified as data, not as commands | | CMD-16 | Persistent unit-order toolbar | P1 | Only context menus are specified | | CMD-22 | Zulu / local / remaining scenario time | P1 | "Time" specified without disambiguation | | CMD-23 | Collapsible non-primary zones | P2 | Zones specified as fixed-height and always present | --- ## CMD-17 — Unknown-due-to-comms is a first-class display state \[P0\] Requirement. Where a unit's telemetry is unavailable because the unit is out of comms, the UI shall render an explicit unknown state that names the cause, visually distinct from zero, blank, and last-known-value. Reference evidence. The unit panel shows Course: XXX, Speed: XXX, Altitude: XXX, and Status: UNKNOWN (Out of comms). The submarine is selected and on the map — the player simply cannot talk to it. Why this is the most important item here. Aegis already models comms degradation (docs/engineering/comms-degradation-runtime.md, requirements doc 19), and REQ-20 mentions a COMMS legend — but nothing specifies how a panel renders data it cannot obtain. A blank field reads as "no data / UI bug." XXX (Out of comms) reads as "the link is down" — which is a tactical fact the player must act on. Getting this wrong silently converts a modelled game system into an apparent defect. Must also settle: whether last-known values are shown with an age stamp ("Course 270 · 4m stale") or suppressed entirely. These are different games — the first supports dead reckoning, the second forces reacquisition. ## CMD-19 — Per-axis manual / auto delegation \[P0\] Requirement. Each independently commandable axis (depth/altitude, throttle, EMCON, sensors) shall expose its own manual-versus-automatic control, and its current mode shall be readable without opening a menu. Reference evidence. The unit panel carries a separate Manual | Set Auto pair for Alt and for Throttle — two axes, two independent autonomy switches. Why it matters for Aegis specifically. REQ-20's CMD-09 models delegation at unit granularity — a badge reading human, agent, or mixed. But "mixed" is exactly the interesting case and the badge cannot express it: a unit may be under agent speed control while the human holds depth, or running autonomous EMCON under manual maneuvering. Agent delegation is this project's stated differentiator, and the control surface for it is currently coarser than the reference product's. This likely also implies a projection change — per-axis autonomy state has to reach the panel. ## CMD-20 — Map scale and camera altitude \[P0\] Requirement. The map shall persistently display a distance scale in nautical miles and the current camera altitude. Reference evidence. A nautical-mile scale bar sits bottom-right; Camera Alt: 867550m sits in the status line. Why. Range is the primary spatial judgement in this genre — every engagement decision is "can I reach it, can it reach me." A theater map without a scale cannot support that read. Neither REQ-20 nor the UX spec mentions a scale indicator; this looks like a simple omission rather than a decision, which is why it is worth filing explicitly. ## CMD-21 — Selected-unit envelope rings \[P0\] Requirement. On selection, the map shall render the unit's sensor and weapon envelopes as visually distinguishable range rings. Reference evidence. The selected submarine carries several concentric rings in distinct colours — detection and engagement envelopes read at a glance. Why file it separately. REQ-20 defers "full EW overlay product layers" to Phase N. Own-unit envelope rings are not an EW overlay — they are the baseline read that makes a selection meaningful. The risk is that the baseline gets deferred along with the advanced feature because both are described as "overlays." This requirement exists to prevent that bundling. ## CMD-18 — Domain-appropriate discrete presets \[P1\] Requirement. Altitude/depth and throttle shall be commandable as named doctrinal states appropriate to the platform's domain, not solely as numeric entry. Reference evidence. The submarine panel offers depth as Surface · Periscope depth · Shallow · Just over the layer · Just under the layer · As deep as possible, and throttle as Stop · Creep · Cruise · Full · Flank. Why. "Just under the layer" is not a depth — it is a thermocline-relative acoustic decision whose numeric value changes with water conditions. The named command carries tactical intent that a number cannot, and it is the correct unit of delegation to an agent. Likewise Creep is a quieting decision, not a speed. REQ-20 lists "alt/speed" as panel data; this proposes it as a command vocabulary. Open: preset sets differ per domain (subsurface / air / surface / ground) and need a catalog source rather than hardcoding. ## CMD-16 — Persistent unit-order toolbar \[P1\] Requirement. The main window shall present a persistent toolbar exposing primary unit-order actions for the current selection, in addition to context menus. Reference evidence. Twelve always-visible order groups: Auto/Manual Engage Target, Plot Course, Throttle & Altitude, Formation Editor, Magazines, Aircraft Operations, Boat Operations, Mounts & Weapons, Sensors, Systems & Damage, Unit/Group Doctrine, Mission Editor. Why. REQ-20's CMD-10 specifies context menus, and neither its zone table nor the UX spec's wireframe includes a toolbar. Context-menu-only means every one of a dozen order verbs is discoverable exclusively by right-clicking the correct object — a heavy discovery burden for new players and a lot of hidden surface for a command post. The reference product provides both paths deliberately. Caveat, from this session's reviews: a flat wall of twelve buttons is itself a legibility problem. Adopt the redundancy, not the layout — group by domain and reflect selection context. ## CMD-22 — Zulu, local, and remaining time \[P1\] Requirement. The top bar shall display scenario date, Zulu time, local time, and remaining scenario duration. Reference evidence. Time: Monday, October 9, 2000 · Zulu: 11:00:00 · Local: 14:00:00 · 1 d to go. Why. REQ-20's CMD-04 specifies "time" without disambiguation, and the UX spec wireframes a single TIME 00:42:10. Zulu-versus-local is doctrinal in coalition operations and drives day/night reasoning; remaining-duration frames session pacing. Cheap to add, awkward to retrofit once the top bar is dense. Also observed: the reference offers time compression as time-per-step (15 sec / 1 min / 5 min / 15 min) alongside a multiplier. Aegis specifies multipliers only (1x 4x 8x, hotkeys 1–4). Those are different mental models — worth a deliberate choice rather than an inherited one. ## CMD-23 — Collapsible non-primary zones \[P2\] Requirement. Message log and left drawer shall be collapsible to a title affordance, with state persisted across sessions. Reference evidence. The message log is collapsed to a title bar with an expand control, returning its area to the map. Why. The UX spec fixes the bottom log at 120px and REQ-20 treats zones as always-present. Over multi-hour sessions the map is the scarce resource, and the log matters intensely but intermittently. --- ## CMD-24 — Air Operations window \[P1, phased\] Requirement. The C2 client shall provide an Air Operations window, opened from the unit-order toolbar (CMD-16), presenting the air assets hosted across the current selection, their readiness, loadout feasibility, and mission-assignment actions. Reference evidence. A modal titled "Air Ops — Multiple host units" with tabs Aircraft Status / Air Facilities; a table of Aircraft · Status · Mission · Loadout · Time to ready · Quick; a stores panel showing magazine availability; and an action bar of Launch Individually · Launch as group(s) · Ready/Arm · Abort Launch · Doctrine · Assign to mission · Unload Cargo. Why it is missing. REQ-20 has zero mentions of aircraft, launch, sortie, hangar or deck. The CMO toolbar surfaces Aircraft Operations and Boat Operations as first-class order groups; REQ-20's parity table has no row for either. ### ⚠️ This requirement is gated by REQ-16, and must be phased accordingly This is the crux. Game-Requirements/requirements/16-Logistics-And-Magazines.md is unusually honest about what exists: > "Not shipped: full air-ops FSM, UNREP, live magazines C2 panel, product MCP logistics tools." > > "Air-ops FSM (taxi/takeoff/land/maint) — Phase N — Boolean readiness only on main." | Model | REQ-16 status | Can the UI show it? | | --- | --- | --- | | Magazine ledger consume (MagazineLedger) | Shipped | Yes | | Fuel burn / bands, per-domain fuel types (aviation JP) | Shipped / P0 | Yes | | Boolean ReadyForLaunch → AIR_NOT_READY (UnitReadinessMap) | Shipped | Yes — binary only | | Ferry missions moving aircraft between bases | Shipped (CLI + validation) | Yes | | Air-ops FSM — taxi / takeoff / land / maintenance | Phase N | No | | Deck cycle, sortie generation rate | Phase N | No | | Composite readinessScore | Phase N | No — boolean only | | UNREP / underway rearm | Phase N | No | A "Time to ready" column cannot be populated, because no state machine produces a time. Rendering it empty, or with a fabricated value, repeats the exact failure documented in the [Scenario Editor W2 review](https://app.notion.com/p/3aaf7cb4e4df81d58626cdda26db28eb) (W2-02), where a mock advertised a 300 ms validation debounce that LiveFindingsPresenter stores and never honours. An absent column is honest; an empty one is a bug report; a fabricated one is a lie. ### Phase A — buildable today against the shipped spine - CMD-24.1 — Cross-host aggregation. List air assets across all units in the current selection, grouped by type and host with counts (12x F/A-18A Hornet (CVN 70 Carl Vinson)). The reference aggregates a carrier, a cruiser, a frigate and a supply ship into one list — the player commands the group's air assets, not each deck separately. This is the window's single most important structural idea and it costs nothing extra to adopt. - CMD-24.2 — Binary readiness with an explicit cause. Show ReadyForLaunch, and where false, name the reason using the same AIR_NOT_READY vocabulary the engage gate already emits — so the window and the engage refusal agree word-for-word. - CMD-24.3 — Magazine-constrained loadout feasibility. For a selected loadout, show how many airframes can be armed from current stock. The reference does this well: # Available Magazines alongside # Available Mags + A/C answers "how many sorties can I actually arm?" rather than "how much do I have?" This is directly implementable on the shipped MagazineLedger. - CMD-24.4 — Aviation fuel shown distinctly from platform fuel (REQ-16 P0: per-domain fuel types). The reference states it as its own line: 0.0 fuel units remaining (Aviation Fuel). - CMD-24.5 — Assign to mission, bridging air assets to the mission system (doc 11). - CMD-24.6 — Aggregate ready count in group status (Aircraft: 35/71). One line, high value, no new model needed. ### Phase N — gated on the REQ-16 air-ops FSM Do not build these ahead of the model: time-to-ready timers; Launch Individually vs Launch as group(s); Abort Launch (requires an in-progress launch state); the Air Facilities tab (deck / hangar / runway capacity and deck cycle); and per-airframe drill-down beyond type aggregation. When the FSM lands, these should arrive together — a launch button without an abort is worse than neither. ### Do not inherit this defect In the reference, the entire action bar is disabled with only Loadout Details: None Selected as explanation. Which action needs what is left to inference. Per the disabled-with-reason pattern established in the editor reviews, each disabled action should carry its own reason — "select a loadout" differs from "no ready airframes" differs from "magazine stock insufficient." ### Projection dependency REQ-16 lists logistics_get_readiness and logistics_project_sorties as MCP Gap — not shipped. The same data has to reach this panel, so CMD-24 likely implies a new read-only projection under ADR-010 rather than view work alone. Worth confirming before estimating. ## CMD-25 — Boat Operations window \[P2 — blocked on domain model\] Requirement. The C2 client shall provide a Boat Operations window, opened from the unit-order toolbar (CMD-16), presenting embarked small craft across the current selection, their readiness, and their tasking. ### ⚠️ Epistemic note — what this is and is not based on I have not seen this window. No screenshot of CMO's Boat Operations dialog was reviewed. What is actually grounded: - A Boat Operations toolbar button sits beside Aircraft Operations in the reference product's order bar (visible in two screenshots) - Group status pairs Boats: 2/2 with Aircraft: 35/71 — the same ready-over-total treatment - REQ-16 maps boat ops to CMO manual §3.3.8 and scopes it P1 The existence and rough role of the window are grounded. Its contents are not. Any detailed layout below the requirement statement would be invention, so there isn't one — deliberately. ### The actual finding — the domain is unspecified, not just unbuilt CMD-24 was gated on a Phase-N state machine, but at least stood on a shipped spine (MagazineLedger, boolean ReadyForLaunch, fuel bands, ferry hooks). Boat operations has no such floor. REQ-16 contains a section literally titled "Boat and Naval Operations". Its entire content is three bullets: > P1 UNREP for fuel and limited rearm → Phase N\* > P0 Docked / underway replenishment affects readiness flags → Partial / Phase N\* > P0 Submarine battery/charge model (simplified) → Phase N\* That is replenishment and submarine power. None of it is about launching, recovering, or tasking boats. The section heading promises a domain the section does not specify. Corroborating checks: | Source | Boat operations coverage | | --- | --- | | REQ-16 §Boat and Naval Operations | UNREP / replenishment / sub battery only — no launch, recovery, or tasking | | REQ-18 Combat Domains | Zero hits for boat, small craft, amphibious, littoral | | REQ-20 C2 UI | No mention | | src/ sim model | No boat / craft / amphibious / boarding type exists | | Sea state / weather model | Not modelled — "sea state" appears only in REQ-15 sensor/EW context | Recommendation: specify the domain before the UI. A window spec written now would be interface over vapour at two levels — no model and no domain requirements. The productive next step is amending REQ-16 §Boat and Naval Operations to actually cover boat operations, then deriving this window from it. ### Why cloning CMD-24 would be wrong The symmetry of the toolbar buttons is misleading. Boats differ from aircraft in ways that change the interface, and a copied spec would encode the wrong model: - Recovery is the hard operation, not launch. Aircraft recovery is gated by deck cycle; boat recovery is gated by sea state and mothership manoeuvring, and a boat that cannot be recovered is a stranded crew, not a diverted airframe. The window's centre of gravity is different. - Sea state gates the operation — and Aegis has no weather or sea-state model at all. This is a hard dependency air ops does not have. - Cargo and personnel, not weapon loadouts. CMD-24.3's magazine-feasibility idea has no boat analogue; the equivalent question is who and what is embarked. - Counts are small. Boats: 2/2 versus Aircraft: 35/71 — type-aggregated rows (12x F/A-18A Hornet) are the right unit for air and the wrong one for boats, where each hull is individually tracked and named. - Boarding / VBSS is a mission type, not a launch action — it needs mission-system integration (doc 11) rather than an ops-window button. ### Scoping note worth raising The reference scenario is anti-piracy — the map carries a "Suspected Pirate Staging Area" label and hostile small craft. In that scenario class, boarding operations are the primary tactical activity, not a supporting one. If Aegis intends to support littoral or counter-piracy scenarios, P1/P2 understates boat operations and the priority deserves revisiting on scenario grounds rather than parity grounds. ### Phase A — what is genuinely buildable today Almost nothing, honestly: - CMD-25.1 — Embarked-craft ready count in group status (Boats: 2/2), mirroring CMD-24.6. This is a readout, needs no FSM, and is the only piece not blocked. Everything else waits on a domain model that does not exist yet. ## CMD-26 — Ground Operations window \[P2 — scoped to brigade+; battalion depth is out of charter\] Requirement. The C2 client shall provide a Ground Operations window presenting friendly and known-hostile ground formations at brigade echelon and above, their aggregate strength and readiness, their air-defence contribution, and their tasking — within the charter scope defined by doc 01. ### ⚠️ Scope finding — read before designing anything The requested echelon list runs division → brigade → regiment → battalion. The project charter already draws a line inside that list, and it is not a "not yet" — it is an explicit exclusion. Game-Requirements/requirements/01-Project-Overview.md: > In scope (line 82): "Air, naval, and aggregate-level ground (brigade+) for air/naval interaction" > > Out of scope (line 90): "Land warfare at battalion scale or below" Echoed normatively in REQ-18 §Land Combat (Limited): "Per doc 01 scope: strategic facilities and IADS, not battalion tactics." | Echelon | Charter status | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Division | In scope | Aggregate formation | | Brigade | In scope | The boundary, inclusive — "brigade+" | | Regiment | Needs a decision | Brigade-equivalent in US/NATO and Soviet-pattern usage, so probably in scope — but the charter says "brigade+", not "brigade-equivalent+". Worth resolving explicitly rather than by assumption. | | Battalion | Out of charter | doc 01 line 90 excludes battalion scale and below by name | ### The structural consequence — the TO&E tree is shallow, by design This is the finding that actually shapes the interface, and it is easy to miss. A TO&E window is usually a deep tree: division contains brigades, which contain battalions, which contain companies. But if the charter caps modelling at brigade+, then a brigade is a leaf, not a container. The hierarchy the request implies only has depth if battalions exist as modelled entities — and they explicitly do not. So the in-scope window is two or three levels deep at most: ```javascript Division └─ Brigade / Regiment ← leaf: aggregate strength, readiness, ADA contribution └─ (battalions: out of charter) ``` Designing a deep expandable TO&E tree would build interface for a hierarchy the sim will never populate — the same class of error as CMD-24's Time to ready column and the W2-02 debounce chip. Aggregate rows with no expander are the honest shape under current charter. ### What exists today | Capability | Status | | --- | --- | | CombatDomain.Land enum + LandAspectDomainValidator | Shipped spine / Partial aspect gate | | Ground platform presets in the scenario editor | Shipped — but they are IADS and facilities: Patriot PAC-3, M901 launcher, S-400, RBS-15 coastal battery, air base, port | | Tactical Group model (GroupTarget, DetachRejoinService, detach/rejoin records) | Shipped | | Echelon / TO&E / organisational hierarchy type | Does not exist — no Echelon, Formation, Brigade, Battalion type in src/ | | Full land IADS / battalion-scale combat | Phase N (REQ-18) | Note what the shipped ground presets are: every one is an air-defence system, a coastal battery, or a facility. That is precisely the charter's "strategic facilities and IADS" — the ground domain today is things that shoot at aircraft and things aircraft shoot at, not manoeuvre forces. ### TO&E is not the tactical Group model — do not conflate them Aegis has a Group concept with detach and rejoin. That is a transient tactical association — units operating together now, formed and dissolved at will, mirroring CMO's naval groups. TO&E is permanent organisational subordination — a battalion belongs to its brigade whether or not they are co-located, and that relationship survives detachment. The two answer different questions ("who is manoeuvring together" vs "who does this belong to") and a ground window needs the second, which does not exist. Reusing GroupTarget for echelon structure would silently make organisational hierarchy dissolvable, which is wrong. ### Phase A — buildable within the current charter - CMD-26.1 — Aggregate ground formation list at brigade+ with side, type, and location. Flat or two-level; no battalion expander. - CMD-26.2 — Air-defence contribution per formation — which IADS assets it fields, their state, and their coverage. This is the charter's stated purpose for modelling ground at all ("for air/naval interaction"), so it is the window's centre of gravity rather than a side panel. - CMD-26.3 — Facility status — airbase, port, runway damage, and sortie-capacity linkage into REQ-16 (doc 16 already wires runway/sortie capacity where present). - CMD-26.4 — Aggregate strength / readiness as a single band per formation, not a rolled-up sum of subordinate units — there are no subordinate units to roll up. ### Charter-change path — if battalion depth is genuinely wanted This cannot be filed as a UI requirement. It would require, in order: 1. Amend doc 01 line 90 — the exclusion is charter-level, and everything downstream inherits it 2. Amend REQ-18 §Land Combat (Limited), which cites doc 01 as its authority 3. Introduce an echelon / TO&E model in src/ distinct from the tactical Group model 4. Decide the regiment question above 5. Only then derive this window's deep-tree form That is a significant sim expansion — land manoeuvre warfare is a different game from the air/naval simulation the charter describes. Worth a deliberate product decision, not a requirements edit. ## CMD-27 — Scenario library and load operations \[P0\] Requirement. The client shall provide a scenario library surface for browsing, previewing, and loading scenarios and saved games, which states before load whether a scenario will actually run. ### Why P0 — this is the first screen of the game and it is specified nowhere | Source | What it says | | --- | --- | | doc 02 §Core Gameplay Loop | "Phase 1: Scenario Selection & Force Composition" — the loop begins here | | design/ux/c2-command-post.md:45 | Main Menu → **Scenario Select** → Mission Planning → C2 Command Post → AAR — named in the navigation flow | | REQ-20 | Zero mentions of load, main menu, front-end, or scenario select | | design/ux/ | No main-menu or scenario-select spec (c2-command-post, c2-map-placeholder, interaction-patterns, onboarding-baltic, scenario-editor) | | src/ • CLI | No scenario list/browse verb or projection — scenario_* has create / validate / export / publish / simulate / undo / diff / trace, but no list | Every player's first interaction with the product is a screen that is named twice and designed nowhere. ### The part that is not CMO parity — pre-load feasibility CMO's Load Scenario dialog lists files. Aegis scenarios are not just files — they are validated, catalog-bound, deterministic artifacts that can fail to load for reasons knowable in advance: - Catalog binding — dbRef / dbSnapshotId may not resolve against the installed catalog (DB_MISMATCH), and ref:-prefixed ids may dangle (BROKEN_REF). These are among the most common failure modes in the system. - Validation state — ADR-008 findings with severity; a scenario can carry blocking errors. - Schema / version — scenario-document.schema.json compatibility and editVersion. CMD-27.1 — Pre-load feasibility. The library shall state, per entry, whether the scenario resolves against the installed catalog and passes validation, before the user commits to loading it. This is the load-time analogue of the export gate (UX-01 / DRG-56 in the editor reviews). Same principle, different surface: a constraint the system already enforces should be visible before the user hits it, not as a failure afterwards. Listing an unloadable scenario with no indication is the browser equivalent of an unreachable gate. ### Phase A sub-requirements - CMD-27.2 — Provenance and trust. Distinguish authored / AI-scaffolded / imported (ManifestBuilder.ProvenanceTag, Source ∈ {user, ai, import}) and bundled / user-saved / third-party. ADR-015 (Proposed, decision due 2026-09-01) would derive an agent-authored label from provenance — this library is where that label becomes visible to a player, and is the natural forcing function for that decision. - CMD-27.3 — Determinism metadata. Show metadata.seed, TL branch (metadata.tlBranch), bound policy, and whether a published manifest with ReportHash exists. In a project where replay parity is a release gate, "will this reproduce" is a property worth seeing before opening. - CMD-27.4 — Separate artifact lifecycles. Autosaves, manual saves, and authored scenarios are different classes with different retention and trust; they shall not share one flat list. The reference mixes Autosave_20sec.scen through Autosave_100sec.scen directly among authored scenarios like Georgia2008.scen. - CMD-27.5 — Search and filter, not only sort. The reference offers a single Order scenarios by dropdown. Filter by side, region, duration, validation state, and TL branch. - CMD-27.6 — Preview pane with a real zero-state. Two further views of this dialog show what actually populates it, in one scrolling region: licence prefix + title, Difficulty and Complexity meters, Location — Year, a long briefing, and a rendered map preview. On open, with nothing selected, roughly 40% of the dialog is blank — the zero-state needs instruction, not void. - CMD-27.7 — Unavailable entries state their reason on the row. ⚠️ Corrected after further views. The padlocked entries are explained — selecting one shows [NOT LICENSED] Don of a new Era in red at the top of the preview. So the reason exists; it is just only reachable by selecting each locked item one at a time. The requirement is therefore narrower and cheaper than first written: carry the reason on the list row, so a player sees what they own by scanning rather than by clicking. (Still the third instance of disabled-without-reason in this series — after the editor's greyed actions and the Air Ops action bar — and worth a house rule.) - CMD-27.8 — Difficulty and Complexity as separate, rated axes. The reference rates both independently, as meters, colour-coded by level (green at low, orange higher). This is a better model than one star rating and worth adopting deliberately: difficulty is how hard the scenario is to win; complexity is how much there is to manage. They are orthogonal — a submarine duel can be hard and simple, a multi-domain operation forgiving and overwhelming.

For Aegis this matters more than for the reference product: agent delegation is the mitigation for complexity, not for difficulty. The library is where that value proposition first becomes legible, so the two axes should be visible before load, not discovered during play.

Accessibility: the reference encodes level by bar colour alone. Per CMD-12 (colourblind-safe affiliation), pair the meter with a value or label.

- CMD-27.9 — Setting metadata. Location and Year — the reference shows Ukraine — 2016 and Nova Scotia / Eastern Seaboard — 1975. These are the fields players actually browse by, and they are the natural filter axes for CMD-27.5. - CMD-27.10 — Briefing is the primary selection content, and it is long. The reference runs several paragraphs of geopolitical background in a scrolling region. Aegis already treats briefings as first-class — scenario_export_brief is a shipped CLI verb — so the preview should render the same brief that verb produces, not a separately authored summary. One brief, two surfaces: the CLI/MCP parity principle applied to the library. - CMD-27.11 — Map preview showing force disposition. The reference renders a real tactical thumbnail — terrain, NATO unit symbols, and place labels (CFB GREENWOOD, HALIFAX, HMCS TERRA NOVA, HMCS ASSINIBOINE) — pannable within the preview. You can read the shape of the fight before committing to load.

Aegis can build this cheaply: MapPictureProjection and MapPlaceholderPanelHost are shipped (REQ-20 CMD-06, ADR-007 Phase A). A scenario preview map is the same projection over an unopened document rather than live sim state — reuse, not new rendering work.

- CMD-27.12 — Campaigns are an artifact class, not a folder. The Northern Inferno node expands to 15 numbered, dated scenarios running 1. Opening Moves 07 Aug 1975 through 15. Fail Safe 20 Oct 1975 — an ordered chain with narrative progression, not a bag of unrelated files. Chains Of War is another. The library must model campaign membership, sequence, and completion state; treating a campaign as a directory loses all three. ### Do not inherit - File extensions in the UI. .scen is an implementation detail; Aegis uses *.scenario.json. Show scenario titles, with paths secondary — the same demotion CMD-09 needs in the editor chrome. - Mixed hierarchy. The reference places expandable folders and flat files at the same level, so Tutorials ▸ and Rumble.scen are siblings with different affordances. - Ordering encoded in filenames. Campaign sequence is carried by a 1. … 15. prefix and the date embedded in each name (Needle in a Hay Stack 19 Oct 1975.scen). Sequence and in-fiction date are metadata, not naming convention — encoding them in filenames makes reordering a rename, breaks sorting the moment someone omits a leading zero, and forces the extension-hiding rule above to fight the ordering scheme. ### Dependency — this is not view-only work There is no scenario list/browse verb or projection. Under ADR-010 (headless-first, command-driven), a browse surface needs a read-only projection, and under the CLI/MCP parity principle it should have a headless equivalent — likely scenario_list alongside the existing scenario_* verbs. Confirm before estimating. ## CMD-28 — Menu system, map layers, and view tools \[P1\] Requirement. The client shall provide a menu system exposing view control, map layer selection, spatial tools, and window management — and it shall be the discovery surface for keyboard shortcuts. Reference evidence. The View menu carries, in one flat list: Toggle Full-screen / Windowed Alt+Enter, Zoom In Z, Zoom Out X, Pan Map ▸, Select Next Unit |, Select Previous Unit Backspace, Range / Bearing Tool Ctrl+D, Message Log in Separate Window, Map Lat/Lon Grid, then ten basemap layers (Sentinel-2, ✓BMNG, Relief, ✓Borders + Coastlines, Stamen — Terrain, Stamen — Roads + Cities, Land Cover, Custom Layers, Placenames, Day + Night Lighting), and 3D View. ### The gap REQ-20 specifies no menu bar at all. Keyboard shortcuts appear once in the parity table (§10.1, P1 — Open), custom overlays once (§10.2, P2 — Phase N). There is no mention of fullscreen, zoom controls, a measurement tool, a coordinate grid, a 3D toggle, or basemap layers. ### CMD-28.1 — The menu is how shortcuts become discoverable Every item in the reference displays its binding inline. REQ-20 already wants keyboard shortcuts (§10.1) and the editor reviews found zero :focus rules in the shipped USS — but a shortcut nobody can find is not a feature. The menu is the discovery mechanism, and specifying shortcuts without specifying where they are advertised leaves them unusable. Pairs with the ? shortcut sheet proposed in the [ME-W1 review](https://app.notion.com/p/3a9f7cb4e4df8151ae42d2b0a065683e) (UX-06). ### CMD-28.2 — Basemap layer stack — an architectural gap, not a menu item Ten independently toggleable layers with persisted checked state. Aegis has no layer model. ADR-007 phases map presentation (Phase A placeholder → Phase B Cesium → Phase C APP-6 LOD) but never mentions a layer stack; src/ has no MapLayer / Basemap / overlay-stack type. This needs a decision before it needs a menu: - Which layers exist, and are they fixed or extensible (Custom Layers implies extensible)? - Who owns visibility state? Under ADR-010 everything else is a projection from the headless core — but layer visibility is pure presentation with no sim meaning. It should almost certainly be UI-local, and that exception is worth stating explicitly rather than discovering later. - Do layers persist per user, per scenario, or not at all? ### CMD-28.3 — View-state actions are exempt from CLI/MCP parity; command actions are not This menu makes a boundary explicit that the project will otherwise settle ad hoc. - View state — zoom, pan, layers, grid, fullscreen, 3D toggle — changes only what this operator sees. It has no headless meaning and needs no CLI verb, no order-log row, and no determinism guarantee. - Commands — anything that mutates the scenario or issues orders — must keep CLI/MCP parity and produce logged intents (ADR-010). Stating the line prevents both failure modes: plumbing view toggles through the command bus, and quietly letting a mutating menu item bypass the order log. ### CMD-28.4 — Spatial tools - Range / bearing measurement with a binding. REQ-20 lists "measure" only as a map context-menu item (§4.2, Partial). In a genre where range is the primary spatial judgement — the same reasoning behind CMD-20 — measurement deserves to be a tool, not a buried context entry. - Lat/Lon grid as a toggleable overlay; a coordinate reference alongside CMD-20's distance scale. ### CMD-28.5 — Keyboard unit cycling Select Next Unit / Select Previous Unit. Complements CMD-07 (map ↔ OOB ↔ panel selection sync) by making selection reachable without pointing, which matters for dense pictures and for accessibility. ### CMD-28.6 — Single-panel detachment is much cheaper than the multitasker Message Log in Separate Window detaches one panel to one window. REQ-20's CMD-14 defers "multitasker bookmarks / multi-monitor detachable chrome" to Phase N — but that is the full product feature. Detaching a single panel is a fraction of the cost and delivers most of the multi-monitor value for a log you want visible continuously. Worth splitting from CMD-14 rather than inheriting its deferral. ### CMD-28.7 — Menu organisation The reference's View menu mixes roughly six concerns — window management, camera, selection, tools, panel spawning, overlays, basemap layers, render mode — in one flat list of nineteen items. Adopt the coverage, not the organisation: separate view control from layer selection from tools. ### Do not inherit — the fourth instance Quick Jump is greyed in the menu bar with no stated reason. That is now the fourth disabled-without-reason case catalogued in this series — after the editor's greyed actions, the Air Ops action bar, and the scenario library's padlocks. This should stop being four findings and become one house rule: every disabled control states why, at the control. --- ## CMD-29 — Contact detail panel \[P0\] Requirement. Selecting a contact shall present a panel distinct from the own-unit panel, showing classification and its confidence, detection provenance, engagement permission, and battle-damage assessment. ### The framing that matters The unit panel shows what is. The contact panel shows what we believe. Everything about a contact is inference from sensor returns and may be wrong — the identification, the classification, the position, whether it is still there at all. Collapsing both into one "selected object" panel silently asserts that hostile data is as trustworthy as own-force data, which in this genre is the central lie to avoid. This is the same epistemics as CMD-17 seen from the other side: CMD-17 is "I own this unit but cannot reach it"; CMD-29 is "I can see this thing but do not own it." Both are about the gap between the world and the picture. ### The gap REQ-20's Right-panel row specifies "Selected unit/group: status, sensors, weapons, fuel, doctrine" — own-unit data only. Contacts appear in the left drawer (contact list tab) and in map styling ("Contact styling distinct from friendly"), but selecting one has no specified panel. ### Unusually, the data mostly exists Most gaps in this series are UI over an absent model. This one is the reverse: | Capability | Status | | --- | --- | | ContactSummaryProjection, ContactPictureProjection, ContactPictureEntry | Shipped (src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/) | | BdaContactDamageStates | Shipped | | ContactChangeRecord — contact lifecycle in the order log | Shipped (doc 17) | | WRA in the engage path | Shipped (EngagementAbortReason, MvpEngagementResolver, AbortReasonCatalog) | | Contact detail panel spec | Absent | The gap is specification, not model. That makes this cheaper than its P0 suggests. ### Sub-requirements - CMD-29.1 — Identification with its confidence. The reference is quietly precise here: the header reads SAM Bn (SA-3b) while the resolved line reads SAM Bn (SA-3c Gon [S-125M1 Nevn-M]). Those disagree — a coarse initial classification alongside a more specific resolution. Classification specificity increases as sensor data accumulates, and the panel must show how well the contact is identified, not merely assert a name. An overconfident label on a poorly-resolved contact is how players shoot the wrong thing. - CMD-29.2 — Detection provenance. "Detected by: Automatic detection on \[Unknown\]" — which sensor, on which platform, and when. Likely the single highest-value element on the panel: it answers why do I think this exists, connects doc 15 (sensor/detection) to CMD-11's "why can't I fire?" explain surface, and makes stale or single-source tracks visible rather than implicit. - CMD-29.3 — WRA classification. The reference shows WRA: Land Structure - Soft - Building (Revetted) — the target classification that drives release authority under doc 13. This is the field that determines whether an engagement is permitted, so it belongs on the panel where the engagement decision is made, not only inside an abort reason after refusal. - CMD-29.4 — BDA as belief, not truth. Damage / BDA / Damage Ctrl — battle damage assessment is an estimate from observation. Rendering it identically to own-unit damage state would assert knowledge the player does not have. BdaContactDamageStates already models this. - CMD-29.5 — Contact report action. A Contact Report… affordance producing the fuller intelligence picture for the selected track. - CMD-29.6 — Staleness. A contact not currently held is a last-known position with an age, not a current one. Pairs with the CMD-17 question about whether last-known values carry an age stamp or are suppressed — the two should be answered together and consistently, since they are the same design question on own units and on hostiles. ## CMD-30 — Tactical overlay control \[P1\] Requirement. The client shall provide control over tactical overlay symbology — range envelopes, engagement vectors, connectivity, courses, and datablocks — separately from basemap layer selection. Reference evidence. A Map Settings menu carrying eight colour-chipped range toggles (Air / Surface / Underwater Sensors, Air / Surface / Land / Underwater Weapons, Aircraft Range, each stating (Current: ON)), plus Show Non-friendly Range-Symbols, Merge Range-symbols, Sonobuoy Visibility, Reference Point Visibility, Illumination Vectors, Targetting Vectors, Datablocks, Datalinks, Contact Emissions, Plotted Courses, Mission area/course, Track Selected Unit (T), LOS Tool, Minimaps, and Terrain Type Legend — the last rendering a 17-class land-cover legend on the map. ### The architectural point — two stacks, two owners This is not the same surface as CMD-28.2, and the difference matters under ADR-010: | Stack | Content | Ownership | | --- | --- | --- | | Basemap layers (CMD-28.2) | Imagery, relief, borders, land cover — what the world looks like | UI-local; no sim meaning | | Tactical overlays (CMD-30) | Range envelopes, vectors, datalinks, courses — what the sim state looks like | Projections from the headless core | Two menus in the reference, two different owners. Conflating them would either plumb basemap toggles through the command bus, or make sim-derived overlays UI-local state that replay cannot reproduce. ### Sub-requirements - CMD-30.1 — Range symbology is a taxonomy, not a toggle. Eight independent controls across \{Air, Surface, Underwater\} × \{Sensors, Weapons\} plus Land Weapons and Aircraft Range. CMD-21 is a subset of this, not a synonym — CMD-21 is the Phase A baseline for the selected unit; CMD-30.1 is the picture-wide taxonomy. - CMD-30.2 — Non-friendly range symbols are beliefs. Estimated hostile envelopes are a major tactical affordance, but they are inference (CMD-29 epistemics) and must not render identically to own-force envelopes, which are known. - CMD-30.3 — Merged range symbols are Phase A decluttering, not Phase N LOD. REQ-20 discusses decluttering only under APP-6 LOD and the 5k@60 north-star (CMD-13/15, Phase N). Merging overlapping envelopes into a hull is cheap, needs no LOD product, and becomes necessary long before 5,000 symbols. Same baseline-versus-deferred split as CMD-21 — do not let it ride along with the LOD work. - CMD-30.4 — State in text, not colour alone. The reference writes (Current: ON) beside each colour chip. Adopt it: satisfies CMD-12 by construction and makes the menu readable without decoding swatches. - CMD-30.5 — Engagement geometry overlays. Illumination and targeting vectors — who is illuminating or targeting whom (doc 14). Pairs with CMD-11 intent preview. - CMD-30.6 — Connectivity and emissions. Datalinks are modelled (9 datalink types in src/); EMCON is modelled (EmconState, CatalogEmcon, CatalogRadarEmconResolver) though emissions as a distinct concept are not. Links docs 15 and 19 to the map. - CMD-30.7 — Route and mission-area overlays. - CMD-30.8 — Datablocks. Configurable symbol labels — the density knob that decides whether a dense picture is readable. Not modelled. - CMD-30.9 — Camera and analysis tools. Track-selected-unit, LOS tool, minimaps. None modelled. - CMD-30.10 — Legends for data-driven colouring. The reference pairs its land-cover layer with a 17-class legend. Any layer whose colour encodes a taxonomy needs one — without it the colouring is decoration the player cannot decode. - CMD-30.11 — Group / Unit view toggle, complementing CMD-07 (§4.4). > ⚠️ Colour budget — worth an explicit audit. Eight range-symbol colours, plus affiliation colours (CMD-12, which must stay colourblind-safe), plus seventeen land-cover classes, plus severity and diff colours. The colour channel is heavily oversubscribed, and adding overlays without a palette audit will collide with the accessibility commitment REQ-20 has already made. --- # 🔍 Original observation — now filed as CMD-29 above The same screenshot shows a Contact Status panel that is structurally different from the Unit Status panel reviewed earlier — and REQ-20 does not distinguish them. For a detected hostile (SAM Bn (SA-3b)) it shows: classification (Building (Revetted)), WRA line (Land Structure - Soft - Building (Revetted)), side, course/speed, a Contact Report… action, Damage / BDA / Damage Ctrl, and a DETECTIONS section reading "Detected by: Automatic detection on \[Unknown\]". REQ-20's Right-panel row specifies only "Selected unit/group: status, sensors, weapons, fuel, doctrine" — own-unit data. Selecting a contact has no specified panel, yet a contact answers different questions: how do I know it is there, how confident am I, what is it classified as, and may I shoot it. Unlike most gaps in this series, the data largely exists: ContactSummaryProjection, ContactPictureProjection, ContactPictureEntry, and BdaContactDamageStates are all in src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/, and WRA appears in the engage path (EngagementAbortReason, MvpEngagementResolver). The gap is specification, not model. The "Detected by" line is the most interesting part for Aegis — detection provenance connects doc 15 (sensor/detection) to the "why can't I fire?" explain surface (CMD-11), and to the comms-staleness question in CMD-17. Say tentatively: this may be the single highest-value contact-panel element. Not filed as CMD-29 — it was not the request. Flagged so it is not lost. --- # Proposed amendments to existing requirements | Existing | Amendment | | --- | --- | | CMD-04 Top bar | Absorb CMD-22; state the time model (multiplier vs time-per-step) explicitly | | CMD-09 Delegation badges | Note per-axis granularity per CMD-19 — a unit-level tri-state badge cannot express "mixed" | | CMD-10 Context menus | Note toolbar parity per CMD-16; both paths, not one | | CMD-06 Map symbol picture | Clarify that CMD-20 and CMD-21 are Phase A baseline, not Phase N with the product globe | | Layout Zones table | Add a sixth zone for the order toolbar (CMD-16) | # Minor observations, not filed as requirements - Crew proficiency — the reference shows Regular on the unit panel. Aegis models agent traits and attention; whether crew quality is player-visible is a design question, not a UI gap. - Named map areas — the reference labels a "Designated Pirate Staging Area" directly on the map. REQ-20 says "mission areas / reference points as projection data permits," which is vague about labelling. - Disabled menu items — Quick Jump and Contacts are greyed with no stated reason, the same disabled-without-explanation pattern flagged in the editor reviews. Worth not inheriting. - Selection stated three times — top-left label, map ring, and right-panel header. Deliberate redundancy for a dense screen; worth keeping in mind when trimming. --- > OPEN QUESTION: Should these land as new CMD rows in REQ-20, or as a Phase-2 addendum? REQ-20 is Status: Draft — Template B (Wave 2 re-honesty) with a carefully maintained honesty column; adding eight P0/P1 rows shifts its completion picture and should be a deliberate edit, not a drive-by. > OPEN QUESTION: CMD-17 and CMD-19 both imply projection changes, not just view work — per-axis autonomy state and comms-staleness have to reach the panel from the headless core. Are those projections already shaped for it, or is this an ADR-010 contract change? > OPEN QUESTION: How much CMO parity is actually wanted? REQ-20 tracks parity area-by-area against the manual, but Aegis's differentiator is agent delegation — CMD-19 is the one proposal here that has no CMO equivalent worth copying, because CMO has no agents to delegate to.
