One line, high value, no new model needed. ### Phase N — gated on the REQ-16 air-ops FSM Do not build these ahead of the model: time-to-ready timers; Launch Individually vs Launch as group(s); Abort Launch (requires an in-progress launch state); the Air Facilities tab (deck / hangar / runway capacity and deck cycle); and per-airframe drill-down beyond type aggregation. When the FSM lands, these should arrive together — a launch button without an abort is worse than neither. ### Do not inherit this defect In the reference, the entire action bar is disabled with only Loadout Details: None Selected as explanation. Which action needs what is left to inference. Per the disabled-with-reason pattern established in the editor reviews, each disabled action should carry its own reason — "select a loadout" differs from "no ready airframes" differs from "magazine stock insufficient." ### Projection dependency REQ-16 lists logistics_get_readiness and logistics_project_sorties as MCP Gap — not shipped. The same data has to reach this panel, so CMD-24 likely implies a new read-only projection under ADR-010 rather than view work alone. Worth confirming before estimating. ## CMD-25 — Boat Operations window \[P2 — blocked on domain model\] Requirement. The C2 client shall provide a Boat Operations window, opened from the unit-order toolbar (CMD-16), presenting embarked small craft across the current selection, their readiness, and their tasking. ### ⚠️ Epistemic note — what this is and is not based on I have not seen this window. No screenshot of CMO's Boat Operations dialog was reviewed. What is actually grounded: - A Boat Operations toolbar button sits beside Aircraft Operations in the reference product's order bar (visible in two screenshots) - Group status pairs Boats: 2/2 with Aircraft: 35/71 — the same ready-over-total treatment - REQ-16 maps boat ops to CMO manual §3.3.8 and scopes it P1 The existence and rough role of the window are grounded. Its contents are not. Any detailed layout below the requirement statement would be invention, so there isn't one — deliberately. ### The actual finding — the domain is unspecified, not just unbuilt CMD-24 was gated on a Phase-N state machine, but at least stood on a shipped spine (MagazineLedger, boolean ReadyForLaunch, fuel bands, ferry hooks). Boat operations has no such floor. REQ-16 contains a section literally titled "Boat and Naval Operations". Its entire content is three bullets: > P1 UNREP for fuel and limited rearm → Phase N\* > P0 Docked / underway replenishment affects readiness flags → Partial / Phase N\* > P0 Submarine battery/charge model (simplified) → Phase N\* That is replenishment and submarine power. None of it is about launching, recovering, or tasking boats. The section heading promises a domain the section does not specify. Corroborating checks: | Source | Boat operations coverage | | --- | --- | | REQ-16 §Boat and Naval Operations | UNREP / replenishment / sub battery only — no launch, recovery, or tasking | | REQ-18 Combat Domains | Zero hits for boat, small craft, amphibious, littoral | | REQ-20 C2 UI | No mention | | src/ sim model | No boat / craft / amphibious / boarding type exists | | Sea state / weather model | Not modelled — "sea state" appears only in REQ-15 sensor/EW context | Recommendation: specify the domain before the UI. A window spec written now would be interface over vapour at two levels — no model and no domain requirements. The productive next step is amending REQ-16 §Boat and Naval Operations to actually cover boat operations, then deriving this window from it. ### Why cloning CMD-24 would be wrong The symmetry of the toolbar buttons is misleading. Boats differ from aircraft in ways that change the interface, and a copied spec would encode the wrong model: - Recovery is the hard operation, not launch. Aircraft recovery is gated by deck cycle; boat recovery is gated by sea state and mothership manoeuvring, and a boat that cannot be recovered is a stranded crew, not a diverted airframe. The window's centre of gravity is different. - Sea state gates the operation — and Aegis has no weather or sea-state model at all. This is a hard dependency air ops does not have. - Cargo and personnel, not weapon loadouts. CMD-24.3's magazine-feasibility idea has no boat analogue; the equivalent question is who and what is embarked. - Counts are small. Boats: 2/2 versus Aircraft: 35/71 — type-aggregated rows (12x F/A-18A Hornet) are the right unit for air and the wrong one for boats, where each hull is individually tracked and named. - Boarding / VBSS is a mission type, not a launch action — it needs mission-system integration (doc 11) rather than an ops-window button. ### Scoping note worth raising The reference scenario is anti-piracy — the map carries a "Suspected Pirate Staging Area" label and hostile small craft. In that scenario class, boarding operations are the primary tactical activity, not a supporting one. If Aegis intends to support littoral or counter-piracy scenarios, P1/P2 understates boat operations and the priority deserves revisiting on scenario grounds rather than parity grounds. ### Phase A — what is genuinely buildable today Almost nothing, honestly: - CMD-25.1 — Embarked-craft ready count in group status (Boats: 2/2), mirroring CMD-24.6. This is a readout, needs no FSM, and is the only piece not blocked. Everything else waits on a domain model that does not exist yet. ## CMD-26 — Ground Operations window \[P2 — scoped to brigade+; battalion depth is out of charter\] Requirement. The C2 client shall provide a Ground Operations window presenting friendly and known-hostile ground formations at brigade echelon and above, their aggregate strength and readiness, their air-defence contribution, and their tasking — within the charter scope defined by doc 01. ### ⚠️ Scope finding — read before designing anything The requested echelon list runs division → brigade → regiment → battalion. The project charter already draws a line inside that list, and it is not a "not yet" — it is an explicit exclusion. Game-Requirements/requirements/01-Project-Overview.md: > In scope (line 82): "Air, naval, and aggregate-level ground (brigade+) for air/naval interaction" > > Out of scope (line 90): "Land warfare at battalion scale or below" Echoed normatively in REQ-18 §Land Combat (Limited): "Per doc 01 scope: strategic facilities and IADS, not battalion tactics." | Echelon | Charter status | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Division | In scope | Aggregate formation | | Brigade | In scope | The boundary, inclusive — "brigade+" | | Regiment | Needs a decision | Brigade-equivalent in US/NATO and Soviet-pattern usage, so probably in scope — but the charter says "brigade+", not "brigade-equivalent+". Worth resolving explicitly rather than by assumption. | | Battalion | Out of charter | doc 01 line 90 excludes battalion scale and below by name | ### The structural consequence — the TO&E tree is shallow, by design This is the finding that actually shapes the interface, and it is easy to miss. A TO&E window is usually a deep tree: division contains brigades, which contain battalions, which contain companies. But if the charter caps modelling at brigade+, then a brigade is a leaf, not a container. The hierarchy the request implies only has depth if battalions exist as modelled entities — and they explicitly do not. So the in-scope window is two or three levels deep at most: ```javascript Division └─ Brigade / Regiment ← leaf: aggregate strength, readiness, ADA contribution └─ (battalions: out of charter) ``` Designing a deep expandable TO&E tree would build interface for a hierarchy the sim will never populate — the same class of error as CMD-24's Time to ready column and the W2-02 debounce chip. Aggregate rows with no expander are the honest shape under current charter. ### What exists today | Capability | Status | | --- | --- | | CombatDomain.Land enum + LandAspectDomainValidator | Shipped spine / Partial aspect gate | | Ground platform presets in the scenario editor | Shipped — but they are IADS and facilities: Patriot PAC-3, M901 launcher, S-400, RBS-15 coastal battery, air base, port | | Tactical Group model (GroupTarget, DetachRejoinService, detach/rejoin records) | Shipped | | Echelon / TO&E / organisational hierarchy type | Does not exist — no Echelon, Formation, Brigade, Battalion type in src/ | | Full land IADS / battalion-scale combat | Phase N (REQ-18) | Note what the shipped ground presets are: every one is an air-defence system, a coastal battery, or a facility. That is precisely the charter's "strategic facilities and IADS" — the ground domain today is things that shoot at aircraft and things aircraft shoot at, not manoeuvre forces. ### TO&E is not the tactical Group model — do not conflate them Aegis has a Group concept with detach and rejoin. That is a transient tactical association — units operating together now, formed and dissolved at will, mirroring CMO's naval groups. TO&E is permanent organisational subordination — a battalion belongs to its brigade whether or not they are co-located, and that relationship survives detachment. The two answer different questions ("who is manoeuvring together" vs "who does this belong to") and a ground window needs the second, which does not exist. Reusing GroupTarget for echelon structure would silently make organisational hierarchy dissolvable, which is wrong. ### Phase A — buildable within the current charter - CMD-26.1 — Aggregate ground formation list at brigade+ with side, type, and location. Flat or two-level; no battalion expander. - CMD-26.2 — Air-defence contribution per formation — which IADS assets it fields, their state, and their coverage. This is the charter's stated purpose for modelling ground at all ("for air/naval interaction"), so it is the window's centre of gravity rather than a side panel. - CMD-26.3 — Facility status — airbase, port, runway damage, and sortie-capacity linkage into REQ-16 (doc 16 already wires runway/sortie capacity where present). - CMD-26.4 — Aggregate strength / readiness as a single band per formation, not a rolled-up sum of subordinate units — there are no subordinate units to roll up. ### Charter-change path — if battalion depth is genuinely wanted This cannot be filed as a UI requirement. It would require, in order: 1. Amend doc 01 line 90 — the exclusion is charter-level, and everything downstream inherits it 2. Amend REQ-18 §Land Combat (Limited), which cites doc 01 as its authority 3. Introduce an echelon / TO&E model in src/ distinct from the tactical Group model 4. Decide the regiment question above 5. Only then derive this window's deep-tree form That is a significant sim expansion — land manoeuvre warfare is a different game from the air/naval simulation the charter describes. Worth a deliberate product decision, not a requirements edit. ## CMD-27 — Scenario library and load operations \[P0\] Requirement. The client shall provide a scenario library surface for browsing, previewing, and loading scenarios and saved games, which states before load whether a scenario will actually run. ### Why P0 — this is the first screen of the game and it is specified nowhere | Source | What it says | | --- | --- | | doc 02 §Core Gameplay Loop | "Phase 1: Scenario Selection & Force Composition" — the loop begins here | | design/ux/c2-command-post.md:45 | Main Menu → **Scenario Select** → Mission Planning → C2 Command Post → AAR — named in the navigation flow | | REQ-20 | Zero mentions of load, main menu, front-end, or scenario select | | design/ux/ | No main-menu or scenario-select spec (c2-command-post, c2-map-placeholder, interaction-patterns, onboarding-baltic, scenario-editor) | | src/ • CLI | No scenario list/browse verb or projection — scenario_* has create / validate / export / publish / simulate / undo / diff / trace, but no list | Every player's first interaction with the product is a screen that is named twice and designed nowhere. ### The part that is not CMO parity — pre-load feasibility CMO's Load Scenario dialog lists files. Aegis scenarios are not just files — they are validated, catalog-bound, deterministic artifacts that can fail to load for reasons knowable in advance: - Catalog binding — dbRef / dbSnapshotId may not resolve against the installed catalog (DB_MISMATCH), and ref:-prefixed ids may dangle (BROKEN_REF). These are among the most common failure modes in the system. - Validation state — ADR-008 findings with severity; a scenario can carry blocking errors. - Schema / version — scenario-document.schema.json compatibility and editVersion. CMD-27.1 — Pre-load feasibility. The library shall state, per entry, whether the scenario resolves against the installed catalog and passes validation, before the user commits to loading it. This is the load-time analogue of the export gate (UX-01 / DRG-56 in the editor reviews). Same principle, different surface: a constraint the system already enforces should be visible before the user hits it, not as a failure afterwards. Listing an unloadable scenario with no indication is the browser equivalent of an unreachable gate. ### Phase A sub-requirements - CMD-27.2 — Provenance and trust. Distinguish authored / AI-scaffolded / imported (ManifestBuilder.ProvenanceTag, Source ∈ {user, ai, import}) and bundled / user-saved / third-party. ADR-015 (Proposed, decision due 2026-09-01) would derive an agent-authored label from provenance — this library is where that label becomes visible to a player, and is the natural forcing function for that decision. - CMD-27.3 — Determinism metadata. Show metadata.seed, TL branch (metadata.tlBranch), bound policy, and whether a published manifest with ReportHash exists. In a project where replay parity is a release gate, "will this reproduce" is a property worth seeing before opening. - CMD-27.4 — Separate artifact lifecycles. Autosaves, manual saves, and authored scenarios are different classes with different retention and trust; they shall not share one flat list. The reference mixes Autosave_20sec.scen through Autosave_100sec.scen directly among authored scenarios like Georgia2008.scen. - CMD-27.5 — Search and filter, not only sort. The reference offers a single Order scenarios by dropdown. Filter by side, region, duration, validation state, and TL branch. - CMD-27.6 — Preview pane with a real zero-state. Two further views of this dialog show what actually populates it, in one scrolling region: licence prefix + title, Difficulty and Complexity meters, Location — Year, a long briefing, and a rendered map preview. On open, with nothing selected, roughly 40% of the dialog is blank — the zero-state needs instruction, not void. - CMD-27.7 — Unavailable entries state their reason on the row. ⚠️ Corrected after further views. The padlocked entries are explained — selecting one shows [NOT LICENSED] Don of a new Era in red at the top of the preview. So the reason exists; it is just only reachable by selecting each locked item one at a time. The requirement is therefore narrower and cheaper than first written: carry the reason on the list row, so a player sees what they own by scanning rather than by clicking. (Still the third instance of disabled-without-reason in this series — after the editor's greyed actions and the Air Ops action bar — and worth a house rule.) - CMD-27.8 — Difficulty and Complexity as separate, rated axes. The reference rates both independently, as meters, colour-coded by level (green at low, orange higher). This is a better model than one star rating and worth adopting deliberately: difficulty is how hard the scenario is to win; complexity is how much there is to manage. They are orthogonal — a submarine duel can be hard and simple, a multi-domain operation forgiving and overwhelming.

For Aegis this matters more than for the reference product: agent delegation is the mitigation for complexity, not for difficulty. The library is where that value proposition first becomes legible, so the two axes should be visible before load, not discovered during play.

Accessibility: the reference encodes level by bar colour alone. Per CMD-12 (colourblind-safe affiliation), pair the meter with a value or label.

- CMD-27.9 — Setting metadata. Location and Year — the reference shows Ukraine — 2016 and Nova Scotia / Eastern Seaboard — 1975. These are the fields players actually browse by, and they are the natural filter axes for CMD-27.5. - CMD-27.10 — Briefing is the primary selection content, and it is long. The reference runs several paragraphs of geopolitical background in a scrolling region. Aegis already treats briefings as first-class — scenario_export_brief is a shipped CLI verb — so the preview should render the same brief that verb produces, not a separately authored summary. One brief, two surfaces: the CLI/MCP parity principle applied to the library. - CMD-27.11 — Map preview showing force disposition. The reference renders a real tactical thumbnail — terrain, NATO unit symbols, and place labels (CFB GREENWOOD, HALIFAX, HMCS TERRA NOVA, HMCS ASSINIBOINE) — pannable within the preview. You can read the shape of the fight before committing to load.

Aegis can build this cheaply: MapPictureProjection and MapPlaceholderPanelHost are shipped (REQ-20 CMD-06, ADR-007 Phase A). A scenario preview map is the same projection over an unopened document rather than live sim state — reuse, not new rendering work.

- CMD-27.12 — Campaigns are an artifact class, not a folder. The Northern Inferno node expands to 15 numbered, dated scenarios running 1. Opening Moves 07 Aug 1975 through 15. Fail Safe 20 Oct 1975 — an ordered chain with narrative progression, not a bag of unrelated files. Chains Of War is another. The library must model campaign membership, sequence, and completion state; treating a campaign as a directory loses all three. ### Do not inherit - File extensions in the UI. .scen is an implementation detail; Aegis uses *.scenario.json. Show scenario titles, with paths secondary — the same demotion CMD-09 needs in the editor chrome. - Mixed hierarchy. The reference places expandable folders and flat files at the same level, so Tutorials ▸ and Rumble.scen are siblings with different affordances. - Ordering encoded in filenames. Campaign sequence is carried by a 1. … 15. prefix and the date embedded in each name (Needle in a Hay Stack 19 Oct 1975.scen). Sequence and in-fiction date are metadata, not naming convention — encoding them in filenames makes reordering a rename, breaks sorting the moment someone omits a leading zero, and forces the extension-hiding rule above to fight the ordering scheme. ### Dependency — this is not view-only work There is no scenario list/browse verb or projection. Under ADR-010 (headless-first, command-driven), a browse surface needs a read-only projection, and under the CLI/MCP parity principle it should have a headless equivalent — likely scenario_list alongside the existing scenario_* verbs. Confirm before estimating. ## CMD-28 — Menu system, map layers, and view tools \[P1\] Requirement. The client shall provide a menu system exposing view control, map layer selection, spatial tools, and window management — and it shall be the discovery surface for keyboard shortcuts. Reference evidence. The View menu carries, in one flat list: Toggle Full-screen / Windowed Alt+Enter, Zoom In Z, Zoom Out X, Pan Map ▸, Select Next Unit |, Select Previous Unit Backspace, Range / Bearing Tool Ctrl+D, Message Log in Separate Window, Map Lat/Lon Grid, then ten basemap layers (Sentinel-2, ✓BMNG, Relief, ✓Borders + Coastlines, Stamen — Terrain, Stamen — Roads + Cities, Land Cover, Custom Layers, Placenames, Day + Night Lighting), and 3D View. ### The gap REQ-20 specifies no menu bar at all. Keyboard shortcuts appear once in the parity table (§10.1, P1 — Open), custom overlays once (§10.2, P2 — Phase N). There is no mention of fullscreen, zoom controls, a measurement tool, a coordinate grid, a 3D toggle, or basemap layers. ### CMD-28.1 — The menu is how shortcuts become discoverable Every item in the reference displays its binding inline. REQ-20 already wants keyboard shortcuts (§10.1) and the editor reviews found zero :focus rules in the shipped USS — but a shortcut nobody can find is not a feature. The menu is the discovery mechanism, and specifying shortcuts without specifying where they are advertised leaves them unusable. Pairs with the ? shortcut sheet proposed in the [ME-W1 review](https://app.notion.com/p/3a9f7cb4e4df8151ae42d2b0a065683e) (UX-06). ### CMD-28.2 — Basemap layer stack — an architectural gap, not a menu item Ten independently toggleable layers with persisted checked state. Aegis has no layer model. ADR-007 phases map presentation (Phase A placeholder → Phase B Cesium → Phase C APP-6 LOD) but never mentions a layer stack; src/ has no MapLayer / Basemap / overlay-stack type. This needs a decision before it needs a menu: - Which layers exist, and are they fixed or extensible (Custom Layers implies extensible)? - Who owns visibility state? Under ADR-010 everything else is a projection from the headless core — but layer visibility is pure presentation with no sim meaning. It should almost certainly be UI-local, and that exception is worth stating explicitly rather than discovering later. - Do layers persist per user, per scenario, or not at all? ### CMD-28.3 — View-state actions are exempt from CLI/MCP parity; command actions are not This menu makes a boundary explicit that the project will otherwise settle ad hoc. - View state — zoom, pan, layers, grid, fullscreen, 3D toggle — changes only what this operator sees. It has no headless meaning and needs no CLI verb, no order-log row, and no determinism guarantee. - Commands — anything that mutates the scenario or issues orders — must keep CLI/MCP parity and produce logged intents (ADR-010). Stating the line prevents both failure modes: plumbing view toggles through the command bus, and quietly letting a mutating menu item bypass the order log. ### CMD-28.4 — Spatial tools - Range / bearing measurement with a binding. REQ-20 lists "measure" only as a map context-menu item (§4.2, Partial). In a genre where range is the primary spatial judgement — the same reasoning behind CMD-20 — measurement deserves to be a tool, not a buried context entry. - Lat/Lon grid as a toggleable overlay; a coordinate reference alongside CMD-20's distance scale. ### CMD-28.5 — Keyboard unit cycling Select Next Unit / Select Previous Unit. Complements CMD-07 (map ↔ OOB ↔ panel selection sync) by making selection reachable without pointing, which matters for dense pictures and for accessibility. ### CMD-28.6 — Single-panel detachment is much cheaper than the multitasker Message Log in Separate Window detaches one panel to one window. REQ-20's CMD-14 defers "multitasker bookmarks / multi-monitor detachable chrome" to Phase N — but that is the full product feature. Detaching a single panel is a fraction of the cost and delivers most of the multi-monitor value for a log you want visible continuously. Worth splitting from CMD-14 rather than inheriting its deferral. ### CMD-28.7 — Menu organisation The reference's View menu mixes roughly six concerns — window management, camera, selection, tools, panel spawning, overlays, basemap layers, render mode — in one flat list of nineteen items. Adopt the coverage, not the organisation: separate view control from layer selection from tools. ### Do not inherit — the fourth instance Quick Jump is greyed in the menu bar with no stated reason. That is now the fourth disabled-without-reason case catalogued in this series — after the editor's greyed actions, the Air Ops action bar, and the scenario library's padlocks. This should stop being four findings and become one house rule: every disabled control states why, at the control. --- ## CMD-29 — Contact detail panel \[P0\] Requirement. Selecting a contact shall present a panel distinct from the own-unit panel, showing classification and its confidence, detection provenance, engagement permission, and battle-damage assessment. ### The framing that matters The unit panel shows what is. The contact panel shows what we believe. Everything about a contact is inference from sensor returns and may be wrong — the identification, the classification, the position, whether it is still there at all. Collapsing both into one "selected object" panel silently asserts that hostile data is as trustworthy as own-force data, which in this genre is the central lie to avoid. This is the same epistemics as CMD-17 seen from the other side: CMD-17 is "I own this unit but cannot reach it"; CMD-29 is "I can see this thing but do not own it." Both are about the gap between the world and the picture. ### The gap REQ-20's Right-panel row specifies "Selected unit/group: status, sensors, weapons, fuel, doctrine" — own-unit data only. Contacts appear in the left drawer (contact list tab) and in map styling ("Contact styling distinct from friendly"), but selecting one has no specified panel. ### Unusually, the data mostly exists Most gaps in this series are UI over an absent model. This one is the reverse: | Capability | Status | | --- | --- | | ContactSummaryProjection, ContactPictureProjection, ContactPictureEntry | Shipped (src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/) | | BdaContactDamageStates | Shipped | | ContactChangeRecord — contact lifecycle in the order log | Shipped (doc 17) | | WRA in the engage path | Shipped (EngagementAbortReason, MvpEngagementResolver, AbortReasonCatalog) | | Contact detail panel spec | Absent | The gap is specification, not model. That makes this cheaper than its P0 suggests. ### Sub-requirements - CMD-29.1 — Identification with its confidence. The reference is quietly precise here: the header reads SAM Bn (SA-3b) while the resolved line reads SAM Bn (SA-3c Gon [S-125M1 Nevn-M]). Those disagree — a coarse initial classification alongside a more specific resolution. Classification specificity increases as sensor data accumulates, and the panel must show how well the contact is identified, not merely assert a name. An overconfident label on a poorly-resolved contact is how players shoot the wrong thing. - CMD-29.2 — Detection provenance. "Detected by: Automatic detection on \[Unknown\]" — which sensor, on which platform, and when. Likely the single highest-value element on the panel: it answers why do I think this exists, connects doc 15 (sensor/detection) to CMD-11's "why can't I fire?" explain surface, and makes stale or single-source tracks visible rather than implicit. - CMD-29.3 — WRA classification. The reference shows WRA: Land Structure - Soft - Building (Revetted) — the target classification that drives release authority under doc 13. This is the field that determines whether an engagement is permitted, so it belongs on the panel where the engagement decision is made, not only inside an abort reason after refusal. - CMD-29.4 — BDA as belief, not truth. Damage / BDA / Damage Ctrl — battle damage assessment is an estimate from observation. Rendering it identically to own-unit damage state would assert knowledge the player does not have. BdaContactDamageStates already models this. - CMD-29.5 — Contact report action. A Contact Report… affordance producing the fuller intelligence picture for the selected track. - CMD-29.6 — Staleness. A contact not currently held is a last-known position with an age, not a current one. Pairs with the CMD-17 question about whether last-known values carry an age stamp or are suppressed — the two should be answered together and consistently, since they are the same design question on own units and on hostiles. ## CMD-30 — Tactical overlay control \[P1\] Requirement. The client shall provide control over tactical overlay symbology — range envelopes, engagement vectors, connectivity, courses, and datablocks — separately from basemap layer selection. Reference evidence. A Map Settings menu carrying eight colour-chipped range toggles (Air / Surface / Underwater Sensors, Air / Surface / Land / Underwater Weapons, Aircraft Range, each stating (Current: ON)), plus Show Non-friendly Range-Symbols, Merge Range-symbols, Sonobuoy Visibility, Reference Point Visibility, Illumination Vectors, Targetting Vectors, Datablocks, Datalinks, Contact Emissions, Plotted Courses, Mission area/course, Track Selected Unit (T), LOS Tool, Minimaps, and Terrain Type Legend — the last rendering a 17-class land-cover legend on the map. ### The architectural point — two stacks, two owners This is not the same surface as CMD-28.2, and the difference matters under ADR-010: | Stack | Content | Ownership | | --- | --- | --- | | Basemap layers (CMD-28.2) | Imagery, relief, borders, land cover — what the world looks like | UI-local; no sim meaning | | Tactical overlays (CMD-30) | Range envelopes, vectors, datalinks, courses — what the sim state looks like | Projections from the headless core | Two menus in the reference, two different owners. Conflating them would either plumb basemap toggles through the command bus, or make sim-derived overlays UI-local state that replay cannot reproduce. ### Sub-requirements - CMD-30.1 — Range symbology is a taxonomy, not a toggle. Eight independent controls across \{Air, Surface, Underwater\} × \{Sensors, Weapons\} plus Land Weapons and Aircraft Range. CMD-21 is a subset of this, not a synonym — CMD-21 is the Phase A baseline for the selected unit; CMD-30.1 is the picture-wide taxonomy. - CMD-30.2 — Non-friendly range symbols are beliefs. Estimated hostile envelopes are a major tactical affordance, but they are inference (CMD-29 epistemics) and must not render identically to own-force envelopes, which are known. - CMD-30.3 — Merged range symbols are Phase A decluttering, not Phase N LOD. REQ-20 discusses decluttering only under APP-6 LOD and the 5k@60 north-star (CMD-13/15, Phase N). Merging overlapping envelopes into a hull is cheap, needs no LOD product, and becomes necessary long before 5,000 symbols. Same baseline-versus-deferred split as CMD-21 — do not let it ride along with the LOD work. - CMD-30.4 — State in text, not colour alone. The reference writes (Current: ON) beside each colour chip. Adopt it: satisfies CMD-12 by construction and makes the menu readable without decoding swatches. - CMD-30.5 — Engagement geometry overlays. Illumination and targeting vectors — who is illuminating or targeting whom (doc 14). Pairs with CMD-11 intent preview. - CMD-30.6 — Connectivity and emissions. Datalinks are modelled (9 datalink types in src/); EMCON is modelled (EmconState, CatalogEmcon, CatalogRadarEmconResolver) though emissions as a distinct concept are not. Links docs 15 and 19 to the map. - CMD-30.7 — Route and mission-area overlays. - CMD-30.8 — Datablocks. Configurable symbol labels — the density knob that decides whether a dense picture is readable. Not modelled. - CMD-30.9 — Camera and analysis tools. Track-selected-unit, LOS tool, minimaps. None modelled. - CMD-30.10 — Legends for data-driven colouring. The reference pairs its land-cover layer with a 17-class legend. Any layer whose colour encodes a taxonomy needs one — without it the colouring is decoration the player cannot decode. - CMD-30.11 — Group / Unit view toggle, complementing CMD-07 (§4.4). > ⚠️ Colour budget — worth an explicit audit. Eight range-symbol colours, plus affiliation colours (CMD-12, which must stay colourblind-safe), plus seventeen land-cover classes, plus severity and diff colours. The colour channel is heavily oversubscribed, and adding overlays without a palette audit will collide with the accessibility commitment REQ-20 has already made. --- # 🔍 Original observation — now filed as CMD-29 above The same screenshot shows a Contact Status panel that is structurally different from the Unit Status panel reviewed earlier — and REQ-20 does not distinguish them. For a detected hostile (SAM Bn (SA-3b)) it shows: classification (Building (Revetted)), WRA line (Land Structure - Soft - Building (Revetted)), side, course/speed, a Contact Report… action, Damage / BDA / Damage Ctrl, and a DETECTIONS section reading "Detected by: Automatic detection on \[Unknown\]". REQ-20's Right-panel row specifies only "Selected unit/group: status, sensors, weapons, fuel, doctrine" — own-unit data. Selecting a contact has no specified panel, yet a contact answers different questions: how do I know it is there, how confident am I, what is it classified as, and may I shoot it. Unlike most gaps in this series, the data largely exists: ContactSummaryProjection, ContactPictureProjection, ContactPictureEntry, and BdaContactDamageStates are all in src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/, and WRA appears in the engage path (EngagementAbortReason, MvpEngagementResolver). The gap is specification, not model. The "Detected by" line is the most interesting part for Aegis — detection provenance connects doc 15 (sensor/detection) to the "why can't I fire?" explain surface (CMD-11), and to the comms-staleness question in CMD-17. Say tentatively: this may be the single highest-value contact-panel element. Not filed as CMD-29 — it was not the request. Flagged so it is not lost. --- # Proposed amendments to existing requirements | Existing | Amendment | | --- | --- | | CMD-04 Top bar | Absorb CMD-22; state the time model (multiplier vs time-per-step) explicitly | | CMD-09 Delegation badges | Note per-axis granularity per CMD-19 — a unit-level tri-state badge cannot express "mixed" | | CMD-10 Context menus | Note toolbar parity per CMD-16; both paths, not one | | CMD-06 Map symbol picture | Clarify that CMD-20 and CMD-21 are Phase A baseline, not Phase N with the product globe | | Layout Zones table | Add a sixth zone for the order toolbar (CMD-16) | # Minor observations, not filed as requirements - Crew proficiency — the reference shows Regular on the unit panel. Aegis models agent traits and attention; whether crew quality is player-visible is a design question, not a UI gap. - Named map areas — the reference labels a "Designated Pirate Staging Area" directly on the map. REQ-20 says "mission areas / reference points as projection data permits," which is vague about labelling. - Disabled menu items — Quick Jump and Contacts are greyed with no stated reason, the same disabled-without-explanation pattern flagged in the editor reviews. Worth not inheriting. - Selection stated three times — top-left label, map ring, and right-panel header. Deliberate redundancy for a dense screen; worth keeping in mind when trimming. --- > OPEN QUESTION: Should these land as new CMD rows in REQ-20, or as a Phase-2 addendum? REQ-20 is Status: Draft — Template B (Wave 2 re-honesty) with a carefully maintained honesty column; adding eight P0/P1 rows shifts its completion picture and should be a deliberate edit, not a drive-by. > OPEN QUESTION: CMD-17 and CMD-19 both imply projection changes, not just view work — per-axis autonomy state and comms-staleness have to reach the panel from the headless core. Are those projections already shaped for it, or is this an ADR-010 contract change? > OPEN QUESTION: How much CMO parity is actually wanted? REQ-20 tracks parity area-by-area against the manual, but Aegis's differentiator is agent delegation — CMD-19 is the one proposal here that has no CMO equivalent worth copying, because CMO has no agents to delegate to.

linear.title: [C2-05 follow-up] Cache attack-options preview; stop per-frame rebuild in AttackOptionsPreviewBinder
linear.description:
Follow-up from the Codex P2 review on <pull-request id="933188ec-4367-4e5e-b094-e376ee16a53f" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#678" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featui-drg-262-attack-options-menu-preview-parity-af04e6c6149b" /> (<issue id="edefdae9-4a5b-49dc-ba94-cc0d4a461203" label="DRG-262" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262/c2-05-attack-options-menu-preview-parity" />): [https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/678#discussion_r4116585799](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/678#discussion_r4116585799>)

While the panel is visible, `RightUnitPanelHost.LateUpdate()` calls `Refresh()` every frame, and that unconditionally rebuilds the preview arrays, per-option records and joined strings in `AttackOptionsPreviewBinder`. The result is continuous managed garbage and possible Unity GC stutter.

## AC

- [ ] Rebuild the bound preview only when the projected attack menu changes (cache it by menu fingerprint or contents)
- [ ] Zero per-frame allocations from the binder while the menu is unchanged, with a headless test asserting the cache hit
- [ ] No new sim queries and no edits to DelegationBridge Tick or the hotpath

## Surface (proposed)

`AttackOptionsPreviewBinder` plus its tests only. Do not overlap with <issue id="5ac73570-f572-45f1-bc7b-013650ad64ed" label="DRG-258" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-258/c2-01-weapon-abort-tooltip-top-3-fireabortreason" />'s `RightUnitPanelHost` work; sequence this after 258 lands if 258 touches `Refresh()`.

## Context

* Remainder of <issue id="25d518d7-1839-4600-8aef-bbea420601a1" label="DRG-322" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-322/c2-05-follow-up-cache-attack-options-preview-stop-per-frame-rebuild-in" /> after [drgaciw/cmano-clone#700](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-card-drg-353354355-contact-card-hardening-drg-322-attack-283b8d44d493>).

## Acceptance criteria

* Rendered output is unchanged, with a test proving no rebuild when inputs are unchanged.
* Replay goldens stay unchanged.

For combat detail: `LastCombatFrame` reference, `Presentation.CombatInspection.SelectedKey`, `SelectedUnitId`, `SelectedContactId` (the inputs of `ProjectCombatDetail()`, L205). For engage explanation: the `ProjectSelectedEngagePreview()` result. The test proves no rebuild when inputs are unchanged and identical output when they change.

Read-only, do not edit: `DelegationBridgeHost.cs`, `WeaponAbortTooltipBinder.cs` and `WeaponAbortTooltip*Tests.cs` (DRG-352), `EngageExplainProjection`, `CombatSelectionPresenter`. No DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath change, no ReplayGolden change.

linear.title: DRG-165 follow-up: wire Slice A targetability into production CombatPresentationFrame.Build; match targetability on shooter + target
linear.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review findings on [PR #696](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/696>) (<issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" /> combat event contract consumes Slice A targetability + execution facts), plus a matching finding on [PR #702](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/702>) (<issue id="28e8db3d-4595-4bbb-ba4d-c38283aa6261" label="DRG-166" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-166/combat-vertical-slice-scenario-and-acceptance-harness" /> vertical-slice harness).

## Findings

1. `CombatPresentationFrame.cs:79` **— Slice A link exists only in tests.** The bridge and `SliceBCombatScenario` call `Build` without Slice A targetability, so the targetability → combat-event link DRG-165 advertises is only exercised by unit tests, never on the production/scenario path.
2. `CombatEventProjection.cs:240` **— targetability lookup matches target only.** It should also match the requested shooter; otherwise a targetability fact for a different shooter on the same target can be attached to the event.
3. **Same pattern in PR #702:** `EngagementExplanationProjection.cs:90` uses a target-only lookup, so an earlier refusal can show later (or other-shooter) facts.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #696 / #702)

The PRs land the headless contract and harness; changing the bridge/scenario composition widens Surface beyond the stamped presentation files. The lookup fixes are correctness hardening with no current production consumer depending on multi-shooter disambiguation.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* Bridge and `SliceBCombatScenario` pass the authoritative Slice A targetability state into `CombatPresentationFrame.Build`; a scenario-level test (not a hand-built frame) proves the link appears.
* `CombatEventProjection` targetability lookup keys on (shooter, target) \[and correlation/time where applicable\]; test with two shooters on one target proves the correct fact is attached.
* `EngagementExplanationProjection` lookup keys on shooter + target and respects ledger/sim-time order so an earlier refusal never shows later facts; regression test included.
* Replay-stable; ReplayGolden / Baltic v2 hash untouched; `DelegationBridge` hotpath unchanged unless a separate single-owner story owns it.

Surface (CMANO re-stamp 2026-10-29, main 3bcfbb7b): `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/CombatVerticalSliceHarness.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/SliceBCombatScenario.cs` (only if the scenario `Result` must carry the targetability frame), `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Baltic/CombatVerticalSliceHarnessTests.cs`. All three exist on main 3bcfbb7b; none is hard-no.

Dependency cleared: PR <pull-request id="7cb3625f-5a34-475a-99d8-8786ce00096d" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#710" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-preserve-shooter-scoped-slice-a-facts-65e19ccd2f6f" /> (`fix(combat): preserve shooter-scoped Slice A facts`) merged into `main` 2026-10-15 (merge commit 7674649f, an ancestor of 3bcfbb7b). It covered findings 1, 2 and 3 (runtime bridge plus shooter + target lookups). This story is the residual scenario path: on 3bcfbb7b `CombatVerticalSliceHarness.cs:97` still passes `SliceAContactFrame.Empty` into `CombatPresentationFrameBridge.Build`; pass a frame carrying the authoritative targetability built at line 95, plus a scenario-level test (not a hand-built frame) proving the link appears in `slice.Frame.Events.Targetability`.

Read-only, do not edit (landed via <pull-request id="7cb3625f-5a34-475a-99d8-8786ce00096d" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#710" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-preserve-shooter-scoped-slice-a-facts-65e19ccd2f6f" />, now on main): `CombatPresentationFrame.cs`, `SliceAContactFrame.cs`, `CombatEventProjection.cs`, `CombatEventLogProjection.cs`, `CombatEventFingerprint.cs`, `CombatEventTypes.cs`, `EngagementExplanationProjection.cs`, `TargetabilityAcceptProjection.cs` and their tests. Not touched: `DelegationBridgeHost.cs`, `SimulationSession.cs` (used, not edited), ReplayGolden / Baltic v2 hash. Open gap outside this Surface: on 3bcfbb7b `EngagementExplanationProjection.FindTargetability` is shooter + target scoped but has no sim-time ordering, so <pull-request id="7cb3625f-5a34-475a-99d8-8786ce00096d" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#710" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-preserve-shooter-scoped-slice-a-facts-65e19ccd2f6f" /> did not cover the sim-time acceptance bullet. Track that in a separate follow-up; do not widen this Surface.

Owner lane: SliceA. Not reserved.

linear.title: Manual autonomy is non-functional — GateResult.QueueForApproval has no product consumer
linear.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28. Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD.

## The contradiction

Req 04 defines autonomy level **Manual** as:

> **Manual** — Agent suggests actions only; player must approve (`HUMAN_IN_LOOP`)

There is no approval path. The suggestion is computed, logged, and discarded.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | The gate models an approval outcome | `Orchestration/AutonomyGate.cs:7` — `GateResult(bool ExecuteNow, bool QueueForApproval, bool Rejected, FireAbortReason PolicyDenialReason)` |
| 2 | Manual autonomy sets it | `AutonomyGate.cs:29` — `AutonomyLevel.Manual => new GateResult(playerApproved, !playerApproved, false)` |
| 3 | The caller hardcodes no approval | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:141` — `gate.Evaluate(Autonomy, order, playerApproved: false)` |
| 4 | Only two branches are handled | `AgentController.cs:142-158` — `if (gateResult.Rejected && ...)` logs a denial; `if (gateResult.ExecuteNow)` issues. `QueueForApproval` **is never read** |
| 5 | Nothing else consumes it | Repo-wide grep for `QueueForApproval` outside its declaration returns only `AutonomyGateTests.cs` (3 assertions) |

## Effect

At **Manual** autonomy — and at **Assisted** with a high-risk order — the agent runs its full decision pipeline, appends a `DecisionRecord` (chosen action, candidate set, rationale, attention load/budget, RNG draw), and the resulting order is then **silently dropped**. The player is never asked. The unit does nothing.

The decision *record* survives in the order log, so a replay shows the agent deciding and no order following — which reads as an engine bug rather than a missing feature.

## Why it matters beyond the one level

`HUMAN_IN_LOOP` is the autonomy tier that makes lethal delegation defensible (req 13: full-auto lethal engagement requires explicit opt-in per mission phase). The tier below full-auto currently does nothing at all.

## To close

- [ ] Retain approval-gated orders as durable pending items bound to unit + agent + originating `DecisionRecord` (req 04 **AGD-07**)
- [ ] Approve/reject path, both logged, so an AAR distinguishes *proposed and refused* from *never proposed* (**AGD-08**)
- [ ] Tick-based expiry, identical at 1× and 60× compression — must not vary with frame rate, to preserve replay determinism (**AGD-09**)
- [ ] Surface the backlog with alert priority (**AGD-10**, doc 20 **ALR-01**)
- [ ] Determinism: `ReplayGolden` held; Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged or golden-updated with an ADR

## Related

Requirements written up in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-07 – AGD-10, acceptance criteria 1–2). The UI half depends on the command result channel tracked separately in doc 20 **CMD-16**.

linear.title: SkillEnvelopeValidator.Validate has no production caller — wire it in or remove it
linear.description:
## Problem

`SkillEnvelopeValidator.Validate(SkillEnvelope, bool proposalApproved)` is public and tested, but no production code calls it. Production code reuses only its reason-code constants. Either the skill-envelope check is never enforced at runtime, or the method is dead code.

## Evidence

* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Skills/SkillEnvelopeValidator.cs` (L31, `Validate`).
* GitHub code search for `SkillEnvelopeValidator` on main finds only tests (`src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Skills/SkillEnvelopeValidatorTests.cs`), docs/contract files (`production/docs/skills/agent-c2-skill-contract/*`, `docs/engineering/c2-authority-escalation-chrome.md`), and `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Skills/C2AuthorityProjector.cs`. `C2AuthorityProjector` references only the `Reason*` constants (L15–17) and never calls `Validate`.
* `production/qa/drg-197-gitnexus-reindex-evidence.md` (<issue id="72627172-94af-41de-b160-61e0febb7890" label="DRG-197" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-197/reindex-gitnexus-and-verify-the-post-implementation-knowledge-graph" />, PR <pull-request id="6557634e-7317-47ec-9c33-b2e9d8669d2a" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#681" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/drg-197-gitnexus-reindex-verify-evidence-at-7a097f93-737a691527e4" />): the GitNexus query for the envelope validator returned 0 processes.

## Acceptance criteria

* Make a decision, written down: either wire `Validate` into the production skill/engage command path, or remove it and move the constants somewhere else.
* If wired in: a production caller exists, a test proves a rejected envelope is blocked, and the skill contract doc is updated.
* If removed: the tests and the contract docs (`CONTRACT.md`, `PROOF.md`, `verify-contract.ps1`) are updated, and the build is green.

Source: Project Aegis room 2026-10-07 (SliceB/SliceC/Hygiene)

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

linear.description:

**User story:** As a player, I want to seize, pause, and return a delegated unit from the unit panel.

## AC

- [ ] Take control yields agent immediately; unit shows Human; group member detaches per locked decision
- [ ] Pause suspends intents without clearing tasking; Resume restores

User instruction: “proceed with your recommendations” following the game-mechanics/UX review. [Delivery plan](<https://app.notion.com/p/409f7cb4e4df815bbccfe465326584cc?pvs=204>). notion.title: 🎯 Combat Interaction UX — Proposed Requirements and Vertical Slice
notion.note:
[🎯 Combat Interaction UX — Proposed Requirements and Vertical Slice] — Status: Draft — Matched: Delivery status (Linear 2026-09-04): Headless Combat UX stories DRG-206–230 are Done on main @ 6f80d226 (#610 docs W1-HUB). Wave 5 leftovers (#600–#603) remain --- ## Four-system delivery contract - Notion: requirements, slice framing, acceptance gates, and design decisions. - Linear: milestones, epics, stories, ownership, dependencies, and delivery status. - GitHub: code, pull-request review, CI evidence, merge history, and release provenance. - Graphite: atomic branch stacks and pull-request ordering; each layer remains independently reviewable. ### Required traceability Every Linear implementation story links to this requirements page. Every GitHub pull request names its Linear story, links the relevant Notion requirement, states acceptance criteria and test evidence, and records its Graphite stack position when applicable. On merge, the Linear story records the merged pull request and moves only when its acceptance criteria are verified. --- ## Delivery roadmap Linear is the execution system of record; this page is the requirements and design source. Each delivery epic and story links back here rather than duplicating its full specification. - Slice A — Sense and target: Find, Fix, Track, Target; contact-state projection, information quality, authority and ROE, sensor-to-shooter traceability, and a targetability scenario. - Slice B — Engage and assess: Target, Engage, Assess; event contract, missile/gun/laser rendering, explanation, contact combat card, replay, and accessibility. - Slice C — Command, learn, adapt: confidence-aware recommendations, after-action review, sensor/EW understanding, damage state, and formation coordination. - Cross-cutting readiness: performance and declutter budgets, usability scenarios, and kill-chain traceability. - Slice G - Unity UX/UI rebaseline and acceptance: Slice G - Unity UX/UI Rebaseline and Acceptance extends acceptance across C2 and Mission/Platform Editor surfaces, reusing existing A-C and cross-cutting stories. [DRG-233](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-233) owns delivery; this addition does not close any existing acceptance gate. --- Delivery status (Linear 2026-09-04): Headless Combat UX stories DRG-206–230 are Done on main @ 6f80d226 (#610 docs W1-HUB). Wave 5 leftovers (#600–#603) remain on main. This page stays the requirements SoT. Update 2026-09-30: UI stories proceed under the authorized S122.0–S127 evidence rebaseline. DRG-180/181/182 are Done in live Linear; DRG-183/169/258/197 are In Progress. Owner Play Mode [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208) remains Todo and human-only at Linear-reported integration1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd. It is an acceptance gate for the program. The current roadmap and mandatory QA plan separate delivery status, retained technical evidence and owner acceptance. Proposed VER-07.3–6 strengthens revision provenance under DRG-201/244. Do not treat this page as a second board. ## Slice framing ### Slice A — Sense and target Find → Fix → Track → Target. A player can trace a contact from detection to targetability, including provenance, confidence, freshness, comms state, classification, authority, and rules-of-engagement constraints. ### Slice B — Engage and assess Target → Engage → Assess. The existing vertical slice proves a missile, gun, and laser engagement from command through outcome, explanation, accessible symbology, replay, and assessment. ### Slice C — Command, learn, and adapt Observe → Orient → Decide → Act. The player reviews outcomes, receives clearly non-authoritative recommendations, commands formations within delegated authority, and updates intent using battle-damage assessment. ## Cross-cutting requirement lenses - Command and control: make authority to observe, recommend, approve, engage, abort, and delegate explicit. - Sensor-to-shooter: preserve traceability from detection through firing solution to engagement and assessment. - Rules of engagement and escalation: explain permitted, withheld, and approval-required actions. - Information quality: distinguish confidence, provenance, freshness, comms loss, and genuine unknowns. - Mission command and BDA: express intent and constraints, then support retasking, withdrawal, or re-attack from assessed results. --- Status: Accepted for headless delivery; UI/render in progress under S122–S127, owner acceptance via [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208).
Purpose: Requirements and slice framing. Linear holds story status.
Scope: Cross-domain C2 presentation only. The simulation remains the source of combat facts; the UI renders projections and submits commands through the approved boundary. --- ## Recommended requirement set ### CMB-UI-01 — Combat event grammar \\\[P0\\\] Every player-visible engagement shall have a consistent lifecycle: intent accepted, authorization or refusal, weapon launch or firing, in-flight or sustained effect where applicable, terminal outcome, and replay correlation. The event payload shall identify shooter, target, weapon family, outcome, and explanation reference. ### CMB-UI-02 — Weapon-family symbology \\\[P0\\\] The tactical map shall distinguish missile, gun, and laser engagements without depending on color alone. Each family shall have distinct iconography, line behavior, motion treatment, and accessible text or tooltip labels. The same semantics shall appear in the event log and replay. ### CMB-UI-03 — Engagement explanation \\\[P0\\\] For a selected engagement or blocked order, the player shall be able to see firing solution state, hard constraints, doctrine or policy constraints, sensor/contact confidence, selected weapon, and the actionable reason for refusal. ### CMB-UI-04 — Contact combat card \\\[P0\\\] A selected contact shall have a presentation distinct from an own-unit panel. It shall show identity confidence, detection provenance and freshness, posture, targetability, associated engagement status, and battle-damage assessment when known. ### CMB-UI-05 — Scale-aware declutter and accessibility \\\[P0\\\] At operational scale, salvos and gun bursts shall aggregate while selected or replay-inspected engagements remain explorable. Weapon family, affiliation, clearance, and outcome shall use redundant channels: shape, line style, label, and color. --- ## Vertical slice One deterministic scenario shall show one shooter and one target for each family: missile, gun, and laser. It shall prove command acceptance, permitted and refused engagement states, event ordering, map symbology, impact or miss, event-log correlation, replay determinism, and usable presentation at tactical and operational zoom. --- ## Story sequence 1. Combat event projection contract — headless projection with replay correlation; blocks all UI stories. 2. Missile, gun, and laser renderer — consumes only the event projection; validates the visual vocabulary. 3. Engagement explain surface — connects selected event to constraints and doctrine reasoning. 4. Contact combat card — provides provenance, confidence, targeting state, and BDA. 5. Declutter and accessibility pass — validates three zoom bands and non-color-only recognition. 6. Replay acceptance harness — asserts event-to-render outcomes across the vertical slice. --- ## Acceptance gates - A user can identify shooter, target, weapon family, and outcome without opening a detail panel. - A blocked shot states the reason and the next corrective action when one exists. - Replay emits the same combat event sequence and yields the same presentation state. - Weapon family and outcome remain distinguishable in a non-color-only mode. - No presentation code derives combat truth independently from the simulation projection. --- ## Dependencies and boundaries - Reuse existing sensor and weapon envelope overlays; do not rebuild them. - Keep the simulation and C2 command contracts headless-first. - Do not start implementation until this draft is accepted and placed in a newly authorized delivery scope. --- ## References - [Combat domains and damage](https://app.notion.com/p/3a7f7cb4e4df816995d5d02e5d5bd9ec) - [C2 UI requirements delta](https://app.notion.com/p/3aaf7cb4e4df816992cff848b5532378) - [Unity UI maturity plan](https://app.notion.com/p/3abf7cb4e4df812f8128c528ce3f3f7b) - [Command UI reference](https://command.matrixgames.com/?page_id=2697) Any Sensor, Best Shooter — Derived Requirements IBCS-Informed Combat C2 Framework — Derived Requirements Agentic Combat Capabilities — Proposed Requirements QA Gauntlet Architecture — Requirements and Delivery Sequence

notion.title: Core Simulation Design
notion.note: [Core Simulation Design] — Status: Draft — source reconciliation authored; owner review pending. — Matched: - CS-07: collect criterion-level SHA/build/local delta/scenario/catalog/policy/test-layer/result evidence and an explicit owner decision und --- Status: Draft — source reconciliation authored; owner review pending. Owner: drg amtd Related Linear Milestone: M3 / Core — S122–S127 evidence rebaseline. Last updated: 2026-09-30. Design review task: [DRG-343](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-343). Evidence identity: The 2026-09-30 refresh cited a local checkout at C:\Users\dgorn\cmano-clone\cmano-clone, HEAD 4190fb1b49cd15775b6b995b7c245d73828cd7a2, with uncommitted changes. As of 2026-11-20 that SHA is not on origin (absent from a fetched clone and from GitHub), and uncommitted working-tree changes cannot be pinned. Published main SHAs: last main tip at the time of the refresh, [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, 2:40 PM CDT, #681), which this page already named as a separate target; current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b) (2026-11-17, 7:16 PM CT). Blob links that previously used 4190fb1b now point at the same paths on [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd). Refreshed against main 1902dc12 because 4190fb1b was never pushed (ruling: Decision, 2026-11-20). Planning completion does not grant product acceptance. --- ## Overview The headless simulation supplies authoritative execution; the player prepares the scenario, begins execution, delegates orders, and inspects outcomes. This page describes the implemented session/tick contract and distinguishes it from proposed session restoration. UI reads projections and submits intent through approved command seams; it does not own the simulation clock or world state. The main orchestration source is [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs); delegation is [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs). GitNexus path-qualified context calls against this exact checkout corroborated both classes, plus ReplayCheckpointStore and the delegation SeededRng. Same-name sibling indexes are not interchangeable; graph results corroborate source navigation, not runtime proof. ## Player Fantasy Command a theater at the pace needed to understand events: plan before execution, pause to inspect attention and constraints, accelerate quiet periods, then see why delegated or human orders executed or were withheld. Outcomes remain reproducible for a fixed build and input sequence. Pause freezes the interactive simulation clock; it must not be presented as a guarantee that all orchestration queues and logs stop changing. ## Detailed Rules 1. Planning versus execution. SimulationSession.Tick and TickHeadless return false in Planning before running the session. BeginExecution changes the orchestrator phase; its initial Planning-to-Executing transition appends a mode-change record. The session does not infer readiness from elapsed calendar time. 2. Outer delegation call. RunExecutingTick calls Orchestrator.Tick once with the supplied ObservedState. The orchestrator drains approved orders, evaluates active agents, and drains agent/human issued queues into ExecutedOrders. It derives its order tick from the observed SimTime; this is distinct from the pipeline clock. 3. Interactive pause. The pause check occurs after the orchestrator call. A paused executing session may therefore drain queues or emit decision/denial records while its simulation clock does not advance. Tick returns true for the executing call even when paused; that return value alone does not prove a new simulation tick. 4. Engagement and cadence. An unpaused call selects Engage orders, applies communications and salvo/deconfliction gates, enqueues requests, and calls Sim.TickOnce in RealTime mode. It logs the initial results and applies damage handling, then performs acceleration-factor-minus-one extra pipeline steps. Delegation, result logging/damage handling, and the final logistics FSM call are not repeated for every extra step by this method. Do not describe acceleration as a whole-session tick repeated uniformly. 5. Headless execution. TickHeadless selects HeadlessBatch, bypassing the pipeline pause gate while retaining the pause flag. In Planning it still returns false. Watch attention can require acknowledgement or explicit override through TryResumeSim; legacy ResumeSim bypasses that watch gate. 6. Verification checkpoints. [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs) appends strictly increasing checkpoint ticks and finds the latest at/before a requested tick. [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpoint.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpoint.cs) contains SimTick, WorldHash, LogFingerprint, and LastSequenceId. These are verification metadata, not a serialized restorable session. ## Formulas - Clock time is SimClock.SimTime = SimTick * FixedDeltaSeconds; default delta is 1/60 second. Acceleration changes the number of fixed steps, not the delta. See [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Time/SimClock.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Time/SimClock.cs). - For an executing, unpaused session call with factor F, the pipeline advances 1 + max(0, F - 1) steps. F is clamped to 1–256. The session owns this outer acceleration loop; direct pipeline Accelerated mode separately uses F steps. See [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SimTickPipeline.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SimTickPipeline.cs). - Delegation [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/SeededRng.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/SeededRng.cs) initializes state from global seed XOR salted agent identity, substitutes 1 for zero, applies xorshift updates (13, 7, 17), then returns (state & 0xFFFFFF) / 0x1000000. Reproducibility requires the same seed, salt, and draw order. - The separate [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SeededRng.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SeededRng.cs) uses seed/domain/entity/tick/draw-index hashing. Its masked uint division can include the endpoint 1.0; the two RNG contracts must not be conflated. ## Edge Cases - Calling Tick during Planning is rejected even when headless execution was requested. - Paused execution is not queue immutability; distinguish observed order time, orchestration effects, and pipeline tick progression in diagnostics. - Repeating a checkpoint tick or recording an earlier tick is ignored; an empty/before-first lookup returns no checkpoint. - A hash checkpoint cannot reconstruct pending events, RNG state, engagements, resources, or authority-bearing mission state. - Proposed RPL-29–31 require same-build/scenario/catalog/policy uninterrupted-versus-restored equality and non-mutating corrupt/incompatible-load failure. These contracts, [DRG-348](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-348) and [DRG-349](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-349), are gated backlog work; save/resume and multiplayer are not established by replay goldens. ## Dependencies The [cmano-clone project](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9) links requirements 03/08/17, ADR-001 simulation boundary, ADR-003 order log, ADR-004 tick pipeline, and presentation ADR-010 sections 2–3 plus ADR-007. DelegationBridge remains zero-touch. Scenario policy, catalog, seed and ordered input identities are required context for deterministic comparisons. S122–S127 delivery follows evidence gates; [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208) remains owner Play Mode acceptance. ## Tuning Knobs Fixed delta and clock factor are existing implementation settings; factor bounds 1–256 are code constraints, not newly accepted product performance targets. Scenario-policy values govern gameplay tuning. Checkpoint frequency is chosen by the harness/caller, not persisted as a save/resume contract. Any cadence or performance change needs profiling, criterion-specific evidence and current upstream impact analysis before symbol edits; no parameter changes are authorized by this page. ## Acceptance Criteria These are review/verification criteria, not fresh execution results or owner signoff. - CS-01: verify Planning calls do not advance the pipeline; BeginExecution exposes the documented phase/log transition. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionPhaseTests. - CS-02: verify paused interactive clock remains unchanged while separately inspecting approved/human queue and log behavior; do not accept only the Tick boolean. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionClockControlsTests; queue/log coverage must be checked explicitly. - CS-03: compare factors 1 and greater than 1 against the documented outer/inner cadence; confirm fixed delta does not stretch. Existing clock tests are candidate mappings, not proof of uniform subsystem acceleration. - CS-04: verify headless pause override and watch acknowledgement/override behavior. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionWatchAttentionTests. - CS-05: repeat identical build/input/seed runs and compare state/order fingerprints; retain Baltic v2 hash 17144800277401907079. Use [AGENTS.md](http://AGENTS.md) standing gates and the six canonical replay cases; recorded counts must identify revision and local delta. - CS-06: review checkpoint metadata honesty and keep RPL-29–31 proposed until schema/feasibility/ADR and differential restore tests exist. - CS-07: collect criterion-level SHA/build/local delta/scenario/catalog/policy/test-layer/result evidence and an explicit owner decision under proposed VER-07.3–6. This draft and source inspection satisfy neither Editor coverage nor owner acceptance.

linear.title: Introduce typed mission-thread evidence and a unified evidence ledger
linear.description:
## Goal

Replace fragile, substring-oriented proof as the primary integration mechanism with versioned, typed mission-thread evidence correlated to replay, requirements, and CI results.

## Acceptance criteria

* Defines schema/versioning for relevant contact, authority, data-link, recommendation, engagement, and assessment facts.
* Correlates a scenario run with replay, oracle outcome, Buildkite evidence, and defect follow-up.
* Retains existing fingerprint checks during migration; no silent loss of fail-closed coverage.
* Keeps simulation facts authoritative and observable without duplicating tactical logic.

## Dependency

Requires the capability manifest.

## Revision-bound evidence extension — 2026-09-30

Owner: drg amtd. Requirement VER-07.3–6 (proposed). Every evidence row records requirement/AC ID, inspected and executed revision (and dirty-tree identity), scenario/seed/policy/catalog identity, command or harness, timestamp, artifact link, result and evidence kind (static inspection/headless/Editor capture/human acceptance). Keep declared floor separate from observed counts; historical results cannot satisfy a different revision. Missing, skipped or blocked evidence remains explicit. Owner signoff is a separate row with person/date/revision; technical success never infers acceptance.

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

* **Links:** parent epic [DRG-198](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-198>); blocks [DRG-202](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-202>). The 'capability manifest' dependency has no Linear issue.
* **Decision needed (CMANO):** the capability manifest it depends on is unticketed, and the evidence schema/version format is a design decision.

Missing/changed document, explicitdbRef failure and blocking validation preserve prior session/no tick. linear.title: [H5] Draft content-pipeline / Addressables ADR
linear.description:
## Context

The H5 entry gate is "Content pipeline ADR accepted". No such ADR exists (`docs/architecture/` holds ADR-001…026; ADR-027 is in open PR <pull-request id="540d1213-7de1-4ff7-a462-c2a405c9d241" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#679" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/docsunity-record-unity-mcp-stack-choice-adr-027-and-fix-0860-version-176dd2257933" />).

Addressables use today is a single atlas key, `Map/App6FrameAtlas`:

* `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Addressables/Map/App6AtlasAddressablesManifest.json`
* `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Editor/App6AddressablesGroupSetup.cs`
* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/App6AddressablesCatalog.cs`
* Consumed by `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` with a Unicode fallback (S27-07)

The package is `com.unity.addressables` 2.9.1. The roadmap (`docs/reports/future-sprint-roadmap-07142026.md`) lists "Addressables / remote content design undesigned".

## Scope of the ADR

Write a new ADR under `docs/architecture/` using the next free number.

1. **Content classes** in and out of Addressables:
   * Presentation art/USS/audio (`production/assets/*`, `design/assets/asset-manifest.md`)
   * APP-6 atlases
   * Globe/basemap tiles
   * Scenario packages (`AegisScenarioPackage`)
   * Catalog snapshots (`src/ProjectAegis.Data/Snapshots/`)

   Core sim DLLs are **out** (`.claude/agents/unity-addressables-specialist.md`).
2. **Presentation wall** (ADR-010 / 007 / 001): Addressables APIs only in Unity presentation assemblies. `ProjectAegis.Sim`, `ProjectAegis.Data` and `ProjectAegis.Delegation` keep headless resolvers like `App6AddressablesCatalog` and never reference `UnityEngine.AddressableAssets`.
3. **Determinism**: sim-relevant data (catalog, scenario policy) must reach the sim through existing Data loaders and hashes (`CatalogSnapshotHasher`, `UnifiedReleaseTrainManifest`), not through Addressables. State how the Baltic hash `17144800277401907079` stays preserved. **No silent ReplayGolden re-bless.**
4. **CatalogWriteGate**: Addressables never becomes a write path into the catalog.
5. **Host impact**: bulk loading must go through a new loader seam, not by growing `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` or `GlobeMapProductHost`. If it cannot, name the waiver.
6. **Local vs remote**: local-only for Release, or remote/CDN (Launch-adjacent, and H3 is not open).
7. Build and CI: headless CI cannot build Addressables content, so say what is verified headless and what needs a local Editor.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR file merged with Status Proposed, then Accepted by the owner (this closes the H5 gate)
- [ ] Content-class table with owner and loader for each class
- [ ] Hard-no impact stated per host, gate and golden
- [ ] First slice named, with a non-`TBD` Surface

Surface: `docs/architecture/adr-0NN-content-pipeline-addressables.md` (docs-only)

## Start condition

**Nothing is started until the owner gives GO for H5.** This issue stays in Backlog and no agent is dispatched.

2026-09-30 planning direction authorized by user: local presentation-only pilot first (<issue id="d37c71b0-abcf-43e4-844f-8f7b545a0ffd" label="DRG-347" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-347/h5-pilot-local-presentation-content-loading-with-deterministic-failure" />), with loading failure isolation and authoritative replay invariants. Inventory <issue id="e3383353-b551-45de-807d-60a52efe11ad" label="DRG-332" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-332/h5-content-inventory-classify-addressables-candidates-vs-sim-relevant" /> gates this ADR. Package/version and lifetime decision remain Proposed until reviewed; remote delivery/DLC/catalog behavior is excluded.

linear.description:
## Context

The H5 ADR needs a factual inventory of what content exists and which of it may affect the deterministic sim. Candidate sources on `main`:

* `design/assets/asset-manifest.md`: 42 assets (15 Done, 4 Approved, 20 Specced, 3 In Production)
* `production/assets/{c2,ui,audio,baltic,store}/`: USS and art stubs
* `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Addressables/Map/App6AtlasAddressablesManifest.json`: the only live Addressables entry
* `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Resources/` (fonts): legacy Resources usage
* Scenario data: `assets/data/scenarios/`, `data/scenarios/`, `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/AegisScenarioPackage.cs`
* Catalog: `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Snapshots/` (`DbSnapshotStore`, `CatalogSnapshotHasher`, `UnifiedReleaseTrainManifest`)

Known doc drift: `.claude/agents/unity-addressables-specialist.md` says Addressables **2.3.16**, but `unity/ProjectAegis/Packages/manifest.json` pins **2.9.1**.

## Task (read-only)

1. Build a table covering each content class: path, approximate size or count, presentation-only vs sim-relevant, current loader, and whether it is a candidate for Addressables.
2. Mark anything that feeds `SimWorldHash` or a replay golden as **not Addressables** unless the ADR says otherwise.
3. List the Unity hosts that load each class today, and flag `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` / `GlobeMapProductHost`.
4. Note the 2.3.16 vs 2.9.1 drift for correction in the ADR PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inventory brief under `production/agentic/` linked from the H5 ADR story
- [ ] Every row cites a repo path
